item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
High-Level Meeting at Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi reviews preparations for Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0
KTS 5.0 to be held from Nov 28 to Dec 12, 2026 on the theme ‘Thirukkural Payilvom-Thirukkural Abhyas Karen’
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level meeting to review the preparatory arrangements and inter-agency coordination for Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 (KTS 5.0) was held at the Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, on Nov 3, 2026. Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Smt. Deepti Gaur Mukerjee chaired the Meeting.

Vice-Chancellor, BHU, Prof. Ajit Kumar Chaturvedi; Additional Chief Secretary (Higher Education), Uttar Pradesh Government, Shri Amit Kumar Ghosh; senior officials from the Union Ministry of Education, the State Government, the district administration, BHU and the Indian Railways, attended the Meeting, along with other key stakeholders.

During the Meeting, discussions were held on inter-departmental and district-level administrative coordination; dedicated rail transport arrangements by IRCTC and other logistics; infrastructural facilities; exhibitions; excursions; cultural programmes to be organised as part of KTS 5.0, etc. Senior officials of the Ministry also visited onsite and offsite venues including Namo Ghat to assess operational readiness.

The fifth edition of KTS is scheduled to be held from November 28 to December 12, 2026 on the theme ‘Thirukkural Payilvom- Thirukkural Abhyas Karen’. KTS 5.0 seeks to bring the timeless ethical and moral wisdom of the classical Tamil text Thirukkural closer to the youth and learners across the country.

As part of the Programme, around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, organized into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake an eight-day journey comprising four days of travel and four days of visits and structured programmes. The itinerary will include visits to Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, featuring cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements. 50 teachers from Tamil Nadu will also visit Uttar Pradesh and teach Thirukkural in schools and colleges during KTS 5.0.

The web portal and the delegate registration process for KTS 5.0 were inaugurated by Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi on 22 October 2026.

A nationwide Students’ Engagement Programme will also be undertaken through 1,000 Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) across the country to promote wider understanding of the Thirukkural among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. The Initiative will include structured study, research and campus-based activities for wider dissemination of the teachings and values of the Thirukkural. The details are available at www.kts.cict.in.

The Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Chennai, is spearheading digital outreach, publications, and institutional engagements, while IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University are serving as the nodal coordinating institutions for Tamil Nadu and Kashi, respectively.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar Launches ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’ to Strengthen Intergenerational Bonding Campaign to Promote Sustained Intergenerational Engagement Through the ‘5C’ Model of Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue Union Minister Administers Vayo Samman Pledge; Handbook Released and Vayo SAATHI Volunteer Initiative Launched Two MoUs Signed And Exchanged With Shri Ram Chandra Mission And Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra In Presence Of Hon’ble Minister, Senior Officials “This Deepavali, Let No Elder Be Left Alone”-Dr…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar Launches ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’ to Strengthen Intergenerational Bonding
Campaign to Promote Sustained Intergenerational Engagement Through the ‘5C’ Model of Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue
Union Minister Administers Vayo Samman Pledge; Handbook Released and Vayo SAATHI Volunteer Initiative Launched
Two MoUs Signed And Exchanged With Shri Ram Chandra Mission And Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra In Presence Of Hon’ble Minister, Senior Officials
“This Deepavali, Let No Elder Be Left Alone”-Dr Virendra Kumar
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar today launched the ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), in the National Capital here this evening.

The initiative marks an important step towards strengthening intergenerational solidarity and promoting a society that recognises and values the experience, wisdom and contributions of senior citizens.

The Minister also released the Handbook on Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan and launched the Vayo SAATHI volunteer initiative to mobilise citizens in support of senior citizens.

On the occasion, two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Voluntary organizations namely Shri Ram Chandra Mission (SRCM) and Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra (AVSK), Jodhpur, were signed and formally exchanged in the presence of the Hon’ble Union Minister, Secretary MoSJE and other senior officials of the Ministry.

These collaborations aim to promote the holistic well-being of senior citizens through meditation, yoga and wellness programmes, besides encouraging intergenerational engagement through pledge drives, walkathons and other community-based activities.

Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Additional Secretaries Smt Mona K Khandhar, Smt Debolina Thakur, Joint Secretaries Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Shri Shailendra Kumar, Smt Monali P Dhakate, Shri Rahees M, Economic Advisor, Directors, Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Ms Kajal Singh and other senior officials of the Ministry were present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar described the Abhiyan as an ‘Anubhav aur Urja ka Sangam’, bringing together the experience of senior citizens and the energy of younger generations.

 

He highlighted that India's population aged 60 years and above is projected to increase from approximately 10 crore in 2011 to 23 crore by 2036.

 

The Minister observed that urbanisation, migration and changing family structures have reduced regular interaction between generations, resulting in challenges such as loneliness, limited awareness of welfare schemes and vulnerability to cyber fraud among senior citizens.

Emphasising the importance of mutual learning and intergenerational relationships, the Minister stated, “The youth will connect our elders to the digital world and our elders will give the youth the values of life.”

Giving a special message on the eve of Deepawali, he urged citizens to ensure that no elderly person in their homes or neighbourhoods is left alone and that one diya is lit in their honour.

The Minister highlighted that the Abhiyan would reach every village and mohalla through Panchayats, local bodies and educational institutions. He emphasised that even simple acts of care, such as spending half an hour with an elderly person or accompanying them to a doctor, represent meaningful contributions towards their well-being.

Dr Kumar said the Abhiyan reinforces the message that the welfare, dignity and inclusion of senior citizens are not merely governmental responsibilities but a shared social commitment.

During the programme, the Hon’ble Union Minister administered the Vayo Samman Pledge to all those present, encouraging collective commitment towards ensuring the dignity, care, respect and social inclusion of senior citizens.

Welcoming the gathering, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, stated that the initiative recognises senior citizens not merely as beneficiaries of welfare programmes but as active contributors, mentors and valuable repositories of knowledge, culture and social experience. He encouraged States and Districts to undertake activities in accordance with the Handbook to ensure effective implementation of the Abhiyan.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Abhiyan is based on the ‘5C’ model – Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue – which seeks to establish sustained engagement between generations.

He said Abhiyaan promotes connecting younger and older generations through community platforms and educational institutions, encouraging conversations and storytelling, undertaking joint activities, sharing knowledge and skills for community welfare, and continuing such engagement as a regular community-led practice rather than a one-time activity.

The Official said the Campaign encompasses twelve thematic areas, including ‘30 Minutes Together’, ‘Teach Me – I'll Teach You’, ‘My Story, My India’, ‘Digital Dada-Dadi / Digital Saathi’, ‘Generation Health & Wellness’ and ‘Silver Skills – Seniors as Mentors’.

These themes aim to promote companionship, preserve oral histories, enhance digital literacy, create awareness about cyber fraud, encourage health and wellness, and recognise senior citizens as mentors and knowledge contributors, he said.

Another major component of the initiative is Vayo SAATHI (Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion), a digitally enabled volunteer initiative open to all citizens aged 18 years and above, including students, young professionals and institutions, he said.

Volunteers will act as friends, facilitators and connectors for senior citizens, supporting their social inclusion and well-being adding that interested citizens can register through the SCW SAMAVESH Portal or JEEVAN App and receive a Vayo SAATHI Certificate, the Official further said.

The Official informed the Handbook released during the programme provides a comprehensive guiding framework covering the objectives, implementation strategy, thematic activities and roles of States, Districts and community institutions in carrying forward the Abhiyan.

The MoUs signed with Shri Ram Chandra Mission and Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Jodhpur, will further strengthen efforts towards the holistic well-being of senior citizens through meditation, yoga, wellness programmes and intergenerational engagement activities, he added.

Through Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, the Ministry seeks to build a stronger culture of respect, care, companionship and solidarity across generations. The Department invites citizens, educational institutions, universities, youth organisations, NGOs, Resident Welfare Associations and CSR partners to participate in the initiative and register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Armed Forces Medical Services treats over 4,000 patients and performs 365 sight-restoring surgeries at Rairangpur Mega Multi-Speciality Medical Camp
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) successfully conducted the 12th edition of Operation DRISHTI, a Mega Multi-Speciality Medical Camp at Rairangpur, Mayurbhanj, Odisha, treating over 4,000 patients and performing 365 sight-restoring eye surgeries between November 02-04, 2026. The camp provided comprehensive specialist medical care free of cost, bringing advanced healthcare services closer to the people of the region.

On November 04, 2026, Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja, Director General Armed Forces Medical Services (DGAFMS), visited the camp and interacted with patients undergoing consultation and post-operative care. He also presented medicine kits to patients who had undergone eye surgeries. He appreciated the dedication and commitment of the medical teams, who continued their services despite challenging weather conditions posed by a cyclone, ensuring uninterrupted medical care to the people.

The camp brought together specialists from Ophthalmology, Cardiology, Nephrology, Dermatology, Dental and General Medicine under one roof. Every patient reporting at the camp was provided on-site medical attention. The initiative enabled patients to undergo screening, investigations and treatment, with referrals for advanced care wherever required.

The Cardiology Department attended to over 400 patients, conducted 298 ECGs and 406 echocardiograms, and identified 29 patients requiring advanced interventions, including angiography, CT angiography, valve surgery, device implantation and balloon pulmonary valvotomy. Nephrology treated over 400 patients and conducted 341 ultrasound examinations, while Dermatology attended to over 500 patients. The Dental team treated 221 patients and performed 198 procedures, and General Medicine attended to 339 patients.

The beneficiaries include 75-year-old Biswanath, who had been living with a complicated cataract following an old eye injury. The surgical team successfully performed manual small-incision cataract surgery with a scleral-fixated intraocular lens, restoring the possibility of improved vision. Another beneficiary was 60-year-old Sombari Gope, who had a dense cataract in a structurally small eye. The surgeons successfully performed manual small-incision cataract surgery with a posterior chamber lens, ensuring protection of the cornea.

The camp, conducted at the place where the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu belongs to, marks another significant milestone in Operation DRISHTI, the AFMS initiative to extend specialised eye care and advanced medical services to underserved regions across the country. The successful conduct of the camp reflects the Armed Forces Medical Services' unwavering commitment to humanitarian service and its resolve to make quality healthcare accessible to all, bringing specialised treatment and the gift of sight to the doorstep of the people of Mayurbhanj.

******

SR/Ruchi

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain business of Deutsche Bank Aktiengesellschaft by Kotak Mahindra Bank, and other related transactions
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of certain business of Deutsche Bank Aktiengesellschaft by Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited, and other related transactions.

The Proposed Combination envisages acquisition of Retail Banking/ Private Banking and Wealth Management business of Deutsche Bank Aktiengesellschaft (Seller) undertaken through its branches in India (Target Business), as a going concern on a slump sale basis by Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited (Acquirer) from the Seller [the Acquirer and the Seller are collectively referred to as ‘Parties’].

Further, the Parties, through their affiliates, are contemplating to enter into referral arrangements for referral of customers of investment advisory business and portfolio management services business of Deutsche Investments India Private Limited, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Seller, to relevant wholly owned subsidiaries of the Acquirer.

The Acquirer is a scheduled commercial bank licensed by the Reserve Bank of India to carry on banking business, with its equity share capital listed on Bombay Stock Exchange and National Stock Exchange of India. The Acquirer is engaged in retail banking, wealth management and institutional banking, including provision of (a) deposit accounts, (b) loans, (c) distribution/ referral of third-party investment and insurance products, (d) portfolio management and investment advisory, along with other allied/ ancillary services, in India.

The Target Business consists of Deutsche Bank’s Retail banking/ Private Banking and Wealth Management business in India. Within the Retail banking/ Private banking segment, it provides a wide range of products across deposits, lending, investments, insurance, and foreign exchange. The wealth management business focuses on providing services to high-net-worth individuals.

*****

KT/ONP

The campaign aimed at clearing pendency and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Conclusion of Special Campaign 6 of Department of Food and Public Distribution
Shri Pralhad Joshi Reviews Preparations for Special Campaign 6, Directs Effective Implementation
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), along with its PSUs and subordinate/attached offices, undertook initiatives to implement Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026. The campaign aimed at clearing pendency and promoting Swachhata (cleanliness) in its office premises.

The campaign was conducted in two phases i.e. the Preparatory Phase (15th September to 30th September, 2026) and the Implementation Phase (2nd October to 31st October, 2026). During the Preparatory Phase, various pending matters such as references from Members of Parliament, references from State Governments, public grievances, physical files identified for weeding, scrap disposal/e-waste, and sites requiring cleaning and beautification were identified.

During the period, Hon’ble Minister (Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution), Shri Pralhad Joshi, convened a review meeting with senior officers and provided necessary directions for the effective implementation of Special Campaign 6.

During the campaign period, the achievements under various parameters were regularly updated on the Special Campaign 6 portal. Further, Department of Food and Public Distribution in response to directive issued by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), also undertook a deep cleaning  drive as a  part of one day cleanliness activity on 29.10.2026 at Krishi Bhawan under Special Campaign 6, promoting workplace hygiene, cleanliness and better upkeep of office premises.

Further, one day activity was also undertaken on 29.10.2026 by all offices under DFPD i.e. Food Corporation of India (FCI), Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC), Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA), National Sugar Institute (NSI, Kanpur), Indian Grain Management and Research Institutes (IGMRIs), Quality Control Cells (QCCs), Central Grain Analysis Laboratory (CGAL) and Directorate of Sugar and Vegetable Oil (DSVO). 

During the Implementation Phase, concerted efforts were made by DFPD to clear all identified pendencies. The Department successfully resolved all pending matters within the stipulated timeframe, including State Government References – 03, MP References – 54, Public Grievances – 937, and Public Grievance Appeals – 1479 along with 36824 physical files weeded, 8026 e-files closed,. Additionally, 2977 cleanliness campaigns were conducted, 60788 sq. ft. of office space freed and revenue of ₹4168772/- generated from the disposal of e-waste/obsolete materials.

Tweets, PIB releases etc. were also regularly issued/uploaded to highlight progress and achievements.

***

IA/RP

(Release ID: 2332719)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Captivates Visitors with Vibrant Cultural Performances and Traditional Craftsmanship at Dilli Haat
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, currently underway at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, continues to draw enthusiastic crowds with its spectacular display of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship, and vibrant cultural diversity.

Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the 15-day Mela has transformed into a bustling hub of inclusive celebration and will remain open to visitors until November 15, 2026.

Centred around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the Mela highlights India’s rich heritage of traditional crafts and festive lighting. The fair has been curated across seven distinct thematic zones to offer visitors a multi-sensory cultural experience.

These include कला आँगन featuring live craft demonstrations by skilled artisans, प्रकाश चौक displaying an exquisite collection of lamps and festive lights, पूजा पथ presenting a wide range of devotional products, सजावट बाज़ार focusing on unique and traditional home décor items, घराना featuring a stunning array of traditional textiles and fashion, स्वाद चौक offering diverse culinary delights from different regions, and मंच serving as the vibrant centre for cultural activities and evening performances.

The Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing handicrafts, handloom products, and creative works by artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis, and persons with disabilities. To strengthen economic opportunities and market reach for these artisans, key empowerment components have been integrated into the event.

The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through 15 such fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.

This includes Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans directly with wider markets through e-commerce platforms, providing them with greater visibility, consumer access, and sustainable economic growth, alongside Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity, capabilities, and active contributions of persons with disabilities while promoting equal opportunities and social inclusion.

A major attraction captivating visitors every evening is the series of cultural activities and programmes hosted at the Manch. Artists and troupe performers from different States come together to present colourful folk dances, traditional music, and regional art forms.

These evening programmes offer audiences a mesmerizing window into India's pluralistic cultural expressions on a single platform, creating a festive atmosphere and fostering regional cultural exchange.

Participating beneficiaries are supported by the Ministry's apex corporations, including the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC).

Artisans are provided with free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances, and transportation facilities for their goods.

Through the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, the Ministry continues its efforts to strengthen livelihood opportunities, encourage entrepreneurship, and foster inclusive economic growth while preserving India’s rich cultural heritage. The Ministry invites citizens, families, and art enthusiasts to visit Dilli Haat, explore traditional crafts, support artisan communities, and experience the nation's diverse cultural traditions.

**********

PR-213-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.title: Supply chain diversification & greater regional cooperation are key to stronger maritime inter-dependence amid strained security environment: Raksha Mantri at Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Defence
item.description: Ministry of Defence Supply chain diversification & greater regional cooperation are key to stronger maritime inter-dependence amid strained security environment: Raksha Mantri at Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 “Certain actors & nations seek to exploit the criticality of oceans for narrow unilateral gains; Answer to interconnected world’s vulnerabilities lies in building resilience” Maritime security must evolve with emerging threats; Leveraging emerging technologies is the need of the hour, says Shri Rajnath Singh “Technology must not become another source of inequality among nations;…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Supply chain diversification & greater regional cooperation are key to stronger maritime inter-dependence amid strained security environment: Raksha Mantri at Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026
“Certain actors & nations seek to exploit the criticality of oceans for narrow unilateral gains; Answer to interconnected world’s vulnerabilities lies in building resilience”
Maritime security must evolve with emerging threats; Leveraging emerging technologies is the need of the hour, says Shri Rajnath Singh
“Technology must not become another source of inequality among nations; Benefits to a few won’t achieve collective resilience”
“Economic development & environmental responsibility must progress together; Oceans cannot be treated as unlimited source of resources”
“Maritime sector to be a key driver of India’s Viksit Bharat journey; Govt striving to develop a comprehensive maritime ecosystem”
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

            Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for making inter-dependence among regional partners more secure and resilient through diversification of supply chains, reliable maritime infrastructure, enhanced maritime awareness and greater cooperation, along with the ability to anticipate, withstand and recover from disruptions, amid growing strains in the global maritime security environment. He was delivering the commemorative address at the Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue (IPRD), the Indian Navy’s annual apex-level international strategic conference, being held in New Delhi on November 4, 2026.

Describing oceans as bridges rather than barriers among nations & civilisations, Raksha Mantri highlighted their role in sustaining livelihoods and facilitating the exchange of goods, knowledge & culture. He stated that despite the international community's awareness of these universal dependencies, certain actors and nations seek to exploit the criticality of the oceans for narrow unilateral gains. “The global maritime security environment is strained by deliberate trade disruptions. We see blatant challenges to the freedom of navigation and the weaponisation of narrow maritime passages. This growing instability in the maritime domain casts a long shadow over the broader international order,” he added.

Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that the answer to the vulnerabilities of an interconnected world lies in building resilience, emphasising that globalisation cannot be abandoned in response to every disruption, nor should maritime spaces that have enabled human progress be closed. He stressed that the objective must be to make inter-dependence more secure.

Highlighting the evolving nature of maritime security, Raksha Mantri stated that challenges could arise not only from conventional military activities but also from non-traditional threats such as piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing, cyber-attacks and natural disasters. He underscored the need for maritime security to evolve with the changing maritime domain. “Artificial intelligence is changing the way data is processed, while autonomous systems are expanding the possibilities of surveillance & operations. New sensors are improving our ability to observe the oceans. Advances in materials, biotechnology and data analytics are opening new avenues for research and application. These developments have enormous implications for maritime security and economic activity. But technology, by itself, is not the answer. The more important question is how we use technology to address real challenges,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh also underlined that technology must not become another source of inequality among nations as the Indo-Pacific includes countries with different levels of technological and economic capability. “Some possess advanced research infrastructure. Others are still developing the institutional and human resources required to participate fully in this transformation. If technological progress benefits only a limited number of countries, we will not achieve the collective resilience that our region requires,” he said.

Raksha Mantri called for promoting cooperation in research, education, innovation and capacity building, stating that a stronger scientific capability in one country can contribute to the security & prosperity of the entire region. Terming it particularly important for smaller maritime nations and developing countries, he said the most useful technology is not necessarily the most expensive or sophisticated; it is the one that solves a real problem.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that as India moves towards Viksit Bharat by 2047, the maritime domain will play a crucial role in the country’s national transformation. He highlighted Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s efforts to develop a comprehensive maritime ecosystem through investments in port infrastructure and connectivity, port-led development under Sagarmala, promotion of coastal economic activities and strengthening of the maritime industrial base. He described the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 as the national blueprint for this transformation, with emphasis on technology, innovation, research, education and skills.

Raksha Mantri underlined the need for economic development and environmental responsibility to progress together, stating that oceans cannot be treated as an unlimited source of resources. He advocated the protection of marine ecosystems, responsible utilisation of ocean resources and placing the interests of coastal communities at the centre of development efforts. “National prosperity and ecological responsibility are not competing objectives. They must reinforce each other,” he said.

Reaffirming India's commitment to an open, inclusive and rule-based maritime order, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) that recognises the interconnected nature of security and prosperity among nations and underscores that the maritime future of the Indo-Pacific cannot be shaped by any single country acting alone. He also termed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, announced by PM Modi in 2019, as a practical framework for advancing maritime cooperation across seven interconnected areas.

Emphasising the need to translate regional cooperation into tangible outcomes, the Raksha Mantri urged the participants of IPRD to move beyond identifying challenges and focus on practical action. He pitched for stronger scientific networks, joint research, exchanges between universities and maritime institutions, and the development of affordable technological solutions to common challenges. Stressing that the deliberations at the IPRD must lead to concrete outcomes, he said ideas emerging from the dialogue must translate into partnerships, projects and measurable outcomes.

“The future of the Indo Pacific will not be shaped by technology alone. It will be shaped by the wisdom with which we use that technology, the partnerships we build and the confidence we create among nations,” Shri Rajnath Singh said, reiterating India's readiness to contribute to this collective endeavour.

Raksha Mantri expressed hope that the deliberations would lead to meaningful discussions and practical cooperation. He concluded with a call to move “from shared challenges to shared understanding. From shared understanding to shared knowledge. And from shared knowledge to shared resilience and shared prosperity.”

In his address, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) highlighted the interconnected nature of the oceans and the uneven distribution of scientific knowledge, research infrastructure and technological capabilities across the Indo-Pacific. He emphasised that maritime cooperation must extend beyond equipment acquisition to building sustainable capabilities, enabling partner nations to operate, maintain, adapt and upgrade technologies.

Underscoring the need for a broader and more integrated approach to maritime challenges, the CNS called for greater collective investment in ocean science and research, enhanced sharing of scientific data and technology, and collaborative research initiatives, including joint scientific expeditions. He also highlighted the importance of strengthening existing regional institutions and mechanisms through trust, transparency and inclusive ocean governance.

The CNS observed that IPRD-2026 provides an important platform for translating shared maritime interests into practical outcomes and generating concrete, forward-looking recommendations to strengthen science, technology and academic cooperation across the Indo-Pacific

Also among the dignitaries present were Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, former CNS and Chairman, NMF Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi (Retd).

The three-day IPRD 2026, being conducted by the Indian Navy in association with the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), commenced on November 3, 2026. The second day of the dialogue focused upon two closely connected issues of regional maritime resilience: a better shared understanding of activities at sea and a stronger scientific capacity to anticipate and respond to environmental change.

The day also witnessed a ministerial session featuring a special address by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences Dr Jitendra Singh. He also released an NMF publication titled ‘Alternative Hull Forms for the Future Indian Navy’.

Adding a Naval perspective to the overarching theme of IPRD 2026, an interactive session ‘Perspectives from the Flag Bridge’ brought together former Indian Navy chiefs Admiral RK Dhowan, Admiral Sunil Lanba, Admiral Karambir Singh and Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, and former Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy, Admiral Jayantha Perera, in a conversation hosted by Director General, NMF Vice Admiral Pradeep Chauhan. This session offered invaluable insights on the relationship between maritime strategy, technological change and regional cooperation, with a specific reference to naval cooperation under the aegis of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, which is currently being chaired by the Indian Navy.

In addition, a session, moderated by Commodore Abhinav Barve, Indian Navy, focused upon ‘Oceanographic Science and Climate Resilience’. In this session, the speakers deliberated upon the scientific foundations of regional preparedness with special emphasis on cooperative maritime networks for climate resilience in Indian Ocean Island States such as Mauritius and Seychelles.  The aspects of translation of ocean science into policy and collaborative sharing of ocean data, including cooperation involving research vessels, observation networks, forecasting capabilities and appropriate data-sharing arrangements, were also addressed during this session. 

The two ministerial sessions on the second day of IPRD 2026 lent strategic guidance to the conference and offered a holistic perspective on India’s collaborative approach in addressing maritime security concerns in the Indo-Pacific.

VK/VM/Savvy

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal inaugurates Vanijya Bhawan and Udyog Bhawan in Jaipur
Jaipur becomes the first city to house all departments and affiliated offices of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry at one location
Shri Goyal calls for co-location of offices of all 46 organisations under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry across the country
Co-location to create one-stop centres for promoting exports, investments and internal trade, and facilitating businesses
Shri Piyush Goyal reiterates commitment to citizen-centric governance, says serving citizens is the Government's foremost responsibility
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today virtually inaugurated Vanijya Bhawan and Udyog Bhawan in Jaipur, marking the beginning of the co-location of offices of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and its associated and affiliated organisations at a single location. Jaipur has become the first city and the first State capital to bring all these offices together under one roof.

Congratulating the Departments of Commerce and Departments for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) on the initiative, Shri Goyal said that the project should mark the beginning of rapid action towards implementing the concept across the country, particularly in every State capital. He said that these centres would serve as hubs to support industry and international trade and function as one-stop locations for activities relating to the promotion of exports, investments and internal trade. They would also support businesses and industry in their journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

Emphasising that the initiative must become a collective commitment of the entire ecosystem, Shri Goyal called for the active participation of government offices, stakeholders, State Government representatives, exporters, importers, investors and businesses. He stressed that the objective should go beyond administrative consolidation and extend to transforming service delivery, simplifying processes and making it easier to do business and comply with the laws of the land.

The Minister directed that all processes, including applications for licences and permits, SCOMET approvals and other services, should move entirely online. He set 31st March 2027 as the deadline for completing the necessary digitisation, including the digitisation of past data and records at the Regional Authorities (RAs) of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) across the country. From 1st April 2027, no person should be required or expected to visit any of the offices physically for these services.

He said that, wherever physical verification of original documents is necessary, a small counter could be provided to facilitate verification and uploading of documents. Computers could also be installed at office entrances to enable simultaneous verification and uploading of documents, wherever required. The Minister encouraged self-certification and greater trust in stakeholders, stressing that the Government should demonstrate its confidence in citizens and businesses.

Shri Goyal also called for the simplification of processes, formats and forms, and urged the departments to break organisational silos and work collectively to deliver better outcomes for businesses and citizens. He said that improved coordination between the two departments and the various organisations under the Ministry would be essential to achieving the objectives of the initiative.

The Minister informed that the Ministry currently has around 500 offices and 46 organisations. Except for very large campuses, such as the large office of ECGC in Mumbai, which would continue to function independently, the other offices would be brought under the co-location arrangement. He clarified that the co-located centres would not provide services only for the organisations physically situated there but would facilitate services across all 46 organisations and different departments under the Ministry.

He said that even where officials of a particular organisation were not physically stationed at a co-located office, people would be encouraged to interact with them through video conferencing. Accordingly, Shri Goyal directed that adequate video conferencing facilities be provided at every co-located office, with the provision to expand them to two or three counters depending on the size and requirements of the office.

The Minister emphasised that these centres should increasingly function as facilitation and promotion offices. Their role would be to promote investments and foreign trade, assist people seeking guidance, attract investments into India, encourage capital expenditure in the country and promote exports. He clarified that their purpose should not be limited to facilitating the issuance of licences.

Shri Goyal said that the co-location of offices, digitisation and introduction of faceless assessments would enhance transparency, accountability and public confidence. A unified presence of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in each State would assure businesses and stakeholders that they could access support and guidance through a single location.

Highlighting the importance of efficient service delivery amid considerable uncertainty and volatility in international trade and global geopolitical affairs, the Minister said that time was of the essence and competitiveness was crucial for success. He called upon officials to ensure that the functioning of every office was facilitative, supportive, friendly and helpful. He added that bringing offices together under one roof would also help establish checks and balances in their functioning.

The Minister directed that every office be equipped with CCTV cameras connected to a central server in Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, to enable random monitoring of work being undertaken across the country. He clarified that the objective was not continuous monitoring but periodic checks to oversee functioning and provide protection against theft and other such incidents.

He further directed that all offices must possess the necessary approvals required for their functioning, including Fire Brigade approvals and approvals under the Shops and Establishments Act. Emphasising the importance of workplace facilities, he said that every office must have high-quality toilets for men and women, with multi-gender facilities wherever appropriate in smaller offices. All offices must also have accessible toilets for persons with disabilities. He stressed that the quality of these facilities should be at least at par with, and preferably better than, those at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, and directed that adequate resources be allocated for this purpose.

Shri Goyal also emphasised that furniture and equipment should be modular wherever possible and that all procurement, including furniture, equipment, lighting and curtains, should be domestic or Swadeshi, except where absolutely unavoidable.

The Minister urged officials to examine opportunities for further reducing timelines and introducing deemed approvals wherever feasible. He called upon the Secretaries, Additional Secretaries and Joint Secretaries to regularly conduct video conferences or hybrid meetings with stakeholders across different regions. He also stressed the need to continuously identify ways to reduce paperwork and make it easier for people to obtain services and outcomes from the Ministry's offices.

Shri Goyal said that the initiative would strengthen teamwork within the two departments and among various internal and external stakeholders, improve coordination between different wings of the Ministry and enhance overall operational efficiency. It would help the Ministry become more contemporary and modern while preparing it for its role in the journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

Highlighting the expanding responsibilities of the Ministry in the context of several new trade agreements and the opening up of new markets, the Minister said that India had emerged as a bold, confident and unstoppable economy on the global stage. He emphasised the need to prepare the country for the goal of becoming a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047.

Reiterating that the fundamental responsibility of the Ministry was to serve the people and businesses of India, Shri Goyal said that, as Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has emphasised, the citizen is like God and the Government's responsibility is to serve citizens with that spirit.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Abhijith Narayanan/ Ishita Biswas

item.title: India Aiming for Global Competitiveness Through Indigenous Capabilities and International Cooperation: Dr. Jitendra Singh at IPRD 2026
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Earth Sciences
item.description: Ministry of Earth Sciences India Aiming for Global Competitiveness Through Indigenous Capabilities and International Cooperation: Dr. Jitendra Singh at IPRD 2026 India’s First Human Deep-Sea Mission to Reach Depths of Up to 6,000 Metres by 2028, Alongside Progress in Gaganyaan Mission Deep Ocean Resources to Be a Major Source of Economic Value Addition for Achieving Viksit Bharat 2047: Dr. Jitendra Singh ‘One Ocean, Shared Knowledge and Equitable Prosperity’ Should Guide Indo-Pacific Cooperation: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Prime Minister’s Reference to Deep Ocean Mission in…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
India Aiming for Global Competitiveness Through Indigenous Capabilities and International Cooperation: Dr. Jitendra Singh at IPRD 2026
India’s First Human Deep-Sea Mission to Reach Depths of Up to 6,000 Metres by 2028, Alongside Progress in Gaganyaan Mission
Deep Ocean Resources to Be a Major Source of Economic Value Addition for Achieving Viksit Bharat 2047: Dr. Jitendra Singh
‘One Ocean, Shared Knowledge and Equitable Prosperity’ Should Guide Indo-Pacific Cooperation: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
Prime Minister’s Reference to Deep Ocean Mission in Independence Day Addresses Reflects Strategic Priority to Ocean Resources: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

India is aiming to achieve global competitiveness in ocean research and exploration through indigenous capabilities, international cooperation and global co-creation, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said while addressing the Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue (IPRD) 2026, organised by the National Maritime Foundation under the Ministry of Defence.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India's approach to scientific missions in recent years has increasingly been based on a mission-mode framework, bringing together multiple departments and institutions rather than confining research to individual ministries. He highlighted the growing convergence of ocean sciences, space technology, nuclear science, geology, electronics and robotics in advancing India's maritime and deep-ocean capabilities.

Highlighting India's indigenous capabilities in deep-ocean exploration, the Minister said that the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, has developed the capability to conduct trials at depths of 5,000 to 6,000 metres in the Central Indian Ocean Basin. He also referred to the Ocean Mineral Explorer, which enables high-resolution exploration of hydrothermal sulphide deposits, several of which have already been identified.He noted that the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi reference to the Deep Ocean Mission twice in his Independence Day addresses reflects the priority accorded to ocean resources at the highest level and their strategic importance for India's future.

Referring to the Samudrayaan Mission, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the Matsya submersible is designed to carry three aquanauts to depths of 5,000–6,000 metres. He said that India is progressing towards sending its first human deep-sea mission to a depth of up to 6,000 metres by 2028, marking an important milestone in the country's indigenous deep-ocean exploration programme.

Drawing a parallel with India's human spaceflight programme, the Minister said that the country is working towards a remarkable convergence of deep-sea and space exploration. He expressed the vision of having an Indian human being undertake a deep-sea journey to nearly 6,000 metres while almost simultaneously another Indian travels into space, reflecting the country's growing scientific and technological capabilities.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India's ocean research is increasingly supported by space-based capabilities. He referred to dedicated satellites contributing to ocean-related research through observations of ocean colour, sea-surface temperature and wind vectors. These capabilities, he said, are expanding the scope of ocean observation and could also support future exploration of renewable energy resources from the oceans, including wind and solar energy.

Emphasising the importance of a whole-of-government and whole-of-science approach, the Minister highlighted the contribution of different scientific institutions and departments to India's ocean-related missions. He referred to the role of nuclear technology in seawater desalination, including the desalination plant at Kalpakkam established with the support of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and the low-temperature desalination facility in Lakshadweep developed through the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

The Minister said these initiatives demonstrate how different scientific disciplines and technologies can work together to address national requirements, including access to potable water in coastal and island regions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that international cooperation would be equally important in advancing ocean research, as oceans do not follow political boundaries drawn by countries. Issues such as marine pollution and changes in ocean temperature have consequences extending across national jurisdictions, making collective scientific efforts essential.

The Minister called for global strategies and partnerships based on joint scientific missions, reciprocal access to research facilities and data sharing. He said India's approach should be guided by the principle of “One Ocean, Shared Knowledge and Equitable Prosperity”, with the diversity of histories, cultures and geographies across the Indo-Pacific serving as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation.

The Minister outlined key priorities for strengthening regional cooperation, including closing observational gaps and improving the forecasting of extreme events; establishing regional climate services partnerships for coasts and islands; promoting responsible and accessible ocean technologies; advancing deep-ocean research; and strengthening conservation and equitable use of ocean resources.

Highlighting the role of research and innovation funding, Dr. Jitendra Singh referred to the establishment of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and the announcement of the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund to accelerate private-sector participation in research and development.

Dr Jitendra Singh said the RDI Fund provides for a 50:50 equity-based approach, encouraging private-sector stakeholders and investors to participate alongside the government in emerging areas of research and technology. He emphasised that government departments, scientific institutions, private-sector stakeholders and investors must work together to develop new sectors and strengthen India's technological capabilities.

Connecting ocean exploration with the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, the Minister said that achieving the country's development goals would require identifying new sources of economic value addition. He observed that a significant part of this potential lies in resources that remain unexplored or underexplored, with the deep ocean representing one of the major opportunities.

During the interaction with participants, Dr. Jitendra Singh also addressed a question on the potential of nuclear-powered vessels and the future of clean energy in maritime transport. He referred to the recent opening of the nuclear sector to private participation under the SHANTI Act and India's target of achieving 100 GW of nuclear energy capacity by 2047. He said that the Deep Ocean Mission is also exploring different possibilities for generating renewable energy from the oceans, including through solar panels, ocean winds and temperature or energy gradients.

Responding to a suggestion on extending the Swachh Bharat initiative to the oceans, the Minister said that the government had already initiated an annual ocean-cleanliness campaign. Recalling its beginning during the commemoration of 75 years of Independence, he said the initiative had since developed into an annual effort involving coastal district administrations, the Indian Navy, the Indian Coast Guard, NGOs and other stakeholders. He emphasised that marine pollution cannot remain confined to one country and that efforts towards cleaner oceans would benefit the wider Indo-Pacific region.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India's growing indigenous capabilities, combined with international partnerships and responsible sharing of scientific knowledge, would be crucial to strengthening its role in global ocean research and exploration. He called upon stakeholders to work collectively towards the peaceful, sustainable and equitable use of ocean resources, contributing to the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises ‘Samavesh Se VIKAS’ to Review PM VIKAS Implementation and Strengthen Stakeholder Engagement
MoUs with four institutions to expand industry-oriented training and traditional skill development opportunities for youth from minority communities
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Minority Affairs organised “Samavesh Se VIKAS – Implementation Review and Stakeholder Dialogue” on 4 November 2026 at Samrasta Hall, Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The event brought together over 80 participants, in the presence of Shri Shyama Prasad Roy, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, and Ms. Neha Giri, Director, Ministry of Minority Affairs. Representatives of Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) and other stakeholders participated in discussions focused on reviewing the progress of Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), addressing implementation-related challenges and identifying measures to strengthen training quality, placements and overall outcomes under the scheme.

 

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shyama Prasad Roy, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, emphasised the importance of ensuring that skill development translates into meaningful employment opportunities and a better future for beneficiaries.

 

 

“The theme is 'Samavesh Se VIKAS', and it is not a mere slogan. Our expectation is that every beneficiary, whether a girl, a school dropout or any trainee, completes skilling with a certificate in hand, gets a job and moves towards a brighter future. That is the plan,” he said.

The event also marked the signing of Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) under PM VIKAS with Pithampur Auto Cluster (PAC), the Centre of Excellence in Maritime & Shipbuilding (CEMS), and the Institute of Entrepreneurship Development (IED). These partnerships aim to expand access to skill development and industry-oriented training for youth from minority communities across different sectors and regions.

 

 

The partnership with PAC will facilitate skill training for 2,400 candidates in Madhya Pradesh in job roles aligned with emerging industry requirements, including Electric Vehicle Service Technician, CNC Milling Programmer, Warehouse Associate and Supply Chain Executive (Sustainability).

The MoU with CEMS will facilitate skill training for 6,300 candidates across Karnataka, Puducherry, Maharashtra, Telangana, West Bengal, Odisha and Gujarat. The training will cover several job roles, including Business Analyst, Warehouse Supervisor, AI Technocrat and Guest Service Executive (Front Office), among others.

 

Under the partnership with IED, 900 candidates in Uttar Pradesh will receive skill training in the Solar PV Installer (Suryamitra) job role. The initiative aims to equip young people with industry-relevant skills and prepare them for emerging employment opportunities in the renewable energy sector, contributing to the development of a skilled workforce for India's growing green energy ecosystem.

In another development under PM VIKAS, the Ministry of Minority Affairs signed an MoU with the Central University of Kashmir on 3 November 2026 for the implementation of training under the Traditional Skill component of the scheme. Under this initiative, 120 candidates will receive training as willow craft artisans in Ganderbal district, Jammu & Kashmir, through a 390-hour training programme. The initiative aims to preserve traditional craftsmanship while helping participants develop skills that can support sustainable livelihood opportunities.

 

 

During the event, Ms. Neha Giri, Director, Ministry of Minority Affairs, made a presentation on the progress of PM VIKAS, highlighting its implementation status, key areas requiring attention and priorities for the way forward. She stressed the need for PIAs to give greater attention to employment outcomes and maintain closer engagement with employers.

“We expect all our PIAs to place a much sharper focus on placement outcomes, employer engagement and timely reporting of verified placement data,” she said.

 

 

A key session of the event was the PIA-wise implementation review, during which progress under PM VIKAS was examined alongside issues and challenges faced by implementing agencies. The review provided a platform for detailed discussions on implementation-related concerns, identifying areas requiring attention and exploring practical measures to strengthen coordination, training delivery, placement outcomes and monitoring mechanisms. The discussions also focused on improving accountability and ensuring that training programmes lead to meaningful employment opportunities for beneficiaries.

The event further included discussions on strengthening quality assurance through independent monitoring by the Quality Council of India (QCI) and Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore). Technology-driven solutions were also discussed, including BlueDot for improving placement outcomes and Voice AI for collecting candidate feedback, as presented by EkStep Foundation. The discussions also covered the role of the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) in the skill development ecosystem, with emphasis on strengthening industry linkages and employment opportunities.

A presentation by ITIHAAS – Indian Traditions and Heritage Society on “Upskilling for Youth in Heritage and Tourism” highlighted opportunities for developing skills among young people in the heritage and tourism sectors. The presentation focused on connecting skill development with India's cultural heritage and creating livelihood opportunities through tourism-related activities.

The event concluded with an interactive dialogue involving Ministry officials, stakeholders and PIAs, providing an opportunity to share field-level experiences, discuss implementation concerns and challenges, and offer recommendations for strengthening the delivery and effectiveness of PM VIKAS.

The Ministry of Minority Affairs remains committed to improving access to quality skill development, strengthening industry linkages and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for youth from minority communities through PM VIKAS.

item.title: Novel silicon chip allowing terahertz waves to pass through barriers could enable future 6G networks
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Novel silicon chip allowing terahertz waves to pass through barriers could enable future 6G networks Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi A new silicon chip that allows terahertz waves to pass through an engineered barrier with little loss, while carrying data at 100 Gbit/s, points to compact terahertz circuits for future 6G communication technologies. Future sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to use terahertz frequencies, which lie between microwaves and infrared light and offer wide…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Novel silicon chip allowing terahertz waves to pass through barriers could enable future 6G networks
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

A new silicon chip that allows terahertz waves to pass through an engineered barrier with little loss, while carrying data at 100 Gbit/s, points to compact terahertz circuits for future 6G communication technologies.

Future sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to use terahertz frequencies, which lie between microwaves and infrared light and offer wide bandwidth. Guiding these waves through compact circuits is challenging, as bends, junctions and abrupt changes in a waveguide can scatter or reflect part of the signal, weakening it as it travels.

By arranging triangular holes in a carefully designed pattern in a silicon slab, researchers can create a photonic crystal that guides terahertz waves along the boundary between two regions. Such boundary channels resist certain kinds of backscattering, but a practical circuit must also tolerate deliberately introduced obstacles and changes in geometry.

Researchers at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), approached this challenge through topological photonics and demonstrated data transmission at up to 100 gigabits per second (Gbit/s) across an engineered barrier. A single barrier added only about 1–2% loss, and two barriers in sequence about 2–3%. In a conventional, non-topological waveguide, a comparable barrier markedly reduces transmission.

The team designed a silicon photonic crystal whose structure mimics the honeycomb lattice of graphene, and created a barrier by changing the sizes of the triangular holes over a short section of the waveguide.

Transmission remained close to its barrier-free level as long as the barrier strength stayed below a characteristic coupling strength of the crystal. Because the barrier is set by hole geometry, this offers a practical design rule for such devices.

The researchers tested the concept in three devices fabricated on high-resistivity silicon, a material compatible with established semiconductor manufacturing: one with two barriers in sequence, one with an omega-shaped route containing four sharp bends and a central barrier, and a power splitter with a barrier in one of its two branches.

Measurements across 310–360 GHz agreed closely with simulations. In the splitter, the two output signals were nearly identical, showing that the barrier had little effect on transmission.

Figure 1. Artistic illustration of photonic Klein tunnelling in a silicon valley photonic crystal chip. A terahertz signal carrying high-speed data crosses the engineered barrier (blue) without significant loss, supporting 100 Gbit/s data transmission for 6G communication.

 

In high-speed data tests, the double-barrier and omega-shaped devices carried 48 and 60 Gbit/s, respectively. The splitter supported 100 Gbit/s using QAM-32 modulation, which encodes information in the signal’s amplitude and phase. At this rate, a 5-gigabyte high-definition film could in principle be transferred in under half a second.

Figure 2. The research team in the Meta Optics Laboratory (MetoLab), JNCASR, with the fabricated silicon chip used to demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling.

 

The study was led by Dr Abhishek Kumar, Assistant Professor at JNCASR, where he heads the Meta Optics Laboratory (MetoLab), with Samina Mulla and Sangram Kumar Sadhu of JNCASR as joint first authors. Collaborators included Asif Iqbal M and N. S. Vidhyadhiraja (JNCASR); Siddhartha Lal (IISER Kolkata); Anshuman Kumar (IIT Bombay); Zhonghua Gu and Prakash Pitchappa (Institute of Microelectronics, A*STAR, Singapore, and Pascal Szriftgiser and Guillaume Ducournau (University of Lille and CNRS, France).

“Showing that terahertz waves can cross a barrier created simply by changing the hole geometry, while carrying 100 gigabits per second, suggests that this effect can become a useful design tool for terahertz chips,” said Dr Abhishek Kumar.

The results could help researchers develop terahertz circuits that route and split signals on a single chip with low loss. The team next plans to tune the barriers electrically, thermally or mechanically, which could allow a device to redirect signals between paths on demand. The work has been published in the journal Advanced Materials.

Publication Link: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.75322

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Advanced protective coatings to improve machining of critical superalloys can help aerospace, energy & petrochemical sectors
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

An advanced surface-engineering approach developed by scientists can help improve the durability of cutting tools used for machining super alloys.

This could help aerospace, energy and petrochemical sectors, where nickel-based superalloys are indispensable for components operating under extreme conditions.

Machining of super alloys for use in aircraft engines, power plants and petrochemical systems is a major manufacturing challenge. Nickel-based superalloys such as Inconel 718 (IN718), IN625 and IN617 possess exceptional strength and hardness which make them difficult to cut or shape. Rapid work hardening, poor thermal conductivity and strong chemical interaction with cutting tools accelerate tool wear, reduce productivity and increase manufacturing costs.

Scientists from the International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI), Hyderabad, an autonomous R&D Centre of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) have developed and evaluated two nanocomposite protective coatings—Titanium Aluminium Silicon Nitride (TiAlSiN) and Chromium Aluminium Silicon Nitride (CrAlSiN)—on widely used tungsten carbide cutting tools.

The coatings were deposited in-house using cathodic-arc physical vapour deposition and this helped evaluate the performance of tools for milling of IN718, IN625 and IN617. The study examined both tool life and the mechanisms governing coating performance.

The research revealed an important finding: there is no single coating that performs best for every superalloy. The effectiveness of a protective coating depends significantly on the chemistry of the material being machined and its interaction with the coating.

For IN718, the TiAlSiN-coated tool improved tool life by about 80% compared with an uncoated tool, while for IN625, the improvement was about 60%. For IN617, however, CrAlSiN proved remarkably superior, increasing tool life by more than 200%. The results demonstrate that one coating may be better suited to IN718 and IN625, while another can perform substantially better for IN617. The findings provide a scientific basis for selecting coatings according to the specific alloy being machined.

Fig 1: Advanced nanocomposite coatings significantly improve the life of tungsten carbide cutting tools. The results show that the optimum coating depends on the specific nickel-based superalloy being machined.

 

The researchers also investigated how cutting tools failed. A major cause of damage was repeated adhesion of workpiece material to the tool surface. During machining, a layer of the superalloy can stick to the cutting edge and, when it subsequently breaks away, it pulls tiny fragments from the tool, progressively causing chipping. The coatings helped delay this damage and extend tool life. Chipping and progressive wear were identified as the major failure modes, with abrasion, adhesion and attrition contributing to the overall wear process.

Fig2: A Scanning Electron Microscope image of a cutting-tool edge showing workpiece adhesion, abrasion, chipping and lateral cracks—key mechanisms responsible for tool failure during machining of nickel-based superalloys.

 

The researchers also examined the metal chips generated during machining. The chips exhibited characteristic shear bands and serrated or saw-tooth patterns, reflecting the intense thermo-mechanical conditions during cutting. The degree of chip segmentation was related to tool performance, providing further insight into the complex machining behaviour of these advanced alloys.

Longer-lasting cutting tools can reduce downtime, improve productivity and lower the cost of machining high-value engineering components.

More significantly, the study points towards a science-based, application-specific approach to protective coatings. Rather than seeking a universally superior coating, manufacturers can select or design coatings based on the composition and behaviour of the particular alloy being machined. This can contribute to more efficient, reliable and cost-effective manufacturing of components made from advanced materials.

The research carried out at ARCI's Centre for Engineered Coatings, has been published in the journal Materials Today Communications.

The study demonstrates that the key to improving the machining of some of industry's most demanding materials lies not merely in developing a better coating, but in matching the right coating to the right material.

Link to Publication:

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtcomm.2024.109101

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Coal
item.description: Ministry of Coal Ministry of Coal Achieves 130% Target in Site Cleaning and 162% in Scrap Disposal Under Special Campaign 6 Scrap Disposal Generates ₹61.41 Crore, with 100% Disposal of Public Grievances and PMO References CPSEs Promote Innovative Waste-to-Wealth Initiatives for Sustainable Resource Management Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Coal and its CPSEs demonstrated extraordinary over-achievement across all key parameters during Special Campaign 6, establishing exemplary benchmarks in institutional clean-up and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal Achieves 130% Target in Site Cleaning and 162% in Scrap Disposal Under Special Campaign 6
Scrap Disposal Generates ₹61.41 Crore, with 100% Disposal of Public Grievances and PMO References
CPSEs Promote Innovative Waste-to-Wealth Initiatives for Sustainable Resource Management
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal and its CPSEs demonstrated extraordinary over-achievement across all key parameters during Special Campaign 6, establishing exemplary benchmarks in institutional clean-up and administrative reform.

The Ministry cleaned 2,035 sites against a target of 1,565 (130% achievement) and cleared over 14.84 million sq. ft. of area against the planned 10.18 million sq. ft. (146% achievement). Alongside these physical accomplishments, the Ministry recorded perfect 100% disposal rates in successfully resolving 253 out of 253 Public Grievances and clearing 52 out of 52 PMO references.

Overall scrap disposal reached 17,686 metric tons against a target of 10,909 metric tons (162% achievement), yielding a total revenue of ₹61.41 crore. Furthermore, the Ministry made monumental strides in streamlining file operations by reviewing 1,79,793 physical and E-files against a target of 59,593 and total files weeding out and closed are 1,70,336. These operational successes were amplified by social media outreach that featured 16,424 tweets and 38 PIB releases issued.

Prominent best practices executed during the campaign include:

  1. NLC India Limited (NLCIL) developed a Waste-to-Wealth Children's Eco Park at Mine-I, Neyveli, inaugurated on 22 October 2026. The park showcases sustainable resource utilisation through the reuse of 2.5 MT of iron scrap, 3,000 solid blocks and salvaged timber, including wood recovered from trees felled during Cyclone Thane.

 

  1. Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), has transformed a large room previously used for storing junk and discarded materials into a beautiful, fully equipped crèche facility at its headquarters here in Sanctoria, demonstrating how effective space utilisation can contribute to employee welfare and workplace improvement.

Before

After

 

  1. Scrap oil drums in the Krishnashila Area, Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) were creatively upcycled and repurposed to construct an aesthetic welcome sign board for “Krishnakunj”. By repainting the discarded drums in vibrant colors and mounting lettering on them, waster material was effectively transformed into an attractive entrance installation.

 

  1. Some notable work from South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) includes:

Singhali Underground Mine in the Korba Area, workers constructed a working model of the Paste-Fill Mining System from scrap materials to demonstrate how fly ash and industrial waste can backfill mined voids to enhance structural stability and prevent land subsidence.

At the Kusmunda Area, employees built a replica of Tiger Hill featuring soldier figures and the National Flag to honor the sacrifices of the Indian Armed Forces during Operation Vijay in the 1999 Kargil War.

Bhatgaon Area introduced a ‘Kabaad Se Jugaad’ installation centered around a miner figure to advocate waste reduction, recycling, and sustainable lifestyle practices.

 

  1. The Mandamarri Area, SCCL creatively transformed waste scrap materials into two distinct artworks: a Shiv Ling idol adorned with sacred symbols and traditional elements, and a separate Trishul artwork. The initiative promotes the Waste to Wealth concept through innovative scrap reuse while reducing scrap accumulation on the premises.

 

Through these comprehensive clean-up operations, innovative waste-to-wealth initiatives, and robust administrative reforms, the Ministry of Coal has set a high standard for public sector efficiency and sustainability. By combining record-breaking physical achievements with creative employee-welfare and environmental practices, the Ministry continues to demonstrate its steadfast commitment to governance excellence, resource optimization, and the broader goals of Swachh Bharat.

NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German…
item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog and GIZ India Sign Implementation Agreement under Nationally Determined Contribution-Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) to Accelerate Road Freight Decarbonisation
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) on 3rd November 2026. NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government's International Climate Initiative (IKI). World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India and Agora Energiewende are among the initiative's implementing partners.

Decarbonising road freight is an important component of India's transition towards a sustainable, energy-efficient and low-carbon transport system. However, the electrification of medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles remains at an early stage, highlighting the need for adequate charging infrastructure, innovative financing mechanisms and an enabling regulatory framework. The Agreement formalises the collaboration between the project partners for accelerating the decarbonisation of India's road freight sector. The initiative will contribute to India's broader efforts to achieve its Nationally Determined Contribution targets and long-term climate goals.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Shram Samvad: Indore & Dhar Region Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

A District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme, “Shram Samvad”, on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection, was jointly organized by Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India (GoI) and Labour Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with Association of Industries Madhya Pradesh and Pithampur Audhyogik Sangathan at Indore, Madhya Pradesh on 3rd November, 2026.

The programme aimed at enhancing awareness among employers, HR, Legal and Finance professionals regarding the Labour Codes and rules made thereunder. It also focused on strengthening awareness and institutional capacity on labour reforms, welfare and social protection, promoting Centre-State coordination and stakeholder engagement. Sushri Sheetala Patle, IAS, Labour Commissioner, Madhya Pradesh presided over the programme and participants included senior officials from MoLE, Labour Department, GoMP, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) , Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC(C)], Directorate General Labour Welfare (DGLW) along with more than 150 participants from employers, industry representatives, legal, HR and finance professionals

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the GoI.

Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE presented the keynote address highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes. Various sessions were conducted by officials from MoLE, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under each of the four Labour Codes and Central Rules notified under the Labour Codes. The sessions provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new labour codes. 

Representatives from EPFO and DGLW also led sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme, respectively.

To facilitate the employers and compliance professionals in effective implementation of the Labour Codes and Rules, ‘Handbook of Compliance for Employers’ and ‘Compilation of Frequently Asked Questions’ developed by MoLE were also shared with the participants.

An engaging Question and Answer session was also held, enabling participants to address their queries and gain greater clarity on the Labour Codes, compliance requirements, and social security provisions. By bringing together Central Government and State Government authorities and industry representatives, the event contributed to enhanced awareness, improved understanding, and stronger stakeholder engagement, thereby supporting the effective adoption and implementation of the New Labour Codes.

item.title: A Rulebook Alone Cannot Guarantee Dignity; Every Hand in Aviation Must Ensure It: Manmeet Kaur Nanda
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
