item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat’s ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ Campaign Engages over 11,800 Youth Through 60 Programmes Across 20 States/UTs
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

Over 11,800 youth participated in 60 editions of ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’, organised across 20 States and Union Territories today by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. With the latest round of programmes, a total of 220 Yuva Samvaads have been conducted across 29 States and Union Territories, engaging 43,995 youth and 220 Youth Icons.

The nationwide campaign is being conducted from 26.10.2026 to 05.11.2026, with the aim of covering 500 universities, colleges and educational institutions across the country. It seeks to promote electoral awareness among young people, particularly first-time voters, and encourage their informed participation in the democratic process. The initiative familiarises them with voting rights, electoral procedures and civic responsibilities while providing opportunities to interact with elected representatives, Youth Icons and other distinguished personalities.

In New Delhi, Union Minister of State for Corporate Affairs and Road Transport and Highways Shri Harsh Malhotra attended the programme and shared insights on voting rights, the importance of electoral participation and the role of young people as responsible citizens in strengthening democracy.

In West Bengal, Member of Parliament from the Ranaghat (SC) Lok Sabha constituency, Shri Jagannath Sarkar, attended the programme in Nadia and interacted with students, while in Assam, MP Shri Devasish Sharma engaged with youth at Nagaon.

In Bihar, programmes in Purbi Champaran (Motihari) and Siwan featured the collective Loktantrik Pledge, with participants reaffirming their commitment to responsible citizenship and active participation in democracy. Shri Tarkishore Prasad, former Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar and MLA from Katihar Sadar, interacted with young participants during the Yuva Samvad in Katihar and encouraged them to understand the importance of their vote and actively contribute to strengthening democracy.

In Haryana, Wushu player and Youth Icon Aryan Sood interacted with young participants in Panipat on the role of youth in politics, voting awareness and career opportunities in sports. In Punjab, the programme at Mansa featured an interactive session between the Youth Icon and participants, along with the collective Loktantrik Pledge.

In Madhya Pradesh, programmes across Barwani, Balaghat, Bhind, Chhindwara, Dindori, Guna, Panna, Ratlam and Sagar featured interactions with Youth Icons, sports personalities and public representatives, and the Loktantrik Pledge. The programmes also introduced youth to MY Bharat opportunities and its digital platforms.

In Uttar Pradesh, the programme at Amethi (Sultanpur) featured a presentation by a Youth Icon, followed by an interactive question-and-answer session. Influencer Rishabh Mishra addressed participants and recited poetry, while Dr. Dhananjay Singh and Shri Vishuv Mishra delivered motivational addresses and interacted with youth.

Through these programmes, MY Bharat continues to provide young people with opportunities to interact with public representatives and Youth Icons, understand electoral processes and engage in discussions on democratic participation and civic responsibilities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE Empanels 19 Institutions as Centres of Excellence-Skills
Certificates of Recognition presented by Secretary, MSDE, at Kaushal Bhawan
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) today formally recognised 19 reputed institutions as Centres of Excellence-Skills (CoE-Skills). The Certificates of Recognition were presented by Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, during a ceremony held at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi. The recognition is valid from 9 October 2026 to 8 October 2029.

The institutions have been empanelled through the Green Channel provided under the Guidelines for Empanelment of Centres of Excellence-Skills and Vocational Training Centres. The mechanism offers an expedited route for eligible institutions of established standing, including Institutes of National Importance, ITIs upgraded under PM-SETU, and Skilling Centres of Excellence operated or empanelled by Central Ministries, Departments and State Governments. Under this route, institutions submit essential information and their applications are placed directly before the Executive Committee for consideration, without nomination or the regular evaluation process. The mechanism seeks to accelerate empanelment of reputed and high-quality institutions through a streamlined approval process.

The Guidelines were unveiled on 15 July 2026 by Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, during the World Youth Skills Day celebrations at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi. The Guidelines seek to strengthen the skilling ecosystem through permanent, advanced and industry-aligned training institutions supported by modern infrastructure, technology and strong industry partnerships.

Speaking on the occasion, Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said: “The empanelment of these 19 institutions as Centres of Excellence-Skills marks an important step towards building a trusted national network of permanent, advanced and industry-responsive skilling institutions. We are building a repository of the country’s most reputed institutions, distinguished by their domain expertise and delivery excellence, to strengthen skill development outcomes while making skilling aspirational for our youth. These Centres can play a pivotal role in delivering high-quality training, supporting trainers and assessors, strengthening industry linkages and improving outcomes for learners. We look forward to working closely with these institutions to make advanced and future-ready skilling accessible across sectors and regions.”

A CoE-Skills is envisaged as a permanent, advanced and sector-focused training centre capable of delivering high-quality, industry-aligned and outcome-oriented skill training. CoE-Skills may undertake functions spanning advanced and technology-enabled training, assessment, mentorship and career coaching, Training of Trainers and Assessors, industry engagement, and achievement and tracking of post-training outcomes. Their scheme-agnostic empanelment is intended to establish a long-term association and enable optimum utilisation of existing infrastructure, equipment, trainers, assessors and institutional capacity.

The recognition provides formal acknowledgement by MSDE of these institutions’ capabilities within the national skilling ecosystem. Empanelled Centres may be leveraged for skill development initiatives of MSDE, other Central Ministries, State Governments, industry, CSR initiatives and other stakeholders, subject to applicable programme guidelines.

By bringing high-quality institutions and specialised centres into a common national framework, the CoE-Skills initiative will help strengthen advanced training capacity, facilitate wider sharing of institutional expertise and promote credible, industry-responsive and outcome-oriented skilling across the country.

Institutions recognised as Centres of Excellence-Skills

Renewable Energy

  1. Hydro & Renewable Energy Department, IIT Roorkee, Uttarakhand
  2. National Institute of Solar Energy, Gurugram, Haryana
  3. National Institute of Wind Energy, Chennai, Tamil Nadu
  4. National Institute of Wind Energy, Kayathar, Tamil Nadu
  5. Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Renewable Energy, Kapurthala, Punjab

Chemicals & Petrochemical

  1. CIPET: CSTS, Guwahati, Assam
  2. CIPET: CSTS, Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra
  3. CIPET: IPT, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
  4. CIPET: IPT, Kochi, Kerala
  5. CIPET: CSTS, Bhubaneswar, Odisha

Construction

  1. Indian Railways Institute of Civil Engineering, Pune, Maharashtra

Multi-Sectoral

  1. National Institute of Hydrography, Vasco da Gama, Goa
  2. Sant Shiromani Ravidas Global Skills Park, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh
  3. World Skill Centre, Bhubaneswar, Odisha
  4. Defence Institute of Advanced Technology, Pune, Maharashtra

Iron and Steel

  1. National Institute of Secondary Steel Technology, Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab

Marine Engineering

  1. INS Shivaji Premier Training Institute for Marine Engineers of the Indian Navy, Pune, Maharashtra

Tourism & Hospitality

  1. Institute of Hotel Management Catering Technology & Applied Nutrition, Bhubaneswar, Odisha 

Agriculture

  1. National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management, Hyderabad, Telangana

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries and its CPSEs and ABs conclude Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6 (SCDPM 6)
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), along with its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and Autonomous Bodies (ABs), has successfully concluded the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6 (SCDPM 6). This year, the campaign placed special emphasis on “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-Waste”, alongside cleanliness, reduction of pendency and improved workplace management.

During the implementation phase of SCPDM 6, observed from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, MHI and its CPSEs/ABs undertook various activities including comprehensive review of old physical and electronic files, identified unserviceable items, scrap and e-waste, and initiated measures for their proper disposal. These activities aimed at freeing up office space, improving record management and promoting cleaner, well-organised and efficient workplaces.

Bridge and Roof Ltd. employees take initiative to free up space at Chennai office through File Weeding

Special Focus on E-Waste Management

In line with this year's theme, special attention was given to the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste across offices and industrial units under MHI. The CPSEs/ABs identified e-waste generated at their respective establishments and took necessary steps for its segregation and disposal in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

  

  Disposal of E-waste at the premises of AYCL and ICAT

The initiative helped to ensure proper handling of e-waste and promote responsible waste management practices across the CPSEs/ABs under the Ministry.

Cleanliness and plantation drives were also organised across office campuses and industrial units. These activities helped in maintaining clean, safe and organised workplaces while encouraging a culture of cleanliness, accountability and responsible waste management.

Key targets achieved during the implementation phase i.e. 02nd October to 31st October 2026 of Special Campaign are as under:

  • 1,540 cleanliness campaigns conducted across office campuses and industrial units.
  • 50,19,777 sq. ft. of space freed due to scrap disposal.
  • 4,467 e-waste items have been collected, segregated and disposed of.
  • A total revenue of Rs. 13,03,93,845/- has been generated through disposal of scrap and E-waste.

To raise awareness and to give wide coverage, 2108 social media posts were posted on different social media handles i.e X(Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, Youtube, LinkedIn etc. highlighting the significant activities undertaken by the Ministry along with its CPSEs/ABs under the Special Campaign 6.

Under Special Campaign 6, Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL), HPEP Hyderabad organised a mass cleanliness drive at Rayasamudram Lake and the adjoining road, with active participation from leadership, employees and the public. Approximately 32,290 sq. ft. of area was cleaned during the drive. BHEL’s PPPU Unit transformed 300 sq. ft. of its Civil Store Area through cleaning and rearrangement.

BHEL HPEP Hyderabad cleanliness drive covering the Rayasamudram Lake premises

Andrew Yule & Company Limited (AYCL) carried out cleanliness drive and weeding out of files and old documents carried out at AYCL’s Rajgarh Tea Estate Office, Assam.

Before and After images of AYCL’s Rajgarh Tea Estate Office, Assam

Cement Corporation of India Limited (CCIL), Bokajan organised a cleanliness drive at the CCIL Township Children’s Park, with the objective of promoting cleanliness and improving the surrounding environment. The initiative contributed towards creating a cleaner, healthier and more vibrant community. Further, the HR Department was renovated to enhance workplace cleanliness, organisation and overall efficiency.

Renovation of the HR Department at CCIL office

Through Special Campaign 6, the MHI endeavoured to promote cleaner, well-organised and efficient workplaces, reduce pendency and strengthen sustainable waste management practices, with a special focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste. The Ministry, along with its CPSEs and ABs, reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining cleanliness, ensuring efficient resource utilisation and promoting a culture of good governance and workplace efficiency.

***

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026
140 crore Indians take pride having navigated world crises effectively, and that despite these headwinds India's growth has remained robust: PM
The future of energy security lies in clean energy: PM
This new era of the solar revolution is not just about adoption, it is equally driven by innovation: PM
I strongly urge our startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs to develop models that ensure the maximum energy needs of a household are fulfilled through solar power: PM
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Addressing the gathering of industry leaders, investors, startup representatives, and senior officials from India and abroad, the Prime Minister noted that this year's summit takes place amid special circumstances dominated by global energy shocks that have underscored the vital importance of renewable energy in daily life and national development. He pointed out that the scope of this year's event is exceptionally broad as it coincides with the Ninth Assembly of the International Solar Alliance and includes delegates from the Fourth Conference on Green Hydrogen.

Observing that the global economy has weathered unprecedented disruptions ranging from the Corona pandemic to the ongoing West Asia crisis, the Prime Minister stated that 140 crore Indians take pride in how effectively the nation has managed the turmoil while maintaining high economic growth. He emphasized that ten years of sustained domestic investment and systemic reforms in clean energy shielded the country from severe external shocks. “If India had not invested in clean energy and created new systems for this over the past decade, then our crisis could have been much more severe than the rest of the world,” noted PM Modi.

Stating that recent global disruptions have demonstrated the direct link between energy security and economic security, the Prime Minister warned that continued over-reliance on fossil fuels will repeatedly disrupt the world economy because fossil reserves are finite and concentrated in a few regions. He contrasted this vulnerability with the boundless, universally accessible potential of clean energy. “And we all know, the future of Energy Security lies in Clean Energy,” asserted Shri Modi.

Describing India's 12-year clean energy journey as one defined by Promises, Passion, and Performance exemplified by its COP-26 commitment to achieve 500 Gigawatts of non-fossil capacity by 2030, the Prime Minister highlighted that the nation fulfilled its Paris pledge of sourcing half its installed power capacity from non-fossil sources in 2025, five years ahead of schedule. Noting that India now ranks among the top three nations in solar and renewable energy with over 50 percent non-fossil installed capacity and nearly 300 Gigawatts already achieved toward the 500-Gigawatt target, he announced an ambitious goal to add another 500 Gigawatts of new non-fossil capacity over the next 10 to 11 years. “This target is somewhat difficult, but I have faith in the capability of my country; therefore I say, We will do it!” affirmed PM Modi.

Emphasizing that India wishes to share the benefits of its innovations and experiences with all of humanity, the Prime Minister stated that the nation approaches green energy with the same cooperative spirit before presenting specific examples. “The successes of India in this field will come in handy for numerous countries of the world,” remarked Shri Modi.

Detailing the rapid progress of the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana launched in February 2024 to install rooftop solar panels in one crore homes, the Prime Minister noted that over 65 lakh households have joined the movement within 24 to 25 months at a pace of one lakh new homes every six days, cutting electricity bills by roughly 76 percent according to a study and reducing bills to zero for lakhs of families who now earn money by selling surplus power to the grid. “This scheme of India can give great strength to energy security in many countries,” observed PM Modi.

Highlighting efforts over the past 12 years to integrate solar power into daily life, industry, and agriculture, the Prime Minister pointed out that connecting over 44,000 government buildings with solar energy is saving nearly 700 crore rupees annually, while the KUSUM scheme has provided solar irrigation to over 30 lakh farmers and saved each solar pump beneficiary nearly one lakh rupees every year. He also cited the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana, which installs solar panels over reservoirs, ponds, and lakes to optimize water bodies and save land acquisition costs. “India is making solar power a part of the lives of its citizens,” noted Shri Modi.

Stating that India's clean energy ecosystem extends beyond hydro, solar, wind, and nuclear power, the Prime Minister explained that the country is advancing in mission mode under the National Green Hydrogen Mission to produce 50 lakh tonnes of green hydrogen by the end of the decade while integrating green hydrogen into the transport sector. “Just a few months ago, India started its first Green Hydrogen Train,” noted PM Modi.

Acknowledging that power generation must be matched by efficient distribution from high-production solar and wind zones to regions with lower output so that homes, farms, and industries across the country benefit equally, the Prime Minister highlighted the development of Green Energy Corridors comprising dedicated transmission lines and substations supported by the One Nation, One Power Grid network that unified five regional grids onto a single frequency. He added that the country is now advancing to the next phase to further strengthen this transmission infrastructure. “Recently, India has set a target of an investment of about 2 lakh crore rupees for this,” observed Shri Modi.

Attributing India's green energy success to a dramatic surge in domestic manufacturing after years of complete import dependence for even minor solar components, the Prime Minister noted that solar module manufacturing capacity has grown from around 2 Gigawatts a decade ago to over 200 Gigawatts today alongside nearly 40 Gigawatts of solar cell capacity and expanding production of other components. “Meaning, India's ambitions related to green energy are also proof of the success of our Atmanirbhar Bharat campaign and the Make in India campaign,” asserted PM Modi.

Stressing that the nation must maintain its rapid momentum rather than resting on its laurels, the Prime Minister called for swiftly connecting every government building, school, college, hospital, and streetlight network to solar energy. He proposed fostering healthy competition among states and local bodies to incentivize top performers and enable peer learning from local success stories. “We have to do this work at a fast pace,” asserted Shri Modi.

Offering a dedicated suggestion for expanding solar power in agriculture, the Prime Minister urged moving beyond the distribution of lakhs of solar pumps to utilizing uncultivated farm spaces. He emphasized the need to encourage farmers across maximum villages to install solar panels on vacant land as well as along farm boundary ridges. “We have to move beyond solar pumps,” remarked PM Modi.

Stating that the new era of the solar revolution relies on innovation as much as adoption, the Prime Minister urged startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs to design round-the-clock, all-weather solar models capable of meeting maximum household needs, including rooftop solar cooking to minimize reliance on imported gas and home solar charging for electric two-wheelers and cars. “Through this, middle-class families of the country can save thousands of rupees every year,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the need for specialized clean energy applications in rural allied sectors, the Prime Minister called for developing dedicated solar products to promote solar power in the dairy sector. “For animal fodder, crop harvesting, and post-harvest, solar equipment should be developed for every such work,” asserted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that achieving these goals requires next-generation innovation, indigenous storage hardware, and new battery storage capacity, the Prime Minister described this need as a massive opportunity for India's youth and urged researchers and investors to seize the moment. “The solutions that you prepare in India will come in handy for numerous countries of the world,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Pointing out that every clean energy initiative in one of the world's youngest nations is generating thousands of jobs across panel and hardware manufacturing, installation, servicing, and transportation, the Prime Minister noted that further expansion of solar capacity will multiply employment opportunities across the economy. “From the kitchen stove to the means of transport, when everything is solar-power-driven and green-energy-driven, then a new industry will be created,” observed PM Modi.

Inviting global investors to leverage India's unmatched demand, scale, scope, and political and policy stability, the Prime Minister noted that the renewable energy sector has attracted over 15 lakh crore rupees, or 164 billion dollars, over the past decade, including over 6 lakh crore rupees, or 63 billion dollars, in just the two years since the 2024 RE-INVEST Summit, with investment opportunities projected to exceed 20 lakh crore rupees, or 220 billion dollars, by the end of the decade. “Therefore, for all of you, a new sky of opportunities is going to open up in India's clean energy sector,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Recalling India's global message of One Earth, One Family, One Future that underpins both its clean energy journey and the International Solar Alliance, the Prime Minister stated that the nation is committed to ensuring necessary funding, technology, and expertise reach every country in need. “Therefore, for Africa, a proposal for a 200 million dollar Africa Solar Facility has been put forward,” noted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that the coming decade is vital for global climate goals, the Prime Minister expressed confidence that summit participants will play a pivotal role in securing the future by connecting every country and region to this transformation before concluding with his best wishes. “Only then will we be able to build a Clean Future, a Green Future, and a Secure Future,” asserted Shri Modi.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
National Conference on “Gender Data and Statistics: From Evidence to Policy Insights | MoSPI and UN Women
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

A one-day National Conference on “Gender Data and Statistics: From Evidence to Policy Insights” was organised by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in collaboration with UN Women on 2nd November, 2026 in New Delhi. The conference brought together policymakers, representatives from Central Ministries/Departments and State Governments, statisticians, researchers, academic institutions, technical experts and representatives of UN agencies to deliberate on strengthening the analysis and use of gender statistics for evidence-based policymaking.

The conference was organised to deliberate on and disseminate the findings of Women and Men in India 2025, a flagship publication of MoSPI, with the aim of deepening the understanding of key findings and their interlinkages across sectors, facilitating discussions among ministries and other stakeholders, and identifying opportunities to strengthen the analytical and policy use of gender statistics.

The conference commenced with a welcome address by Ms. Shoko Ishikawa, Country Representative, UN Women India, who emphasised the importance of gender-disaggregated data and bridging the gap between data producers and users. Mr. Jean-Eric Paque, Ambassador of the European Union (EU) to India, highlighted the EU–India Strategic Partnership in advancing gender equality and women’s economic participation. Dr. Preetam B. Yashvant, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development, also addressed the gathering, followed by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, who emphasised identifying gender gaps to inform evidence-based policies. Dr. Shamika Ravi, Member, Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, highlighted progress in welfare delivery and women’s financial empowerment, while stressing the need for improved employment quality, state-level analysis and stronger gender statistics to guide policy reforms. The inaugural session concluded with a vote of thanks by Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, MoSPI, who acknowledged the contributions of speakers, participants and UN Women.

The conference featured four thematic technical sessions, focusing on health and survival across the life course; girls’ education, learning and transition; women’s work, wages, formality and care; and women’s livelihoods, enterprises, skills and financial inclusion. The sessions brought together experts, policymakers and practitioners to examine key findings from Women and Men in India 2025, identify differences in outcomes between women and men, and explore opportunities for translating statistical evidence into actionable policy insights.

Discussions on health and survival recognised progress in maternal healthcare and essential health services, while highlighting nutritional and adolescent health challenges. The session on girls’ education, learning and transition noted improvements in enrolment, while emphasising gaps in learning outcomes, STEM participation and employment pathways.

Deliberations on women’s work, wages, formality and care acknowledged rising female labour-force participation, while highlighting challenges in job quality, wage disparities and unpaid care work. The session on women’s livelihoods, enterprises, skills and financial inclusion recognised progress in entrepreneurship and financial inclusion, while stressing the need for better access to credit, markets and sustainable livelihoods, alongside women’s agency and safety.

During the valedictory session, Ms. Suhela Khan, Country Programme Manager, Women’s Economic Empowerment, UN Women India, and Ms. Geeta Singh Rathore, Director General (NSS), MoSPI, highlighted the need to address persistent gender disparities in health, education and economic participation, with particular emphasis on quality of employment, unpaid care work and financial inclusion. The discussions also provided valuable inputs for future editions of Women and Men in India, particularly the 2026 edition, underscoring the importance of improved measurement of gender gaps, strengthened inter-ministerial coordination and evidence-based policymaking. The conference concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Ms. Sunitha Bhaskar, Additional Director General, MoSPI.

The conference concluded by reaffirming the importance of strengthening India's gender statistical ecosystem and fostering continued collaboration among government institutions, statistical agencies, researchers and development partners. It underscored the need to translate gender-disaggregated data into meaningful policy insights to support inclusive development and advancing gender equality.

*****

Samrat

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's address at the inauguration of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo in Delhi
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister in my Cabinet, Pralhad Joshi ji, Shripad Naik ji, all industry leaders, investors, colleagues from the startup world, senior officials, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen who have come from India and abroad.

I welcome and greet all of you to the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit. This year's summit is special because it is being held under special circumstances. We have seen how this year has largely been dominated by discussions around energy shocks. The importance of renewable energy in our lives and in our development journey has become even clearer this year. It is also a happy coincidence that the 9th Assembly of the International Solar Alliance is being held alongside this summit. Delegates attending the Fourth Conference on Green Hydrogen are also present here. That means the scale of this year's event is very large. I extend my best wishes to all of you.

Friends,

Over the past few years, the global economy has witnessed unprecedented crises. From the COVID pandemic to the West Asia crisis, the world has faced several major challenges, and the crisis in West Asia is still continuing. But 140 crore Indians feel proud that we have handled these challenges better than many others, and despite these crises, India's growth has remained high. Had India not invested in clean energy and not established new systems in this sector over the past decade, our crisis could have been far more severe than that faced by the rest of the world.

Friends,

This global crisis has delivered a clear message to every country: energy security is directly linked to economic security. And we all know that the future of energy security lies in clean energy. If we continue to remain excessively dependent on fossil fuels, the global economy will continue to face repeated disruptions. Fossil fuel reserves are limited and concentrated in only a few regions. Renewable energy, on the other hand, has unlimited potential, and every region and every country can benefit from it.

Friends,

India's journey in this sector over the past twelve years has been one of promises, passion, and performance. The proof of this is our commitment made at COP-26. At the 2021 Summit, India resolved to achieve 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. We said: We will do it! In our Paris pledge, India had also set the goal of meeting half of its installed power capacity through non-fossil sources. India achieved that target itself in 2025. In other words, we achieved it five years ahead of schedule. Today, more than 50 percent of our installed power capacity is based on non-fossil sources. India is also progressing firmly towards the target of 500 gigawatts. We have already achieved nearly 300 gigawatts. And today, India is among the top three countries in the world in solar and renewable energy. Over the next ten to eleven years, our effort is to add another 500 gigawatts of new non-fossil fuel capacity. This target is somewhat challenging, but I have full confidence in the capabilities of my country. And therefore, I say: We will do it!

Friends,

We want India's innovations and India's experiences to benefit all humanity. This is also our approach towards green energy. India's successes in this field can be useful to many countries around the world. I will explain this through examples.

Friends,

In February 2024, we launched the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. Under this scheme, the target is to install rooftop solar panels on one crore homes. In just the past twenty-four to twenty-five months, more than sixty-five lakh homes have joined this campaign. And as our Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi ji just mentioned, every six days, one lakh new homes become part of this solar movement. The impact of this can also be seen in electricity bills. One study shows that electricity bills for these sixty-five lakh households have fallen by nearly 76 percent. There are lakhs of families whose electricity bills have become zero. There are also many families that are generating surplus electricity and earning income by selling it back to the grid. This scheme can significantly strengthen energy security in many countries, especially in the Global South.

Friends,

India is making solar power a part of the lives of its citizens. Over the past twelve years, we have also tried to connect industries and farms with solar power. More than 44,000 government buildings in India are now connected to solar energy. This is saving nearly ₹700 crore annually. India's farmers are also benefiting greatly from the KUSUM Scheme. Through it, more than 30 lakh farmers have received access to solar-powered irrigation. It is estimated that every farmer benefiting from a solar pump is saving nearly one lakh rupees every year. Let me also give you the example of the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana. Its concept is to generate electricity by installing solar panels on ponds, lakes, and reservoirs. This allows better utilisation of water bodies. Such projects also reduce the costs associated with acquiring land.

Friends,

Our clean energy ecosystem is not limited only to hydro, solar, wind, and nuclear energy. India is moving in mission mode to take a major leap in the field of green hydrogen. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, we have set a target of producing five million tonnes of green hydrogen by the end of this decade. We are also connecting our transport sector with green hydrogen. Just a few months ago, India launched its first Green Hydrogen Train.

Friends,

All of you experts know that merely generating electricity is not enough. It is equally important to distribute it efficiently and deliver it where it is needed. In India, solar and wind energy are generated more abundantly in certain regions. We must ensure that areas where power generation is relatively low also benefit from it, so that homes, farms, and industries there can also run on clean power. That is why Green Energy Corridors are being developed. Under these corridors, a dedicated network of transmission lines and substations is being established. This is making it easier to transfer solar and wind power from places of production to places of demand. And in this effort, the contribution of One Nation, One Power Grid has been immense. Over the years, we have integrated five regional grids into a single national network. Today, the entire country is connected through a power grid operating at a common frequency. To further strengthen this Green Energy Corridor system, we have now moved to the next phase. Recently, India set an investment target of nearly ₹2 lakh crore for this purpose.

Friends,

A major reason behind our success in green energy is also our growing manufacturing capacity. Until a few years ago, we were completely dependent on imports even for the smallest components related to solar energy. A decade ago, our solar module manufacturing capacity was only around 2 gigawatts. Today, it has crossed 200 gigawatts. Solar cell manufacturing capacity has also reached nearly 40 gigawatts. We are now expanding the manufacturing of other components as well. In other words, India's ambitions in green energy are also proof of the success of our Atmanirbhar Bharat mission and the success of the Make in India campaign.

Friends,

India is striving to achieve a great deal within a very short span of time. We cannot stop here. We must connect every government building, every school and college, every hospital, and the entire street-lighting system to solar energy, and we must do so at a rapid pace. I would suggest that healthy competition should be encouraged among states and local bodies, so that those who perform better can be rewarded and others can learn from their success stories.

Friends,

I have a suggestion related to solar power in agriculture as well. We have distributed millions of solar pumps, but we now need to move beyond solar pumps. My vision is that the Annadata should also become an Urjadata - the food provider should become an energy provider. Farmers should install solar panels on unused land. Even the boundaries of fields should not remain unused; solar panels should be installed there as well. We must ensure that this reaches as many villages as possible.

Friends,

This new phase of the solar revolution is not only about adoption; it also depends on innovation. Therefore, I make a special appeal to our startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs: come forward and create models where as many household needs as possible can be met through solar power. We need solutions that make solar power available twenty-four hours a day and in every season. We must move towards a situation where a family can cook food using electricity generated by the solar plant installed on its own rooftop. We need to launch a clean cooking movement. Dependence on imported gas should be reduced as much as possible. We must also create a situation where a larger number of middle-class families have the option of electric vehicles and can charge their scooters, bikes, and cars at home using electricity generated from their own solar systems. This can save middle-class families thousands of rupees every year.

Friends,

We also need products that promote solar power in the dairy sector. Solar-powered equipment should be developed for every activity, from preparing animal feed to harvesting crops and post-harvest operations.

Friends,

None of this will be possible without next-generation innovation. For this, the country needs the necessary hardware. We need indigenous storage solutions. We need to build new battery storage capacity. This is a tremendous opportunity for all of you and for the youth of the country. I urge everyone in the world of research and all investors not to let this opportunity pass by. The solutions you develop in India will serve many countries around the world.

Friends,

India is one of the youngest countries in the world, and every effort in clean energy is creating large numbers of new employment opportunities. Even today, thousands and thousands of people are finding jobs in this sector, and there is tremendous potential for green jobs. These opportunities are being created across different fields, from manufacturing panels and other hardware to installation, servicing, and transportation. In the future, as solar power capacity increases further, just imagine how many more jobs will be created. From kitchen stoves to transportation systems, when everything becomes solar-powered and green-energy-driven, an entirely new industry will emerge.

Friends,

For all of you, for investors across the world, India is opening up enormous opportunities. It is difficult to find elsewhere the kind of demand, scale, and scope that India offers. It is equally difficult to find the kind of political and policy stability that India provides. And we are seeing the results of this. Over the past decade, more than ₹15 lakh crore, that is, 164 billion dollars, has been invested in the renewable energy sector. From the RE-INVEST Summit of 2024 until today, within just two years, investments worth nearly ₹6 lakh crore, that is, more than 63 billion dollars, have come into this sector. It is estimated that by the end of this decade, investment opportunities worth more than ₹20 lakh crore, approximately 220 billion dollars, will be created in this sector. Therefore, a new horizon of opportunities is opening up for all of you in India’s clean energy sector.

Friends,

India has given the world the message of One Earth, One Family, One Future. The same philosophy is reflected in our clean energy journey. This is the thinking behind the International Solar Alliance. Our effort is to ensure that the funding, technology, and expertise required for renewable energy reach every country that needs them. That is why a proposal has been put forward for a 200-million-dollar Africa Solar Facility for Africa.

Friends,

The coming decade is extremely important for our climate goals. And I am confident that everyone present at this summit will play a major role in securing that future. We must connect every country to this mission. Every region must become a participant in this transformation. Only then will we be able to build a clean future, a green future, and a secure future. With these words, I once again extend my heartfelt best wishes to all of you.

Thank you.

****

MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda inaugurates Advanced Radiotherapy Facility at AIIMS Rajkot, reaffirms commitment to quality cancer care for every citizen
Investment of approximately ₹39 crore in advanced cancer care infrastructure at AIIMS Rajkot strengthens tertiary healthcare under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana
Shri Nadda highlights expansion of AIIMS and nationwide cancer screening, with 37.7 crore oral cancer screenings conducted
Shri Praful Pansheriya, MoS Health, Government of Gujarat, welcomes advanced radiotherapy services in Rajkot, expresses gratitude to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for strengthening regional healthcare
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava highlights comprehensive healthcare under National Health Policy 2017, more than 1.8 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and measures to make cancer medicines affordable
Advanced Radiotherapy Facility to serve an estimated 1.54 crore people, with an anticipated annual patient load of 500–700 cases
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, today inaugurated and dedicated to the nation the Advanced Radiotherapy Facility at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Rajkot. Equipped with advanced radiation therapy technologies, the facility marks an important step towards improving access to specialised cancer care for people across Rajkot and the wider Saurashtra region.

With an investment of approximately ₹39 crore, the facility at AIIMS Rajkot has been established under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY). The endeavour reflects the Union Government’s continued efforts to address regional imbalances in the availability of tertiary healthcare services.

Addressing the gathering, Shri J.P. Nadda said that cancer imposes a significant medical, emotional, social and financial burden on patients and their families. He emphasised that timely treatment is critical and that no person should be deprived of quality cancer care because of their location or financial circumstances. The Minister noted that the new facility would particularly benefit people from Saurashtra and Kutch, who previously had to travel to distant cities such as Ahmedabad and Mumbai for specialised treatment. He described the facility as a major step towards improving access to cancer care in the region.

Shri Nadda highlighted the expansion of AIIMS under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, noting that India has progressed from one AIIMS in New Delhi to 18 operational institutions out of 22, significantly strengthening access to specialised tertiary healthcare. He also emphasised the need for seamless linkages across levels of healthcare to ensure patients receive appropriate treatment.

Emphasising prevention and early detection, Shri Nadda highlighted screening initiatives undertaken through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. Since 2018, approximately 44 crore screenings each have been conducted for hypertension and diabetes, while around 37.7 crore people have been screened for oral cancer, with approximately 2.5 lakh cases detected. Breast cancer screening has covered around 17.7 crore women, identifying approximately 95,000 cases, while 9.8 crore women have been screened for cervical cancer, with around one lakh cases detected. He noted that early detection enables patients to access treatment sooner and improves the prospects of recovery.

The Minister also referred to findings cited from a Lancet report indicating that 90 per cent of cancer patients begin treatment within 30 days. He attributed the improvement in timely access to treatment in part to the expansion of financial protection through Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), which has enabled economically vulnerable patients to seek treatment without the same financial constraints. Eligible AB PM-JAY beneficiaries at AIIMS Rajkot will be able to access cancer treatment at no cost, while other patients will receive treatment at subsidised rates to minimise financial burden.

Shri Praful Pansheriya, Minister of State for Health, Family Welfare and Medical Education, Government of Gujarat (Independent Charge), welcomed the inauguration and expressed gratitude to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for strengthening healthcare facilities in the region. He said that the advanced radiotherapy facility would be of considerable benefit to people across Saurashtra.

Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, described the inauguration as an important milestone in AIIMS Rajkot's development and a significant step towards the vision of Viksit Bharat articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. She highlighted the National Health Policy 2017, formulated under the guidance of the Union Health Minister, which envisages comprehensive healthcare encompassing preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative and palliative services, with Universal Health Coverage as a national goal.

Smt. Srivastava noted that the Government has strengthened healthcare infrastructure through more than 1.8 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission. She highlighted AIIMS Rajkot's contribution to advanced treatment and research, cancer screening initiatives under the Swasth Nari Sashakt Parivar campaign and measures to improve the affordability of cancer medicines, including trade margin rationalisation, AMRIT pharmacies, Jan Aushadhi Kendras and basic customs duty exemptions. She also noted the availability of CAR-T cell therapy at affordable rates in India.

Dr. J.S. Titiyal, President, AIIMS Rajkot, described the facility as an important addition to cancer care in the region and commended the Government of India and Gujarat Government for their support, along with the faculty, doctors, nurses and technical staff for establishing the service.

The Advanced Radiotherapy Facility is expected to serve a catchment population of approximately 1.54 crore people across Saurashtra, including Rajkot, Jamnagar, Junagadh, Porbandar, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Morbi, Surendranagar, Gir Somnath, Devbhumi Dwarka and Botad. This benefits the region which largely comprises rural, semi-urban and economically weaker communities.

The facility is equipped with a High Energy Linear Accelerator (LINAC), a Wide Bore CT Simulator and a High Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy Unit. The LINAC enables advanced techniques such as Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy (IMRT), Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (VMAT), Image Guided Radiotherapy (IGRT), Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS), Stereotactic Radiotherapy (SRT) and Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT), supporting precise delivery of radiation with millimetre-level accuracy. The Wide Bore CT Simulator supports three-dimensional treatment planning imaging, while HDR brachytherapy enables targeted internal radiation treatment for gynaecological cancers, head and neck cancers, sarcomas and other tumours.

The Department of Radiation Oncology functions within an integrated cancer care framework, supported by chemotherapy and surgical services, including head and neck, orthopaedic, gynaecological oncology and general surgery. This multidisciplinary arrangement allows patients to receive different forms of cancer treatment within a single institution.

Operational since 29 May 2026, the department has begun providing radiotherapy and chemotherapy services. The facility is expected to initially manage approximately 500–700 cases annually, with a focus on head and neck, gynaecological, breast, bone and soft tissue and other malignancies.

The programme was also attended by Shri Parshottambhai Rupala and Shri Kesridevsinh Jhala, Members of Parliament; Dr. L.N. Dorairajan, Executive Director, AIIMS Rajkot; and other senior officials from the Ministry of Health, faculty members and healthcare professionals.

***

SR

HFW/Union Minister of Health inaugurates Advanced Radiotherapy Facility at AIIMS Rajkot/02 November 2026/1

To address the evolving needs related to the upgradation of grievance redressal framework, the Authority released a consultation paper on the Draft Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, on 7 th May 2026,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI issues the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today issued the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.

To address the evolving needs related to the upgradation of grievance redressal framework, the Authority released a consultation paper on the Draft Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, on 7th May 2026, inviting comments and counter-comments by 12th and 19th June 2026, respectively. A total of 32 comments and 24 counter-comments were received from stakeholders and uploaded to the TRAI website. An online Open House Discussion (OHD) was held on 17th July 2026.

Based on the above consultations, the Authority has finalized the Amendment Regulations. The salient features of the same are given below:

  • The amended regulations shall apply to Internet Service Providers having more than ten thousand subscribers as on the last day of the preceding financial year. The existing alternative criterion based on annual financial turnover exceeding ₹5 crore has been dispensed with thus simplifying the applicability clause.
  • Consumers will now be able to register complaints and appeals, raise service requests, and make service-related queries through the service provider’s mobile application, in addition to the existing channels of the Complaint Centre, website and web portal thus giving wider choice, flexibility and ease to consumers in filing complaint and appeal.
  • Consumer support through Complaint Centres will be available round the clock on all days of the week, instead of the existing 16-hour arrangement. Such support may be provided through human representatives, automated systems, AI agents, other customer-centric technological solutions, or a combination thereof. Human assistance shall be available for at least sixteen hours daily. Technology-based solutions shall function with appropriate human oversight. This will ensure ease and convenience to consumers and gives flexibility to service providers in manning the Complaint Centres.
  • Every service provider shall equip dedicated desks or helplines in their Complaint Centre or Consumer support centres, with personnel or assistive technology capable of receiving calls from persons with disabilities (PwDs). Service providers will ensure that their mobile app, website and portal have accessibility features in accordance with the applicable guidelines or standards on accessibility for Persons with Disabilities issued by the Government of India.
  • The time limit for filing an appeal following disposal of a complaint has been revised from 30 days to 15 days as consumers would normally prefer appeal as soon as possible whereas a longer time allowed unduly increases compliance requirements. Consumers may now file appeals through the service provider’s mobile application, website or portal, in addition to the existing channels of email, post, in person, or through the Consumer Care Number. This will ensure faster resolution of appeal.
  • Also, the Appellate Authority has been made more responsible through the present amendment. It has been mandated that the Appellate Authority shall comprise one or more persons who are regular employees in the management of the service provider and also possess at least five years’ experience. The Appellate Authority shall examine the appeal, take appropriate action for resolution of the grievance, and communicate its final decision within 15 days of receipt of the appeal.
  • The earlier process of resolution of appeal cases through Advisory committee has been dispensed with in order to ensure efficient and time-bound resolution of appeal cases.
  • A new mechanism of “Feedback Survey” has been introduced. Upon resolution or closure of a complaint or appeal, the service provider shall conduct an online feedback survey to assess the consumer’s satisfaction with the resolution. Feedback shall be obtained on a five-point scale, ranging from “Fully Satisfied” (5 points) to “Totally Dissatisfied” (1 point). The service provider shall publish the results of such feedback surveys on its website on a quarterly basis.
  • It has also been mandated that every service provider shall place before its CEO or Board of Directors a quarterly report on the redressal of complaints, appeals and the results of feedback survey. This has been done to ensure suitable review and oversight of the disposal of complaints and appeals by the service providers at the highest level.
  • A new mechanism of Consumer Grievance Redressal Oversight Committee has been introduced. Every Service Provider shall establish a Consumer Grievance Redressal Oversight Committee to oversee and periodically review the functioning of its grievance redressal mechanism. The Committee shall comprise representatives of the Service Provider and at least one representative from each consumer organisation registered with the Authority in the State or Union Territory forming part of the licensed service area.  Service Providers will form such committee taking representation mandatorily from those states and union territories in which their subscriber base is above ten thousand. The Committee shall meet at least once every year to review the grievance redressal mechanism.
  • The amendment introduces a new mechanism of Regulatory Review. The Authority may conduct periodic review of the functioning of the Grievance Redressal Mechanism of the service providers by: -
    • audit and inspection of the records of the service provider,
    • audit and analysis of Quarterly Performance Reports submitted by the service provider,
    • review based on consumer feedback.
  • The amendment introduces the provision of financial disincentives in cases of disposal of complaint or appeal in contravention of the provisions of these regulations observed during the audit, inspection, analysis or review.
  • The provision of financial disincentives has also been introduced for non-submission/ delayed submission of the Quarterly Performance Report.

The amendments strengthen the consumer grievance redressal framework through enhanced digital access available to consumers, round the clock Complaint Centre support, improved accessibility for Persons with Disabilities and faster filing and disposal of complaints and appeals. The Appellate mechanism has been strengthened. Structured consumer feedback surveys, grievance redressal oversight committees, enhanced regulatory review, and financial disincentives for specified instances of non-compliance have been introduced to ensure appropriate supervision and compliance enforcement.

Full text of the Regulation is available on the TRAI's website www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification/information Advisor (Consumer Affairs), TRAI, may be contacted at email ID: adv.ca@trai.gov.in or Telephone +91-11- 26769605.

***

PSF/ ARJ

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
DoPPW Accelerates Digital Empowerment of Pensioners Through Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5
DoPPW, SBI Join Hands to Facilitate Hassle-Free Digital Life Certificates for Pensioners
Over Two Crore Digital Life Certificates Targeted Under Nationwide DLC Campaign 5
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, organised a Mega Camp in collaboration with the State Bank of India (SBI) at the NDCC Convention Centre, New Delhi, on 2 November 2026, as part of the Nationwide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5. The camp witnessed enthusiastic participation from pensioners and senior citizens and aimed to facilitate the submission of Digital Life Certificates through technology-driven, accessible and pensioner-friendly services.

Addressing the gathering, the Secretary, DoPPW, Ms Nivedita Shukla Verma highlighted that digital empowerment of pensioners is an important component of the Government’s commitment to Ease of Living. The Secretary emphasised that technological advancements, particularly face authentication, have transformed the process of submitting life certificates by enabling pensioners to generate their Digital Life Certificates independently through smartphones, without the need to visit banks or other offices.

The Secretary also appreciated SBI’s significant contribution to the initiative, noting that the Bank had facilitated approximately 25 lakh Digital Life Certificates during the previous year’s campaign.

As part of the current campaign, SBI is conducting special DLC camps across 115 cities and extending assistance through its branches and dedicated support teams. The Bank has also undertaken initiatives to expand coverage among its pensioners and facilitate access to digital services, including special arrangements at branches with a substantial pensioner population.

Addressing the gathering Joint Secretary DoPPW Sh Dhrubajyoti Sengupta  urged all pensioners to make use of the facilities available under the campaign and encourage fellow pensioners to adopt digital services, thereby contributing to a more accessible, transparent and citizen-centric pension delivery system.

item.description: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship PM-SETU to strengthen North-East's skilling ecosystem through industry-led ITI transformation; Tourism and Hospitality identified as key sectors for global employment opportunities MoU exchanged between MSDE and Government of Assam for setting up of SIIC; Numaligarh Refinery and Oil India Limited clusters declared under PM-SETU Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised a programme on Skilling for…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
PM-SETU to strengthen North-East's skilling ecosystem through industry-led ITI transformation; Tourism and Hospitality identified as key sectors for global employment opportunities
MoU exchanged between MSDE and Government of Assam for setting up of SIIC; Numaligarh Refinery and Oil India Limited clusters declared under PM-SETU
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised a programme on Skilling for International Mobility & PM-SETU', with a special focus on the Tourism and Hospitality sector in Guwahati today.

The programme brought together senior representatives of the Central and Assam Governments, industry stakeholders and the skilling ecosystem to deliberate on strengthening the North-Eastern Region's skilling infrastructure, expanding international employment opportunities for its youth and fostering industry-led transformation of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU).

The programme highlighted the immense potential of the North-Eastern Region in tourism and hospitality, particularly in the context of the growing demand for skilled professionals in domestic and international markets. Discussions focused on aligning skill development programmes with emerging industry requirements, international standards and opportunities for global workforce mobility.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, highlighted the importance of aligning India's skilling architecture with the changing requirements of industry and the global economy.

He emphasised that initiatives such as PM-SETU are aimed at bringing industry closer to skill development and training, ensuring that ITIs evolve into modern, demand-driven institutions capable of preparing young people for emerging opportunities.

"India's strength lies in the aspirations and capabilities of its youth. Through PM-SETU, we are working towards transforming our ITIs into modern, industry-responsive institutions that equip young people with skills relevant to the future of work. The North-Eastern Region has enormous potential, particularly in tourism and hospitality, and our endeavour is to ensure that its youth are not only prepared for opportunities within the country but are also equipped to participate confidently in the global workforce."

Shri Biswajit Daimary, Minister for Skills, Employment and Entrepreneurship, Sports and Youth Welfare, Handloom, Textile and Sericulture, and Indigenous and Tribal Faith and Culture, Government of Assam, in his special remarks, highlighted the importance of equipping the youth of Assam with industry-relevant skills and creating pathways to employment opportunities both within India and internationally.

"Assam and the entire North-Eastern Region have tremendous potential in sectors such as tourism and hospitality. Our priority is to ensure that the youth of the region are equipped with the right skills, exposure and opportunities to participate in the emerging global economy. Through stronger collaboration between the Central Government, the State Government and industry, we can build a robust skilling ecosystem that translates the aspirations of our youth into meaningful employment and entrepreneurship opportunities."

Smt. Manasi Sahay Thakur, IAS, Joint Secretary, MSDE, set the context for the programme and highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional and industry partnerships to create a future-ready workforce. She emphasised the need to connect the region's youth with emerging employment opportunities through demand-driven skilling and stronger institutional infrastructure.

CEO of Tourism and Hospitality Skill Council (THSC), spoke about the potential of tourism and hospitality skilling in the North-Eastern Region and the opportunities emerging from the sector's growth. He highlighted the importance of developing industry-relevant competencies to enhance the employability of youth and prepare them for opportunities in the global hospitality ecosystem.

The programme featured a dedicated session on PM-SETU, highlighting opportunities for strengthening the skilling ecosystem in the North-Eastern Region through industry-responsive ITI transformation.

As part of the strategic partnerships announced during the programme, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was exchanged between the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Government of Assam for setting up of SIIC.

Letters of Intent (LoIs) were signed for two ITI clusters i.e Jorhat and Tinsukhia, supported by Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) and Oil India Limited (OIL), respectively, under the PM-SETU scheme. This marks a significant milestone in strengthening industry participation and fostering industry-led transformation of the vocational education and training ecosystem in the region.

The programme also deliberated on international mobility and WorldSkills as avenues for expanding opportunities for young people from the North-Eastern Region.

The Government of Assam also presented its CM FLIGHT Scheme and the vision for a Global Skill Center, highlighting the State's efforts towards strengthening skill development and connecting its workforce with emerging opportunities.

 

Attended the Northeast Tourism & Hospitality Skill Conclave 2026 in Guwahati, alongside Hon’ble Minister Sh @BiswajitDaimar5. Led by @MSDESkillIndia, with support from @NSDCIndia and the @skillthsc, the Conclave focused on strengthening tourism-led skilling, industry partnerships and international mobility opportunities for the youth of the North-East. The occasion also witnessed the exchange of an MoU between MSDE and the Government of Assam for establishing a Skill India International Centre (SIIC), and the exchange of LoIs of PM-SETU clusters with Numaligarh Refinery Limited and Oil India Limited. These partnerships aim to strengthen industry-aligned skilling infrastructure, create opportunities, and equip the youth of the North-East with skills for emerging domestic and international markets!

— Jayant Singh (@jayantrld) November 2, 2026

The campaign also focused on cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Mines
Ministry of Mines Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in E-Waste Management, Cleanliness and Governance
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Mines, along with its attached and subordinate offices, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and autonomous bodies, has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, with a particular focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste. The campaign also focused on cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending references, resolution of public grievances and improving administrative efficiency, reaffirming the Ministry's commitment to sustainability and good governance.

A key highlight of Special Campaign 6 was the extensive drive for the collection and disposal of e-waste. During the campaign, a total of 134.92 tonnes of e-waste had been collected/disposed across 96 locations, generating revenue of approx ₹ 1.2 crore. The initiative covered offices of the Ministry of Mines / field offices as well as other government offices, promoting the responsible disposal of electronic waste, resource recovery and environmentally sustainable practices.

During the campaign period, 465 cleanliness campaign were conducted across the Ministry and its organizations. The campaign generated total revenue of approximately 6.19 crore from disposal of scrap and e-waste, and freed approximately 47881 square feet of office space. These efforts contributed to improved workplace conditions, better utilization of office space and the promotion of a culture of cleanliness and sustainability.

Under the record management initiative, 13067 physical files were reviewed, of which 9470 were weeded out. In the electronic records category, 3270 e-files were reviewed and 1812 were closed. Overall 11282 files were weeded out or closed, contributing to streamlined record management and improved administrative efficiency.

The Ministry also achieved its targets in disposing the Public Grievances/ Public Grievances appeals, references received from Members of Parliament, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO), the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) and State Governments reference. In addition, 7 rules/processes were simplified during the campaign to promote ease of governance and administrative efficiency.

Several innovative best practices were undertaken by the Ministry's organisations to promote environmental sustainability and resource conservation. Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) inaugurated a rainwater harvesting facility at Khetri Copper Complex, Rajasthan, and organised a tree plantation drive at Indian Copper Complex, Jharkhand, under the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam initiative. NALCO promoted the use of biodegradable bags in township and undertook plantation drives under its One Employee – One Green initiative. The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) developed a green park on barren land in Ranchi. Other initiatives included innovative waste-to-wealth activities through the reuse of scrap materials, including the creation of decorative plants and toolkits from discarded materials, demonstrating the potential of recycling and creative reuse.

Through the dedicated efforts of its offices and organisations, the Ministry of Mines has made significant progress in promoting cleanliness, sustainable waste management, better record management and citizen-centric governance. The achievements of Special Campaign 6 reflect the Ministry’s continued commitment to environmental sustainability, efficient use of resources and the adoption of good administrative practices.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
HQ IDS-CENJOWS Seminar on Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare Commences in New Delhi
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi

A two-day seminar on “Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare”, organised by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS) under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), commenced in New Delhi on November 02, 2026. The seminar aims to deliberate on the emerging security challenges arising from the convergence of cyber operations, Artificial Intelligence (AI), information influence and human cognition, with particular focus on India's evolving threat landscape.

The sessions focused on the cyber-enabled cognitive battlefield and India's evolving threat landscape, the anatomy of influence operations, including the actors, vectors and narratives shaping the information environment. The deliberations also addressed the targeting of military personnel, veterans and their families, alongside the growing convergence of cyber technologies, Artificial Intelligence and digital manipulation. The discussions highlighted the need for a comprehensive understanding of emerging threats, extending beyond their technological dimensions to encompass their psychological, institutional and societal implications.

The seminar brings together senior military leaders, government officials, strategic affairs experts, diplomats, representatives from academia, technology specialists and media representatives, providing a multidisciplinary platform for deliberations on the challenges and implications of cyber-enabled cognitive warfare.

The inaugural session was attended by Rear Admiral Sanjay Sachdeva, Director General, Defence Cyber Agency, Major General Ashok Kumar (Retd), Director General, CENJOWS, Shri Navin Kumar Singh, National Cyber Security Coordinator, Vice Admiral A N Pramod,  Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff, and Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
1st International Maize Conference 2026 Calls for Higher Productivity, Innovative Breeding and Farmer-Centric Research
Research and extension must translate into higher farm profitability and improved livelihoods: Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE  
Dr. Jat advocates Systems-Science Approach to Bridge Yield Gaps and Strategically Target Maize Across Seasons Without Compromising Oilseeds and Pulses
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi

The 1st International Maize Conference themed “Maize Revolution for Food, Feed, Fodder, Fuel and Sustainability in the Changing World,” (M4FS) commenced at the JD Convention Centre, Hyderabad today, bringing together scientists, policymakers, agricultural institutions and industry stakeholders to discuss strategies for advancing maize research, productivity and value-chain development.

The conference highlighted high-yielding varieties and hybrids, improved nutritional quality, efficient resource utilisation, mechanisation, robust seed systems and maize’s growing role in food, feed, fodder and energy security.

Addressing the conference Secretary, DARE and DG ICAR Dr. M. L. Jat, congratulated the maize research community on India’s maize production reaching approximately 55 million tonnes, accompanied by substantial productivity gains over the past decade. He called for increasing production to 75 million tonnes over the next decade, alongside a further 1.5-fold increase in productivity through technological innovation, improved crop management and efficient resource utilisation.

Emphasising an expansion of the traditional 4F vision—Food, Feed, Fodder and Fuel—to 5F by placing Farmers at the centre, Dr. Jat stressed that research and extension must translate into higher farm profitability and improved livelihoods. He advocated a systems-science approach to bridging yield gaps, particularly those arising from crop management, and strategic targeting of maize across seasons and agroecological zones without compromising other important crops, particularly oilseeds and pulses. He also underscored the need for affordable, quality seed, especially public-sector hybrids, supported by a robust seed system.

Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR, described maize as a model crop for food, nutritional and energy security. Acknowledging progress in maize research and extension over the past five years, including the development of 329 maize hybrids, he called for strengthening the All India Coordinated Research Project on Maize (AICRP on Maize). He emphasised breeding for higher yields, improved nutritional quality and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, alongside input-use efficiency, mechanisation, capacity development and stronger public-sector hybrid seed production. He also highlighted the need for collaboration among research institutions, universities and industry to realise maize’s potential as an ethanol feedstock.

Padma Shri Dr. S. Vasal, eminent maize scientist and a World Food Laurete associated with CIMMYT, advocated simple, cost-effective breeding approaches to accelerate the development of improved varieties and hybrids suited to farmers’ needs.

Padma Bhushan Dr. R. S. Paroda, former Secretary, DARE, and Director General, ICAR, and Chief Guest, stressed the importance of aligning research priorities with the evolving needs of agriculture and allied sectors. He called for greater use of advanced breeding techniques, systematic germplasm conservation and utilisation, stronger maize value chains, and effective aflatoxin management to ensure maize safety and quality for food and feed.

Earlier, Dr. H. S. Jat, President, Maize Technologists Association of India (MTAI), welcomed the dignitaries and highlighted maize’s strategic importance in India’s agricultural transformation. He called for stronger collaboration among research institutions, agricultural universities, policymakers and industry to address emerging challenges.

Several scientific publications were released during the programme, and awards were presented to eminent scientists and researchers in recognition of their contributions to maize research and development.

The conference underscored the importance of collaborative, farmer-centric research to bridge yield gaps, improve seed access, strengthen breeding programmes, enhance nutritional quality and develop sustainable maize value chains. Being held from 2–4 November, 2026 in Hyderabad, the conference provides a platform for national and international experts to shape a roadmap for a productive, profitable and sustainable maize sector in India.

To mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the ‘Iron Man of India’, Shri Satish Kumar, Chairman & CEO of the Railway…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Observes Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Railway Board Chairman & CEO Administers Unity Pledge and Felicitates Safai Mitras at Rail Bhawan
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Railways observed Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and organised activities under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 – Special Campaign 6.0 at Rail Bhawan, New Delhi, on 30 October 2026.

To mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the ‘Iron Man of India’, Shri Satish Kumar, Chairman & CEO of the Railway Board, administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Pledge at Vichar (Conference Hall), Rail Bhawan. Members of the Railway Board, Directors General, senior officers and staff of the Ministry of Railways were present on the occasion.

Rashtriya Ekta Diwas is observed every year on 31st October to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He played a pivotal role in the integration of the princely states into the Union of India and made an enduring contribution towards strengthening the unity and integrity of the nation.

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 – Special Campaign 6.0, various activities were organised at Rail Bhawan to promote cleanliness, hygiene and sanitation. Health check-up camps were organised for Safai Mitras, recognising the importance of their health and well-being.

On the occasion, Chairman & CEO, Railway Board, felicitated Safai Mitras in recognition of their dedicated services and contribution towards maintaining cleanliness at Rail Bhawan. The felicitation acknowledged their hard work and commitment to maintaining cleanliness and upholding the spirit of Swachhata in Indian Railways.

The event recognised the contributions of day-to-day maintenance staff, with senior members of the Railway Board felicitating employees for their dedication and hard work. The felicitation included staff from housekeeping and horticulture, reflecting the deep sense of unity within the Rail family and the spirit of working together as One Family. The occasion also coincided with the felicitation of 11 employees who retired after dedicating a significant part of their lives to the service of Indian Railways and the people of the country.

The celebrations reinforced the message of keeping offices clean and green while fostering a culture of teamwork, mutual respect and collective responsibility. It highlighted the spirit of Indian Railways as One Family, working together as One Team to serve the people of India.

As India moves forward towards the vision of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat, Indian Railways continues to play a vital role in strengthening the unity and integration of the nation. As the country's national transporter, connecting every part of India and carrying millions of passengers to their destinations every day, Indian Railways remains a symbol of national unity, bringing people, regions and states closer together.
