item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to the people of Keralam on Keralappiravi
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has extended greetings to the people of Keralam on the occasion of Keralappiravi, today. Shri Modi said that this special day celebrates the vibrant traditions and extraordinary spirit of Keralam. Blessed with abundant natural beauty and a rich cultural heritage, the state has always held a cherished place in the nation's history.

"The greatest strength of Kerala lies in its people, whose dedication and commitment to excellence have earned admiration far beyond India's shores. Their achievements in diverse fields, including healthcare, education, entrepreneurship and science, have made the nation proud", Shri Modi remarked.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

Keralappiravi greetings to my sisters and brothers of Keralam!

This special day celebrates the vibrant traditions and extraordinary spirit of Keralam. Blessed with abundant natural beauty and a rich cultural heritage, the state has always occupied a cherished place in our nation’s history.

Keralam’s greatest strength lies in its people, whose dedication and commitment to excellence have earned admiration far beyond India’s shores. The achievements of the people of Keralam in several areas like healthcare, education, entrepreneurship, science and several other fields have made the nation proud.

I hope the coming years bring new opportunities, greater prosperity and continued progress to every person of Keralam.

കേരളത്തിലെ എന്റെ സഹോദരീസഹോദരന്മാർക്ക് കേരളപ്പപ്പിറവി ആശംസകൾ!

കേരളത്തിന്റെ സജീവമായ പാരമ്പര്യങ്ങളെയും അസാധാരണമായ ആത്മവീര്യത്തെയും ആഘോഷിക്കുന്ന വിശേഷ ദിനമാണിത്. സമൃദ്ധമായ പ്രകൃതിസൗന്ദര്യവും സമ്പന്നമായ സാംസ്കാരിക പൈതൃകവും അനുഗ്രഹിച്ച ഈ സംസ്ഥാനത്തിന്, എന്നും നമ്മുടെ രാജ്യത്തിന്റെ ചരിത്രത്തിൽ പ്രിയപ്പെട്ട ഒരു സ്ഥാനമുണ്ട്.

കേരളത്തിന്റെ ഏറ്റവും വലിയ കരുത്ത് അവിടുത്തെ ജനങ്ങളാണ്. അവരുടെ സമർപ്പണബോധവും മികവിനോടുള്ള പ്രതിബദ്ധതയും ഇന്ത്യയുടെ അതിരുകൾക്കപ്പുറത്തും ഏറെ പ്രശംസ പിടിച്ചുപറ്റിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. ആരോഗ്യം, വിദ്യാഭ്യാസം, സംരംഭകത്വം, ശാസ്ത്രം തുടങ്ങി നിരവധി മേഖലകളിൽ മലയാളി കൈവരിച്ച നേട്ടങ്ങൾ രാജ്യത്തിന് എന്നും അഭിമാനകരമാണ്.

വരും വർഷങ്ങൾ കേരളത്തിലെ ഓരോ വ്യക്തിക്കും പുതിയ അവസരങ്ങളും കൂടുതൽ ഐശ്വര്യവും തുടർച്ചയായ പുരോഗതിയും കൊണ്ടുവരട്ടെയെന്ന് ഞാൻ ആശംസിക്കുന്നു.


Keralappiravi greetings to my sisters and brothers of Keralam! This special day celebrates the vibrant traditions and extraordinary spirit of Keralam. Blessed with abundant natural beauty and a rich cultural heritage, the state has always occupied a cherished place in our nation’s history. Keralam’s greatest strength lies in its people, whose dedication and commitment to excellence have earned admiration far beyond India’s shores. The achievements of the people of Keralam in several areas like healthcare, education, entrepreneurship, science and several other fields have made the nation proud. I hope the coming years bring new opportunities, greater prosperity and continued progress to every person of Keralam. കേരളത്തിലെ എന്റെ സഹോദരീസഹോദരന്മാർക്ക് കേരളപ്പപ്പിറവി ആശംസകൾ! കേരളത്തിന്റെ സജീവമായ പാരമ്പര്യങ്ങളെയും അസാധാരണമായ ആത്മവീര്യത്തെയും ആഘോഷിക്കുന്ന വിശേഷ ദിനമാണിത്. സമൃദ്ധമായ പ്രകൃതിസൗന്ദര്യവും സമ്പന്നമായ സാംസ്കാരിക പൈതൃകവും അനുഗ്രഹിച്ച ഈ സംസ്ഥാനത്തിന്, എന്നും നമ്മുടെ രാജ്യത്തിന്റെ ചരിത്രത്തിൽ പ്രിയപ്പെട്ട ഒരു സ്ഥാനമുണ്ട്. കേരളത്തിന്റെ ഏറ്റവും വലിയ കരുത്ത് അവിടുത്തെ ജനങ്ങളാണ്. അവരുടെ സമർപ്പണബോധവും മികവിനോടുള്ള പ്രതിബദ്ധതയും ഇന്ത്യയുടെ അതിരുകൾക്കപ്പുറത്തും ഏറെ പ്രശംസ പിടിച്ചുപറ്റിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. ആരോഗ്യം, വിദ്യാഭ്യാസം, സംരംഭകത്വം, ശാസ്ത്രം തുടങ്ങി നിരവധി മേഖലകളിൽ മലയാളി കൈവരിച്ച നേട്ടങ്ങൾ രാജ്യത്തിന് എന്നും അഭിമാനകരമാണ്. വരും വർഷങ്ങൾ കേരളത്തിലെ ഓരോ വ്യക്തിക്കും പുതിയ അവസരങ്ങളും കൂടുതൽ ഐശ്വര്യവും തുടർച്ചയായ പുരോഗതിയും കൊണ്ടുവരട്ടെയെന്ന് ഞാൻ ആശംസിക്കുന്നു.

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 1, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to the people of Haryana on State foundation day
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has extended greetings to the people of Haryana on the occasion of the State Foundation Day, today. Shri Modi said that Haryana, adorned with a glorious history, remarkable valour and rich cultural heritage, is a source of pride for the nation. Its folk traditions and vibrant rural culture have always enriched India's cultural heritage.

"The people of Haryana have demonstrated their talent and determination through hard work and dedication in diverse fields, including agriculture, sports, defence services, industry, education and startups. The state's athletes are enhancing the pride of the Tricolour, while its farmers are strengthening the country's food security", Shri Modi remarked.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

हरियाणा दिवस की राज्य के मेरे सभी परिवारजनों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई और शुभकामनाएं!

गौरवशाली इतिहास, अद्भुत पराक्रम और समृद्ध संस्कृति से सुसज्जित हमारा यह प्रदेश देश की शान है। यहां की लोक परंपराओं और जीवंत ग्रामीण संस्कृति ने राष्ट्र की सांस्कृतिक धरोहर को हमेशा समृद्ध किया है।

हरियाणा के लोगों ने अपने परिश्रम और समर्पण से कृषि, खेल और रक्षा सेवाओं से लेकर उद्योग, शिक्षा और स्टार्टअप तक अपनी प्रतिभा और संकल्प का लोहा मनवाया है। यहां के खिलाड़ी तिरंगे का मान बढ़ा रहे हैं, तो अन्नदाता देश की खाद्य सुरक्षा को मजबूती दे रहे हैं। 

मैं कामना करता हूं कि यह विशेष अवसर यहां के सभी लोगों के जीवन में खुशहाली लेकर आए।

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to the people of Chhattisgarh on State foundation day
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 12:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has extended greetings to the people of Chhattisgarh on the occasion of the State Foundation Day, today. Shri Modi said that Chhattisgarh is renowned for its tribal culture, natural wealth and unique folk traditions. The state's rich archaeological heritage is also a distinctive part of its identity. He added that the environment enriched by its vibrant folk culture embodies a wonderful sense of belonging that attracts everyone.

"It is heartening to see Chhattisgarh moving ahead on the path of development with renewed momentum while eradicating the roots of Naxalism. With the participation of the state's talented and hardworking people, Chhattisgarh will continue to make significant contributions to the prosperity of the nation", Shri Modi remarked.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

छत्तीसगढ़ के सभी निवासियों को राज्य के स्थापना दिवस की अनेकानेक शुभकामनाएं!

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to the people of Madhya Pradesh on State foundation day
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 12:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has extended greetings to all the people of Madhya Pradesh on the occasion of the State Foundation Day, today. Shri Modi said that Madhya Pradesh is a land of glorious heritage, rich culture and stunning natural beauty and it's world-renowned heritage sites further enrich the state's historical identity.

"The people of Madhya Pradesh have made remarkable contributions in every field through their talent and enterprise. From agriculture, industry, tourism, education and infrastructure to innovation, the state is achieving new milestones", Shri Modi remarked.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Hon’ble Union Minister, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, to visit Gangtok and Mangan Districts, Sikkim on 2nd November 2026
Projects worth Rs. 375 Lakh to be inaugurated under PMMSY
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 11:46AM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh Alias Lalan Singh will visit Gangtok and Mangan districts, Sikkim during 2nd-3rd November 2026. During the visit, the Hon’ble Union Minister will review fisheries development initiatives, launch the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for organic fish farming, inaugurate projects worth Rs.375 Lakh under PMMSY and interact with fish farmers. The visit is in line with the structured mechanism for periodic visits of Union Ministers to the Northeastern Region, put in place under the guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister to support effective implementation of development programmes and obtain field-level feedback. The union minister will distribute Kisan Credit Cards to fish farmers and cheques to fish farmers under Mukhya Mantri Matsya Uthpadhan Yojana (MMMUY).

The Hon’ble Union Minister will also interact with the Fish Farmers’ Cooperative Society during the visit to the Live Fish Vending Centre at Mangshila to understand field-level requirements in fish marketing and cooperative activities, review fisheries development and PMMSY interventions at DAC, Mangan, and take feedback from fisheries stakeholders on implementation issues. These engagements will help assess fisheries development needs in Sikkim, particularly in remote and geographically challenging areas.

The visit will also see participation of senior officers of the Government of Sikkim, District Administration, Mangan, along with representatives of Departments of Fisheries, GoI, relevant line Ministries, Fisheries ICAR institutes, Fish farmers, fisheries cooperative societies and fisheries farmer producer organization

The Northeastern Region, endowed with abundant freshwater resources, diverse aquatic ecosystems and rich biodiversity, holds significant potential for the development of sustainable and high-value fisheries and aquaculture. Leveraging these inherent advantages through certification, robust traceability, aggregation, processing and value addition, together with alignment to global export market requirements, can strengthen export readiness and position the region as a hub for certified organic and premium fishery products. This will facilitate access to domestic and overseas markets, improve value realisation for fish farmers and strengthen livelihoods across the fisheries value chain.

The Government has adopted a cluster-based approach for integrated development of the fisheries value chain, bringing together production, processing, value addition and marketing within identified geographical areas. Under PMMSY, 34 fisheries production and processing clusters have been notified across the country, including organic fisheries clusters in Sikkim and Meghalaya. The approach provides a framework for aggregation, value addition and stronger market linkages, enabling differentiated and high-value fishery products to secure better market access and value realisation for fish farmer.

The visit is expected to provide further impetus to the development of a modern, sustainable and market-oriented fisheries ecosystem in Sikkim and the wider Northeastern Region. By bringing together infrastructure development, organic fisheries, certification and traceability, value addition and stronger market linkages, the initiatives will contribute to higher incomes for fish farmers, enhanced livelihood opportunities and improved access to premium domestic and international markets.

                                                        ******

JP 

(Release ID: 2331082)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal to Recognize Outstanding Achievements in Coal and Lignite Mining at Star Rating Awards in Raipur on 2nd November
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 10:52AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal will recognise and celebrate exemplary achievements in coal and lignite mining at the Star Rating Awards Ceremony on 2 November 2026 in Raipur, Chhattisgarh. The awards will honour high-performing mines for their achievements across key parameters, including operational efficiency, environmental sustainability, occupational health and safety, technological advancement and responsible resource management.

The ceremony will be graced by the Union Minister of Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, as the Chief Guest. The Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, will attend as the Guest of Honour, while the Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, will be the Special Guest. Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, and Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, will also attend the ceremony, along with senior officials of the Ministry, CMDs of coal and lignite PSUs, industry stakeholders and representatives of State Governments.

The Star Rating Policy for Coal Mines provides a structured framework for assessing the performance of coal and lignite mines against a comprehensive set of parameters. These include operational efficiency, adoption of technology, occupational health and safety, environmental management, sustainable development, rehabilitation and resettlement, and initiatives for the welfare of local communities. Mines are awarded ratings ranging from five stars to no star following assessment and validation by reviewers appointed by the Coal Controller’s Organisation. Mines achieving the highest star ratings for the assessment year 2024–25 will be felicitated at the ceremony.

The awards reflect the Government’s continued emphasis on promoting scientific, safe, efficient and environmentally responsible mining practices, while strengthening the coal sector’s contribution to the country’s energy security and economic growth.

Through a transparent and performance-oriented assessment mechanism, the Star Rating Policy encourages mining companies to continuously improve operational standards, strengthen environmental safeguards and adopt best practices throughout the mining lifecycle. The awards also promote healthy competition among mining operators and encourage the wider adoption of innovative and sustainable practices across the sector.

The ceremony will serve as a platform to acknowledge mines that have demonstrated excellence in responsible mining, efficient resource utilisation, environmental stewardship and sustainable development.

Key Highlights 1. Coal Imports by…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Coal Imports Decline by 5.83% in August 2026, Reflecting Reduced Import Dependence
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 10:52AM by PIB Delhi

India’s total coal imports declined by 5.83% in August 2026, falling to 104.57 million tonnes (MT) from 111.05 MT in August 2025, a reduction of 6.48 MT. The decline reflects the continued efforts of the Ministry of Coal to enhance domestic coal production, improve availability and strengthen the supply chain, with a view to reducing the country’s dependence on imported coal.

Key Highlights

1. Coal Imports by the Power Sector Decline by 6.39%

Coal imports by power plants decreased by 6.39%, from 22.77 MT in August 2025 to 21.32 MT in August 2026. The decline is consistent with efforts to improve domestic coal availability and reduce dependence on imported coal for blending at domestic coal-based power plants.

2. Imports by Imported Coal-Based Power Plants Register a Marginal Increase

Coal imports by imported coal-based (ICB) power plants increased marginally by 0.98%, from 18.13 MT in August 2025 to 18.31 MT in August 2026. These plants are designed to operate primarily on imported coal.

3. Imports for Blending at Domestic Coal-Based Power Plants Decline by 35.23%

Coal imports for blending at domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants declined by 35.23%, from 4.64 MT in August 2025 to 3.00 MT in August 2026. This reduction indicates lower import requirements for blending and is consistent with efforts to improve the availability of domestic coal for power generation.

4. Share of Imports in Total Coal Consumption Declines

The share of imported coal in India’s total coal consumption decreased from 21.20% in August 2025 to 19.30% in August 2026, a decline of 1.90 percentage points. This reflects a reduction in the country’s reliance on imported coal during the month.

5. Coking Coal Imports Decline by 4.18%

Coking coal imports decreased by 4.18%, from 28.49 MT in August 2025 to 27.30 MT in August 2026. Coking coal is an important input for the steel industry, and domestic availability remains constrained by the quality and characteristics of indigenous reserves. Import requirements in this category are therefore influenced by the specific raw material needs of the steel sector.

Sustained Efforts to Strengthen Domestic Coal Supply

The Ministry continues to focus on increasing domestic coal production and offtake, strengthening First Mile Connectivity (FMC), improving coal evacuation infrastructure and closely monitoring coal stock levels at thermal power plants.

Coordinated efforts with the Ministry of Railways, Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries are aimed at ensuring the timely and adequate supply of coal to power utilities. These measures are intended to improve the reliability of domestic coal supplies, reduce avoidable import dependence and support uninterrupted power generation across the country.

The decline in overall coal imports, particularly imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants, underscores the importance of strengthening domestic production, transportation and supply-chain infrastructure. At the same time, imports by imported coal-based power plants and the steel sector continue to reflect their specific fuel and raw material requirements.

Ministry of Coal remains committed to further enhancing domestic coal production, improving evacuation capacity, strengthening supply-chain efficiency and promoting appropriate coal quality management to reduce import dependence wherever feasible, while ensuring reliable coal availability for the country’s power and industrial sectors.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIP TRISHUL CALLS AT SOUDA BAY, GREECE
Posted On: 01 NOV 2026 10:30AM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Trishul called at Souda Bay, Greece, on 31 Oct 2026, during her ongoing deployment to the Mediterranean Sea.

During the port call, the ship’s crew will participate in a range of activities to further maritime cooperation between the Indian Navy and the Hellenic Navy. These include interactions with senior functionaries of the Hellenic Navy and the Indian Embassy in Athens, professional discussions, cross-deck visits, cultural exchanges and familiarisation with facilities at Naval Support Activity (NSA) Souda Bay and the NATO Maritime Interdiction Operational Training Centre (NMIOTC).

 The crew will also pay homage at the Souda Bay War Cemetery. The ship will remain open to visitors during the port call.

The visit will further consolidate maritime cooperation and strengthen professional linkages between the Indian Navy and the Hellenic Navy.

It concluded today with a renewed commitment to institutionalise…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and its organisations successfully conclude Special Campaign 6
Disposal of Scrap and E-waste results in freeing up 32,854 sq. ft. of space; Revenue worth over Rs. 64.18 lakhs generated
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 11:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), along with its organisations, has successfully undertaken the Special Campaign 6. It concluded today with a renewed commitment to institutionalise Swachhata and minimising pendency within the Ministry and its offices across the country.  A key area of focus during this year’s Campaign has been the ‘Effective collection, segregation and disposal of E-waste’, as per guidelines issued by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) on 13.08.2026. The Campaign was undertaken across all 132 identified locations of the Ministry including its Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Bodies, etc.

Special emphasis was laid on disposal of E-waste following due process, as per the provisions contained in the guidelines and SOP issued by DARPG. The activities underscored the importance of environmentally responsible waste management and sustainable administrative practices. The disposal of e-waste including scrap and redundant items resulted in the generation of revenue amounting to Rs. 64,18,158/-  and reclamation of 32,854 sq. ft. of valuable office space.

Earlier, during the implementation phase, the Secretary (MoEFCC) undertook a comprehensive inspection of the premises of the Ministry at Indira Paryavaran Bhavan, New Delhi to review the status of collection and segregation of E-waste, scrap and redundant items stored. Emphasizing the importance of environmentally sound and responsible E-waste and other waste management, the Secretary directed that all segregated items be disposed of in a safe and scientific manner through CPCB registered E-waste recyclers, refurbishers and producers, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines.

Secretary, MoEFCC, visited the Ministry premises to review the progress of #SpecialCampaign6. The review covered key activities related to cleanliness, record management and e-waste disposal as part of the ongoing campaign. https://t.co/VF8t7zfVqt

— MoEF&CC (@moefcc) October 26, 2026

Under various Parameters of Special Campaign 6, 100 per cent achievement has been recorded in the Cleanliness Campaign covering all 132 identified locations. The Ministry also achieved 100 per cent disposal of State Government References, Public Grievance Appeals, PMO References along with the prescribed targets for the review of Physical Files and E-files. The details of targets vis-a-vis achievement against all the Parameters under Special Campaign 6 are summarised below:-

— MoEF&CC (@moefcc) October 31, 2026

The Special Campaign on Swachhata was launched in 2021 at the behest of the DARPG. Since its inception, the Campaign has evolved into a sustained institutional exercise aimed not only at promoting cleanliness and maintaining a hygienic working environment in Government Offices but also disposing of the pending matters, thereby enhancing administrative efficiency. The Preparatory Phase was conducted from 16th September, 2026 to 30th September, 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase commencing on 2nd October, 2026 and concluded on 31st October, 2026.

The outcomes reflect the MoEFCC’s continued commitment towards strengthening institutional efficiency, promoting systematic record management, ensuring responsible disposal of E-waste, redundant materials and fostering cleanliness and sustainable administrative practices.

Attri, Member Technical and Sh. Vijay Kumar, Scientist ‘C’ from CAQM, held a review meeting with…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
High level CAQM Team reviews Paddy Straw Management Measures reviews in Sangrur, Patiala and Malerkotla of Punjab
Team also visits three Villages and Paddy Stubble/Pellet Utilisation Facilities to see Ground-level In-situ and Ex-situ infrastructure
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 11:23PM by PIB Delhi

A high level Team of Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) comprising Dr. S.D. Attri, Member Technical and Sh. Vijay Kumar, Scientist ‘C’ from CAQM, held a review meeting with Deputy Commissioners, SSPs and officers from PPCB and Agriculture Department of Districts Sangrur, Patiala and Malerkotla and flying squads of CPCB at District Administrative Complex, Sangrur on 31.10.2026. The meeting focused on reviewing preparation and management of paddy straw and control of stubble fires of these districts by the District Administrations. The team visited an Ex-situ paddy stubble utilisation facility, a duplex board/paper making unit at Dhuri Road, Malerkotla, which uses paddy straw as fuel in its boiler of capacity 20 TPH. The representatives of the industry informed that about 17000 MT of paddy straw would be utilised in its boiler furnace on an annual basis.

The team also saw in-situ machinery working in village Ahmadabad of District Malerkotla. Working of super seeder was also shown by Agricultural Department. Further, the team met farmers, who in turn assured that they will not burn paddy straw and manage the same using in-situ machinery. The team reviewed arrangements and measures being undertaken by the District Administrations and concerned departments for effective management of paddy straw and prevention of stubble burning during the ongoing harvesting season.

The CAQM team visited different villages namely Bassiark, Kapial and Jhaneri in Bhawanigarh Tehsil of District Sangrur. Further, at village Gharachon, a hotspot village, ex-situ and and in-situ management of paddy straw were demonstrated. During the visit, the team interacted with farmers of this hotspot village. The CAQM team was also informed about preparedness of the District Administration and the arrangements made for ensuring the availability of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery to farmers for in-situ management of paddy straw. Farmers explained the difficulties faced by them regarding utilization of CRM machinery.

The team visited a paddy straw pelletizing manufacturing unit at Village Nadampur, Bhawanigarh. The CAQM officials, accompanied by officers of the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB) and the District Administration, Sangrur obtained first-hand information regarding the utilisation of paddy straw for manufacturing biomass pellets, which are subsequently used as fuel in thermal power plants. The team was apprised that such pellet manufacturing units are playing a significant role in promoting ex-situ management of paddy straw by providing an alternative avenue for its utilisation, thereby helping farmers avoid crop residue burning and contributing towards the prevention of stubble burning incidents.

The CAQM officials asked concerned departments to continue making concerted efforts with close monitoring to ensure effective prevention of stubble burning incidents. The team advised the Officers to ensure effective paddy stubble management as committed by them in the actions. The actions on ground should match with targets undertaken by them.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Department of Pharmaceuticals Organises Plog Run under Fit India Freedom Run 7.0 on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas; Reaffirms Commitment to National Unity, Fitness, and Cleanliness
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, in association with the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), organised a Plog Run at Nehru Park, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, on 31 October 2026 as part of the nationwide Fit India Freedom Run 7.0 campaign.

The 1500-metre Plog Run was led by Shri Awadhesh Kumar Choudhary, Senior Economic Adviser, Department of Pharmaceuticals, and witnessed participation by officers and officials of the Department of Pharmaceuticals,  National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) and Pharmaceuticals Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI).

The initiative sought to promote the importance of incorporating physical activity into daily life while simultaneously encouraging environmental cleanliness. Through the concept of plogging, which combines jogging with picking up litter, the participants highlighted the message that individual efforts towards fitness and cleanliness can collectively contribute to a healthier society and a cleaner environment.

The Fit India Freedom Run, launched in 2020 under the Fit India Movement, aims to encourage citizens to make physical activity an integral part of their daily routine. Its underlying philosophy of "Run Anywhere, Anytime" promotes widespread participation and a culture of fitness across the country.

The event also coincided with the observance of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day), commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the architect of India's political integration. On the occasion, participants took the National Unity pledge, reaffirming their commitment to the unity, integrity and security of the nation.

Through this initiative, the Department of Pharmaceuticals reiterated its commitment to promoting a healthy lifestyle, environmental responsibility and the values of cleanliness, discipline and national unity among its officers and employees.

The event reinforced the message that a fitter individual, a cleaner environment and a united nation are integral to building a healthier and stronger India.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat - NSS Mobilises Over 96,700 Youth  in Nationwide Cyclothons and Walkathons under Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:47PM by PIB Delhi

Taking the message of an addiction-free India to streets and communities, MY Bharat - National Service Scheme (NSS) organised nationwide Cyclothons, Walkathons and Runs on 30–31 October 2026 under Week 7 of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – 100 Week Sankalp Abhiyan. The initiative witnessed over 96,700 participation across more than 200 institutions nationwide.

Organised under the Month 2 theme, “Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth (Shakti evam Seva)”, the campaign focused on encouraging young people to embrace fitness, healthy lifestyles and community service while spreading awareness about the harmful effects of substance abuse. The activities brought together students, NSS volunteers and community members at public spaces and prominent civic landmarks.

As part of the initiative, NSS units organised cycle rallies covering 10–15 km and walkathons and runs spanning 3–5 km. The Walkathon and Run activities collectively recorded over 23,300 participants, while more than 8,000 youth participated in the Cyclothons. The activities also encouraged inclusive participation, with school units, women's groups and senior citizens joining the walkathons.

Extending the campaign beyond physical fitness, volunteers organised street plays (Nukkad Nataks), slogan-writing activities and songs to engage communities in conversations around substance abuse, peer pressure and recovery. Nukkad Nataks engaged over 5,600 participants and members of the public, while slogan-writing and musical activities witnessed participation of more than 11,800 people. These activities used creative and locally accessible communication to reinforce the message of an addiction-free lifestyle.

The initiative also integrated environmental responsibility through plogging drives, combining jogging and walking with cleanliness activities along rally routes. More than 11,400 youth participated in these drives, collecting litter and handing over segregated waste to local civic bodies. The activities culminated in a collective Nasha Mukt Sankalp, with nearly 26,000 participants and community members pledging their commitment to an addiction-free society.

The campaign also witnessed strong digital amplification, with youth ambassadors sharing reels and photographs of the activities on Instagram using #NashaMuktYuva. Through the Week 7 intervention, MY Bharat and NSS continued to strengthen youth-led community mobilisation, promoting fitness, environmental responsibility and collective action towards the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

****

Gaurav Saini

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s speech at the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas programme in Kevadia, Gujarat
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:34PM by PIB Delhi

I will say, “Sardar Patel,” and all of you respond, “Immortal forever, immortal forever.”

Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.

Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.

Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.

My dear countrymen,

Today’s event is somewhat different. Until now, we have always held this programme on Unity Day in the morning. This time, there has been a slight change. We have all gathered in the evening. In the morning, lakhs and lakhs of citizens participated in the Run for Unity with a pledge of national unity. We saw the enthusiasm of the people in the Run for Unity. Yesterday evening, I witnessed magnificent presentations at the Bharat Parv Pavilion. And now, on this national occasion, we are present at the feet of Sardar Patel.

Friends,

This is the world’s tallest statue, the Statue of Unity. The participation of the entire nation in its construction, the unique aura of this place, and the extraordinary energy and inspiration of Unity Day fill one’s heart with pride and gratitude upon coming here. Pride in being a citizen of this great nation, and gratitude towards Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who united more than 550 princely states after Independence. With an iron resolve, he bound this nation together in the thread of unity.

Friends,

Freedom is essential for any nation. When a nation is free, it determines its own future. But freedom receives the right direction through a republic. A republic shows us the path of taking decisions within the framework of the Constitution. The Constitution keeps us accountable to the people. And unity gives us the strength to move forward as one nation. That is why in our country, Independence Day, Republic Day, and Unity Day are all celebrated with great enthusiasm as national festivals.

Friends,

Once again today, in Ekta Nagar, we have witnessed the grand vision of India’s unity. This year’s National Unity Parade has also been extraordinary. This parade is dedicated to the courage and bravery of our police and security forces. Through the tableaux, the nation’s heritage and aspirations have been presented before the country. Therefore, Unity Day is no longer limited merely to official events. Through public participation, it has become a celebration of national pride. On this occasion, I extend my greetings to all countrymen on National Unity Day. I bow with deep reverence at the feet of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Friends,

Sardar Patel is that great personality in India’s history without whom it is difficult even to imagine present-day India. It was Sardar Patel who shaped the India we know today. Even after Partition, the person who kept India secure from the Himalayas to the Indian Ocean was Sardar Patel.

Friends,

Sardar Patel was able to do this because he understood the character and consciousness of India. He knew that India’s diversity was not its weakness. He knew that India’s diversity was, in fact, the true foundation of its unity. For thousands of years, we have lived in this manner. Through this very strength, we touched the heights of progress and prosperity.

Friends,

Sardar Patel once again laid the foundation of that India. He did not merely shape the geography of the nation; he also bound the country together through emotional unity. Through the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple in Gujarat, he also initiated the cultural renaissance of the nation.

Friends,

This year marks the 75th anniversary of that great work as well. Just as the flag of the Somnath Temple has been flying with pride for a thousand years despite the repeated destruction attempted by aggressors, that same spirit of self-respect inspired us to celebrate the Somnath Swabhiman Parva. And this year, the nation is celebrating that occasion with equal enthusiasm.

My dear countrymen,

Today, these great ceremonies of national unity, India’s rising stature on the global stage, the rapid pace of our economic progress, and the revival of our sacred centres from Kashi Vishwanath to the Ram Temple, all point to the direction in which India is moving. It is a path shown to us by Sardar Patel. And for this, the nation will remain indebted to him forever.

Friends,

Last year, we celebrated the 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. For two years, programmes and celebrations were organised across the country. We took major resolutions for the nation and pledged to fulfil them. And today, as we celebrate his 151st birth anniversary, we can say with satisfaction that the nation has fulfilled those resolutions within a very short period of time. In these two years, the country has achieved several unprecedented accomplishments.

Friends,

On the occasion of Sardar Patel’s 150th birth anniversary, standing here at his feet, I had said, “Until the country is completely free from Naxalism and Maoist terror, we will not rest.” And exactly one year later, as we stand here today, that national resolve has been fulfilled. Today, the backbone of Naxalism has been broken in the country. In 2015, 126 districts of the country were affected by Left-wing extremism. By March 2026, not a single district remained in the country that was still affected by Naxalism. These districts, which suffered for decades from violence and bloodshed, are now becoming part of the mainstream of development. Today, roads are expanding in these areas. Mobile networks are reaching people. Educational and healthcare facilities are increasing. Youth who once faced uncertainty now have new opportunities for education, employment, and progress.

Friends,

This time, at this Unity Day celebration, families from Naxal-affected regions have joined us here as special guests. I welcome all of them and wish them a bright future. Today, I also pay my respects to all those brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice to establish peace in these regions of the country.

Friends,

Today, India is more secure than before. Today, India is more determined than before. And one major reason for this is the increased confidence of our citizens. Confidence comes from achievements. Confidence comes from the sensitivity of the government and the system. Today, I would certainly like to speak about one such major national achievement.

Friends,

Talks of removing poverty in India have been going on since Independence. Votes were sought in the name of eradicating poverty. But we all know what the actual condition of poverty in the country was. Those who raised the slogan of removing poverty themselves kept becoming richer. Change in circumstances began to come in recent years. Just a few days ago, a World Bank report was released. The report states that in the ten to twelve years before 2024, fifty crore Indians defeated poverty. That means where earlier 27 out of every 100 people, more than one-fourth of the population, were trapped in extreme poverty, today that number has fallen to less than 3 out of every 100 people.

Friends,

The entire world is acknowledging that this is a major achievement. But how did this happen? It happened because for the past twelve years, the country has prioritised the welfare and empowerment of the poor. During these twelve years, the nation received a leak-proof system. Through DBT, every rupee sent from Delhi reached the poor. Free ration and free healthcare helped poor families save money. Crores of permanent houses, crores of toilets, and smoke-free kitchens made life easier for the poor. Crores of people received the protection of insurance, which became a source of support during times of crisis. Before 2014, even 25 crore people in the country did not have any social security coverage. Today, nearly 100 crore people in the country have been connected to a social security safety net.

Friends,

Today, when the entire nation is remembering and paying tribute to Sardar Saheb, his soul must surely be blessing us. Through such efforts, we will eliminate poverty from the country and build a Developed India.

Friends,

National unity guarantees a nation's stability and success. And in times of global instability such as these, the importance of unity has increased even more. You all know that today the world is burning in the fires of unrest. This is among the most difficult periods of the past several decades. Wars are taking place between many countries around the world. Major economies are struggling with challenges. The crisis of resources continues to grow. Global supply chains are becoming fragmented. At such a time, India's unity, the unity of all Indians, is our greatest strength. Because it is this unity that will help us overcome every storm.

Brothers and sisters,

In recent months, we have seen the world struggling with an energy crisis. In some countries, limits were even imposed on the purchase of petrol and diesel. It was being said that India would face the biggest crisis because it has such a large population and does not produce sufficient petroleum. Amid these concerns, anti-India forces also became active.

But friends,

This is India's strength. We did not allow the impact of this global energy crisis to fall upon our citizens. This is certainly a diplomatic and strategic success for the country, but the unity and solidarity of our people played an equally important role. While the nation was looking for solutions to external challenges, certain forces within the country were busy spreading lies and rumours in an attempt to create instability. But the people of India stood shoulder to shoulder with the nation. This is the greatest strength of this country. This is the strongest foundation of our confidence.

Friends,

When great leaders such as Sardar Patel and Babasaheb Ambedkar created the Constitution of India, they established the system of a ruling side and an opposition side. They also explained the importance of this arrangement. In a democracy, the responsibility of the opposition is to oppose government policies. But unfortunately, in today's India, the opposition has abandoned its duty and has transformed itself from an opposition into an obstruction. In its frustration and despair, it has begun placing obstacles in the path of the country's development. This is not opposition; this is obstruction. They have made it the basis of their politics. They are engaged in tearing apart the dignity and spirit of the Constitution.

Friends,

These forces are continuously engaged in conspiracies to divide the nation. Attempts are being made to divide and pit against one another the children of Mother India. Due to more than a decade of frustration and disappointment, these people have now come out in the open. We must identify who is secretly meeting whom abroad, which anti-India forces are supporting whom, and who is speaking the language of India's enemies. We must recognise these patterns. We must unite and confront them. Especially the way social media is being used as a weapon, the way rumours are being spread, and the efforts being made to damage India's image, all citizens must come together to deal with these challenges. We have ended Naxalism in remote regions. But the threat of intellectual Naxalism has not yet disappeared from the country. The nation must always remain vigilant against these intellectual Naxals.

Friends,

No matter how difficult the circumstances may be, we must not allow this grand mission of national unity and this journey towards a strong and capable India to stop. We must now work towards the next major goals. We must secure the nation's borders completely. We must stop infiltration and demographic changes caused by it. We must also move forward towards a Secular Civil Code.

Friends,

Whenever a nation takes great resolutions, whenever it takes major decisions, obstacles will arise, difficulties will appear, and storms will have to be faced. But India is no longer going to stop. The mantra of "Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat" and the goal of a Developed India have now become India's unwavering resolve. We will push ourselves to the limits of hard work. We will confront every storm with determination. But our eyes will remain fixed on one objective alone: building a strong, capable, and developed India by 2047, when the nation completes 100 years of independence. This passion must be present in every effort we make and in every breath we take. This idea must beat with every heartbeat in our hearts. With this resolve, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on National Unity Day.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Vande Mataram.

Vande Mataram.

Vande Mataram.

Thank you very much.

DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi. 

****

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Celebrations marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
On Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, we pay tribute to Sardar Patel and remember his immense contribution to national unity: PM
Sardar Patel played a monumental role in shaping and safeguarding the nation's unity: PM
Naxalism has been dealt a decisive blow in the country: PM
India today is more secure and more resolute than ever before, a major reason for this is the growing self-confidence of its people: PM
According to a World Bank report, during the 10 to 12 years leading up to 2024, 50 crore Indians have overcome poverty: PM
Every effort we make must be driven by the resolve to build a strong and Viksit Bharat by 2047: PM
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:24PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister highlighted the shift from the traditional morning schedule to an evening ceremony, recalling the magnificent showcase at the Bharat Parv Pavilion the previous evening and the massive turnout of lakhs of citizens resolved to uphold unity during the morning's Run for Unity.

Pointing to the collective nationwide participation in building the world's tallest statue, the Statue of Unity, alongside the unique aura of the venue and the inspiring energy of Unity Day, the Prime Minister stated that visiting the monument fills the heart with pride in being an Indian citizen and deep gratitude toward Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. “After independence, he united more than 550 princely states and wove this nation into the thread of unity with iron determination,” affirmed PM Modi.

Explaining that while independence empowers a nation to shape its own destiny and a republic guides decisions within constitutional bounds to ensure public accountability, the Prime Minister emphasized that unity provides the vital strength to advance together as one nation. “Therefore, in our country now, Independence Day, Republic Day, and Unity Day, all three national festivals are celebrated with full enthusiasm,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the grand spectacle of national unity at Ekta Nagar through this year's National Unity Parade dedicated to the valor of police and security forces and tableaus showcasing India's heritage and aspirations, the Prime Minister observed that Unity Day has evolved beyond mere formal events into a celebration of public pride driven by public participation. “On this occasion, I congratulate all countrymen on National Unity Day, and I bow with reverence at the feet of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel,” remarked PM Modi.

Describing Sardar Patel as a towering historical figure without whom modern India cannot be imagined, the Prime Minister credited him with shaping the nation's present geographical and political form. “Even after Partition, the one who kept India safe from the Himalayas to the Indian Ocean was Sardar Patel himself,” asserted Shri Modi.

Stating that Sardar Patel succeeded because he deeply understood India's character and consciousness, the Prime Minister explained that the leader recognized diversity not as a hurdle, but as the true foundation of national unity that has sustained Indian civilization for millennia. “With this very strength, we have touched the peaks of progress and prosperity,” observed PM Modi.

Emphasizing that Sardar Patel laid the foundation of modern India by uniting the country both geographically and emotionally, the Prime Minister highlighted his pivotal role in initiating the nation's cultural resurgence. “Through the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple in Gujarat, he also initiated the cultural resurgence of the nation,” noted Shri Modi.

Noting that this year marks the 75th anniversary of the Somnath Temple's reconstruction, the Prime Minister stated that the temple flag flying proudly for a thousand years in defiance of tyrants inspired the ongoing Somnath Swabhiman Parv across the country. “And this year the country is celebrating this festival too with the same enthusiasm,” observed PM Modi.

Connecting the grand ceremonies of national unity, India's rising global stature, rapid economic growth, and the cultural revival spanning from Kashi Vishwanath to the Ram Temple, the Prime Minister stated that the nation is advancing along the very path envisioned by Sardar Patel. “And for this, this country will always remain indebted to him,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Recalling the two-year nationwide celebrations marking Sardar Patel's 150th birth anniversary during which the country took major pledges, the Prime Minister expressed satisfaction on his 151st birth anniversary that those resolutions have been fulfilled within a remarkably short span. “In these two years, the country has achieved several unprecedented milestones,” noted PM Modi.

Reminding the nation of his solemn vow made at Sardar Patel's feet during the 150th birth anniversary not to rest until Naxalism and Maoist terror were completely eradicated, the Prime Minister declared that the back of Left-Wing Extremism has been broken within a year, reducing the number of Naxal-affected districts from 126 in 2015 to zero by March 2026. He highlighted that regions scarred by decades of bloodshed are now joining the developmental mainstream with expanding roads, mobile networks, schools, and healthcare facilities. “For the youth who once faced uncertainty, new opportunities for education, employment, and moving forward are opening up,” asserted Shri Modi.

Welcoming families from formerly Naxal-affected regions attending the Unity Day celebrations as special guests and wishing them a bright future, the Prime Minister paid homage to the security personnel who laid down their lives for peace. “Today I also bow to all those brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice to establish peace in these regions of the country,” affirmed PM Modi.

Observing that India today is safer and more resolute due to heightened public confidence born from tangible national accomplishments and a sensitive administration, the Prime Minister highlighted the historic milestone achieved in poverty alleviation after decades of hollow post-independence slogans where those chanting Garibi Hatao only enriched themselves. He cited a recent World Bank report revealing that 50 crore Indians overcame poverty in the 10 to 12 years prior to 2024. “Meaning, where earlier 27 out of 100 people were in the grip of extreme poverty, today this number has remained less than 3,” noted Shri Modi.

Explaining that this globally acclaimed feat was achieved by prioritizing poor welfare and empowerment over the past 12 years through leakage-free Direct Benefit Transfers, free ration, free healthcare, crores of pucca homes, toilets, smoke-free kitchens, and wide insurance coverage, the Prime Minister pointed out that social security coverage has expanded from under 25 crore people before 2014 to nearly 100 crore citizens today. Invoking Sardar Patel's blessings as the nation pays tribute to him, he reiterated the resolve to completely eradicate poverty. “With such efforts alone, we will remove poverty in the country and make the country a Viksit Bharat,” asserted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that national unity guarantees stability and success during the most turbulent global era in decades marked by wars, economic distress, resource crunches, and fractured supply chains, the Prime Minister stated that the solidarity of Indians remains the country's greatest pillar of strength to weather every global storm. Pointing to the recent international energy crisis that forced fuel rationing in several nations and sparked predictions of severe distress for populous, oil-importing India amid the activation of anti-India forces, he credited both diplomatic agility and public solidarity for shielding citizens from the shock.

Warning against divisive forces that have come out in the open after more than a decade of political frustration to plot conspiracies, pit citizens against one another, and weaponize social media to spread rumors and tarnish India's image, the Prime Minister urged citizens to recognize the patterns of secret foreign meetings, external backing from anti-India elements, and rhetoric echoing the nation's enemies. “We have ended Naxalism in remote areas, but the danger of ideological extremists has not yet passed from over the country, and the country has to remain ever vigilant against such entities,” cautioned Shri Modi.

Stressing that the grand mission of national unity and the journey toward a strong and capable India must continue unabated regardless of difficulties, the Prime Minister outlined the next major national priorities of completely securing India's borders, halting infiltration and demographic changes, and advancing toward a Secular Civil Code. Acknowledging that major resolutions and bold decisions will inevitably face roadblocks and storms, he declared that the nation will not be deterred from the unwavering resolves of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat and a Viksit Bharat, working tirelessly with every breath and heartbeat toward the 2047 goal before concluding with festive greetings and chants of Bharat Mata Ki Jai. “We will reach the pinnacle of hard work, we will firmly confront tempests, but our vision will remain on a single goal, the making of a strong and capable India by 2047!” asserted PM Modi.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Delhi Records Lowest Average AQI for October in the Last Eight Years at 166
Delhi Records 220 Good to Moderate AQI Days During January–October 2026, Highest Since 2018 (except 2020)
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

The monthly average AQI of Delhi for October in 2026 is recorded as 166, against the monthly average AQI for October as 223 in 2025, 234 in 2024, 219 in 2023, 210 in 2022, 173 in 2021, 265 in 2020, 234 in 2019 and 269 in 2018, respectively.

The average AQI of Delhi for the period 01-Jan to 31-Oct is recorded as 167, against the average AQI of 170 in 2025, 184 in 2024, 172 in 2023, 187 in 2022, 179 in 2021, 156 in 2020, 192 in 2019 and 201 in 2018, respectively.

The average PM2.5 concentrations for period 01-Jan to 29-Oct is recorded as 69 µg/m³, against the average concentration of 72 µg/m³ in 2025, 83 µg/m³ in 2024, 76 µg/m³ in 2023, 81 µg/m³ in 2022, 82 µg/m³ in 2021, 71 µg/m³ in 2020, 88 µg/m³ in 2019 and 93 µg/m³ in 2018, during the same period respectively.

The average PM10 concentrations for period 01-Jan to 29-Oct is recorded as 171 µg/m³, against the average concentration of 166 µg/m³ in 2025, 186 µg/m³ in 2024, 174 µg/m³ in 2023, 191 µg/m³ in 2022, 182 µg/m³ in 2021, 147 µg/m³ in 2020, 197 µg/m³ in 2019 and 216 µg/m³ in 2018, during the same period respectively.

The period (January – October) in 2026 witnessed 220 'Good to Moderate' category days (daily average AQI less than 200), against the number of such days being 200 in 2025, 201 in 2024, 206 in 2023, 160 in 2022, 197 in 2021, 224 in 2020, 175 in 2019 and 157 in 2018, respectively.

The period (January – October) in 2026 witnessed 84 ‘Poor to Severe+’ category days (daily average AQI more than 200), against the number of such days being 104 in 2025, 104 in 2024, 98 in 2023, 144 in 2022, 107 in 2021, 81 in 2020, 129 in 2019 and 147 in 2018, respectively.

CAQM is working closely with various stakeholders concerned to take effective measures for prevention, control and abatement of air pollution and to improve the air quality in Delhi-NCR. These efforts would be intensified with an endeavour to further improve upon the air quality scenario in Delhi-NCR in the coming days.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES the Dhwaj Stambh Pujan, Dhawaja Pujan and Dhwajarohan ceremony of Simhastha Maha Kumbh at Nashik
convergence of countless devotees at Kumbh Melas has served as living proof of India’s cultural and spiritual unity and the continuity of traditions: President Droupadi Murmu
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the Dhwaj Stambh Pujan, Dhawaja Pujan and Dhwajarohan ceremony of Simhastha Maha Kumbh at Nashik, Maharashtra today (October 31, 2026). She also addressed a public programme on the occasion.

 

In her address, the President said that the tradition of the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Maha Kumbh is as ancient as it is rich. The Kumbh gatherings held on the banks of the Ganga in Haridwar, at the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, on the banks of the Shipra in Ujjain, and on the banks of the Godavari at Nashik, are renowned across the globe. The continuous organization of these gatherings over centuries stands as a testament to the strength of our nation’s historical, cultural, social, and spiritual traditions.

 

The President said that for centuries, the convergence of countless devotees at these Kumbh Melas has served as living proof of India’s cultural and spiritual unity and the continuity of traditions. These gatherings exemplify faith and social harmony. She expressed confidence that the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Maha Kumbh 2027 will serve as a bridge to connect our ancient heritage with the modern times. She wished that this event be an excellent opportunity to connect our younger generation with India’s magnificent heritage and its core life values.

 

The President said that today, people across the globe are facing numerous crises due to extreme weather conditions. In our own country, including in regions like Maharashtra, many people, especially our farmers, have been affected by drought. Both the central and state governments are making every effort to ensure that our citizens, particularly our farmers, receive support as they navigate these challenges.

 

Underlining the importance of cleanliness and awareness about the environment, the President urged citizens to continue making sustained efforts, both individually and collectively, toward environmental conservation. She expressed confidence that during the 'Maha Kumbh' at Nashik, the efforts of the event management, combined with active public participation, will set an exemplary standard for cleanliness and waste management.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Issues Factual Report With Regard To The Claim—Appearing In A Report Published In The Central Chronicle (Bhopal) On October 31, 2026
Claim That MAPCET Made Payments Amounting To Crores Based On Placements Without Verifying The Placement Data, Is Entirely Incorrect And Baseless
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment has issued a factual report with regard to the claim—appearing in a report published in The Central Chronicle (Bhopal), on October 31, 2026.  

The claim with regard to Madhya Pradesh Council for Employment and Training (MAPCET), having made payments amounting to crores based on placements without verifying the placement data, is entirely incorrect and baseless.

The factual report is attached herewith, for publishing the same with accuracy and factual context:

 

FACTUAL REPORT REGARDING THE NEWS ITEM PUBLISHED IN
CENTRAL CHRONICLE, BHOPAL, ON 31 OCTOBER 2026

The Office of the Commissioner, Scheduled Caste Development Department, sanctioned an amount of Rs. 3,241.37 lakh for skill development training under the “Special Central Assistance for Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan” head.

Against this amount, a total of Rs. 2,945.37 lakh was made available to the Madhya Pradesh Employment and Training Council (MAPCET) during 2021–22. This amount comprised Rs. 1,296.00 lakh (vide Order No. 4695 dated 26 November 2021) and Rs. 1,649.37 lakh (vide Order No. 10283 dated 25 March 2022).

The Madhya Pradesh Council for Employment and Training (MAPCET) issued a request for proposal (RFP) for the training of beneficiaries from below-poverty-line (BPL) families belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category for the year 2021–22. Following the selection process, contracts were signed with 34 training provider organisations, and work orders were subsequently issued to them. Of these, six organisations did not commence the work.

After the work orders were issued by MAPCET, 28 institutions provided training to 4,952 trainees. The training programmes conducted by the Council comply with the standards prescribed by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India. All training activities are managed through a dedicated portal, which facilitates trainee registration, daily attendance tracking, and the uploading of assessment and placement data.

Under Clause 2.1.1 of Schedule IV to the Gazette notification issued by the Government of India, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Notification No. 349 dated 4 December 2020, the payment criteria for training providers conducting training in batch mode are as follows:

No.

Instalment

Percentage of batch amount

Milestone

1

First

30%

Commencement of training

2

Second

40%

Successful completion of certification. Payment is made for the number of candidates certified, after adjustment of advance payments.

3

Third

30%

Achievement of 70% verified employment: continuous employment for three months, with desk verification and placement verification in accordance with standard norms.

The first and second instalments have been paid to the training provider organisations in accordance with the criteria and contractual terms prescribed by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India.

The first instalment is paid when a training batch commences, following physical verification of the trainees. The second instalment is paid after the training has been completed and the trainees have been assessed.

The assessment is conducted by entities designated by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET). Trainees must have attended at least 70 per cent of the training to be eligible for assessment. The first and second instalments have been disbursed on this basis.

The post-training placement information submitted by the training provider institutions in hard-copy form is based on job offers or offer letters. Such submissions do not constitute the basis for releasing the third instalment. To qualify for the third instalment, institutions must upload placement details to the portal in accordance with the prescribed criteria. Only then can the portal generate payment claims for the third instalment. As no such payment claims have been generated for any of these institutions, no third-instalment payments have been made.

The claim made in the news report published in Central Chronicle, Bhopal, on 31 October 2026—that MAPCET disbursed crores of rupees on the basis of placements without verifying the placement data—is entirely incorrect and baseless.

• The third instalment, which is conditional upon placement, has not been paid to any of the institutions. Therefore, the question of tracking such placements for the purpose of releasing this instalment does not arise.

• The institutions have received only the first and second instalments, neither of which is linked to placement. Accordingly, placement or placement tracking is not relevant to the payments already made.

The third instalment will be paid when candidates take up employment after completing their training. The organisation is currently facilitating placements.

****

Eng-Reb: TAR/KV/GA/RK-

Dated 31.10.2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat’s ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ Campaign Engages Over 11,000 Youth Through 62 Programmes Across 16 States/UTs
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

Over 11,000 youth participated in 62 editions of ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’, organised across 16 States and Union Territories on 31.10.2026 by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The programmes were held at 62 colleges and educational institutions as part of the nationwide campaign, being conducted from 26.10.2026 to 05.11.2026, with the aim of covering 500 universities, colleges and institutions across the country.

The initiative seeks to promote electoral awareness among young people, particularly first-time voters, and encourage their informed participation in the democratic process. It familiarises them with voting rights, electoral procedures and civic responsibilities while providing opportunities to interact with elected representatives, Youth Icons and other distinguished personalities on democratic participation and nation-building.

The campaign covered a wide geographical spread, with programmes held across Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh in the northern region. It also reached Arunachal Pradesh and Assam in the North-East; Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha in the east; Madhya Pradesh in central India; Maharashtra and Rajasthan in the west; and Tamil Nadu and Telangana in the south.

With the latest round of programmes, a total of 158 Yuva Samvads have been conducted across 28 States and Union Territories, engaging around 32,000 youth and 158 Youth Icons.

In Jaipur, Rajasthan, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) Shri Ghanshyam Tiwari and Member of Parliament (Jaipur City) Smt. Manju Sharma attended the programme and interacted with students on democratic participation and the importance of voting. Youth Icon Ms. Divyanshi Shekhawat delivered a presentation on ‘Know Your Vote’, while Sports Icon Ms. Bhumika Shukla shared her experiences with the participants. Programmes in Ajmer and Dholpur also featured interactions with elected representatives, voter awareness activities and the Loktantrik Pledge.

In Assam, Shri Sushanta Borgohain, Minister of Water Resources, Government of Assam, interacted with youth at Sivasagar and addressed their queries. The programme also featured an interaction with a Youth Icon on responsible social media use, encouraging young people to verify information and check facts before believing or sharing content. In North Lakhimpur, Youth Icons interacted with participants and answered their questions on voting and civic responsibilities.

In Punjab, Yuva Samvads in Ferozepur, Kapurthala, Sangrur, SAS Nagar and Sri Muktsar Sahib witnessed active participation by students and interactions with Youth Icons and academic representatives. In Ferozepur, around 250 youth took the Loktantrik Pledge, while Youth Icon Ms. Janvi Sharma interacted with participants. At Kapurthala, Youth Icon Shri Satyaprakash encouraged young people to contribute to nation-building, with academic representatives from Lovely Professional University also attending. In Sangrur, students participated in an interactive session led by Youth Icon Ms. Falak Masoom on informed and responsible voting. The programmes also featured discussions on civic responsibilities and the Loktantrik Pledge.

In Jammu and Kashmir, MLA Shri Sunil Bhardwaj addressed participants at the Yuva Samvad in Udhampur, highlighting the importance of voting and democratic participation. In Madhya Pradesh, programmes in Narsinghpur, Neemach and Raisen featured interactions with Youth Icons and elected representatives, discussions on leadership and nation-building, and the Loktantrik Pledge. Youth Icon Ms. Mansi Sharma interacted with participants in Narsinghpur and answered their questions on democratic values.

In Uttar Pradesh, programmes across Barabanki, Bulandshahr, Chandauli, Gorakhpur, Jalaun, Jhansi, Kannauj, Kushinagar, Mirzapur and Prayagraj featured youth interactions, presentations, quizzes, competitions and activities promoting civic awareness. In Bulandshahr, students interacted with an elected public representative, while programmes in Chandauli and Gorakhpur included discussions on sports and the importance of cycling and the Khelo India initiative. Other activities included sessions on Nasha Mukt Bharat, Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue, speech and slogan-writing competitions and youth discussions.

In Bihar, programmes in Banka and Muzaffarpur featured interactive discussions in which students raised questions and shared their perspectives. Participants also took the Loktantrik Pledge, reaffirming their commitment to responsible citizenship and active participation in democracy.

The nationwide campaign will continue until 05.11.2026, with further programmes being organised across universities, colleges and educational institutions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
National CSR Meet for School Education organised through Vidyanjali
The Meet highlights role of corporate participation in strengthening school resources
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, organised the National Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Meet for School Education through Vidyanjali – a school volunteer programme, today in Gurugram, Haryana. The meet aimed to strengthen collaboration between the Government, corporate organisations, States/UTs and implementing agencies to leverage CSR for transforming school education.

An important component of the Meet was the CSR-State Interaction, which brought together representatives from corporate organisations, State Nodal Officers, DoSEL, the Programme Management Unit (PMU) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC). The interaction provided an opportunity to explore avenues for collaboration, facilitate networking between CSR organisations and States and discuss potential projects for supporting schools based on their identified requirements.

Representatives from states and union territories showcased their experiences and initiatives under Vidyanjali. Presentations were made by Andhra Pradesh on the implementation of Vidyanjali, Karnataka on the adoption of schools, Mizoram on the role of community participation, and Delhi on innovations and related activities under the programme.

Implementing agencies, including ChildFund India, SARD India, Inspiring Seniors Foundation and ETI Foundation, also shared their experiences and perspectives on facilitating CSR engagement and supporting school development through Vidyanjali.

The technical sessions featured representatives from leading corporate organisations, including the State Bank of India (SBI) and Bharti Airtel, who shared their experiences and initiatives undertaken towards supporting school education. Their presentations highlighted the role of corporate participation in strengthening school resources and creating opportunities for improved learning environments.

Additional Secretary, DoSEL, Ms. Archana Sharma Awasthi; Economic Advisor, DoSEL, Ms. A. Srija; and other senior officials of the Ministry were present on the occasion.

Vidyanjali is an initiative of DoSEL aimed at strengthening government and government-aided schools through structured community and private sector participation. It provides a digital platform connecting schools with volunteers, organisations and CSR partners to facilitate contributions in the form of services, activities and assets. Its CSR framework includes the CSR Module and Adopt-a-School Module, enabling organisations to support school requirements and contribute towards school development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sarbananda Sonowal Administers National Unity Pledge to Ministry Officials, Student Cadets
Sonowal lauds PM Narendra Modi for Honouring Sardar Patel's Legacy
Sonowal interacts with Student Cadets and other youngsters on the occasion, urged them to commit to the cause of Nation Building
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal administered the National Unity Pledge to officers, employees and maritime cadets at his official residence here today, marking National Unity Day, or Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, observed each year on the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Participants took the pledge, affirming, "I will dedicate myself to maintaining the unity, integrity and security of the nation and will also make every possible effort to spread this message among my fellow countrymen. I take this pledge in the spirit of the unity of my country, which became possible through the foresight and actions of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. I also solemnly resolve to contribute with sincerity to ensure the internal security of my country."

Sonowal paid floral tribute to Patel, India's first deputy prime minister and home minister, widely remembered as the "Iron Man of India" for uniting more than 560 princely states into a single nation after independence.

"Sardar Patel gave us one India. For far too long, the man who stitched this nation together did not receive the honour he deserved for decades," Sonowal said. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi changed that. By building the Statue of Unity, the tallest statue in the world, and by dedicating Oct. 31 to national unity, he has placed the Iron Man of India where he belongs: at the heart of every Indian's sense of nationhood."

Sonowal also interacted with young maritime cadets, saying their passion for the nation reflects the true power of Yuva Shakti, or youth power.

"We remain committed to honoring Sardar Patel's legacy of unity and integrity to build a stronger India with the mantra of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat,'" Sonowal said.

The minister said India has emerged stronger under Modi's leadership and is steadily advancing toward the goal of a developed nation, or Viksit Bharat, by 2047.

"Under Prime Minister Modi, 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat' has moved from a vision to a national mission," Sonowal said. "Our ports, shipping lanes and inland waterways now connect every corner of the country, from the Northeast to the western coast. As India sails toward Viksit Bharat by 2047, these young cadets will be the ones steering the ship."

Vijay Kumar, Secretary of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, and other senior officials attended the event.

The government has observed Oct. 31 as National Unity Day since 2014 to commemorate Patel's role in the political integration of India and to reaffirm the country's commitment to unity, integrity and security.

 

***

Four persons were…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
CBN Madhya Pradesh Unit conducts three major anti-drug operations; seizes 2,774.650 kg of poppy straw and five vehicles; arrests four persons
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

In a continued drive against illicit drug trafficking and illegal cultivation of narcotic drugs, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Madhya Pradesh Unit, conducted three significant enforcement operations during over the past few days, resulting in the seizure of 2,774.650 kg illicit poppy straw (Dodachura) and five vehicles. Four persons were arrested in connection with the cases.

On 27 October 2026, acting on specific intelligence, a team of officers of CBN, MP Unit intercepted a Rajasthan-registered container truck on the Mumbai–Delhi Expressway near Sitamau. The vehicle was suspected of transporting a huge quantity of poppy straw towards Punjab. A thorough search resulted in the recovery of 2,308 kg poppy straw packed in 115 white sacks, concealed beneath 598 white sacks of chana husk being used as cover cargo. After completion of the requisite legal formalities, the contraband and container truck were seized, and one person was arrested under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. Further investigation is underway.

Seizure of 2,308 kg poppy straw along with container truck

 

On the intervening night of 28 and 29 October 2026, acting on specific intelligence, a joint team of officers of CBN, MP Unit, conducted an operation at Village Ishaqpur, Tehsil and District Mandsaur, and intercepted a Mahindra pickup truck bearing a suspected fake registration number and a Mahindra Bolero car. During the operation, one person was apprehended, while another suspect fled after abandoning the Bolero car following a brief chase by a secondary CBN team. A thorough search of both vehicles resulted in the recovery of 416.560 kg illicit poppy straw (Dodachura) packed in 22 plastic bags, comprising 17 bags from the pickup truck and five bags from the Bolero car. After completion of the requisite legal formalities, both vehicles along with the recovered contraband were seized, and one person was arrested under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. Further investigation is underway.

 

Seizure of 416.560 kg poppy straw along with two vehicles

 

On 28 October 2026, acting on specific intelligence, a team of officers of CBN, MP Unit, intercepted a Madhya Pradesh-registered Hyundai Grand i10 car and a TVS motorcycle on the Fatehgarh–Nayakheda–Pipliya Mandi route. The intelligence indicated that the motorcycle was piloting the car, which was suspected of transporting approximately 50–60 kg of poppy straw from Fatehgarh Fanta towards Pipliya Mandi. A thorough search of the car resulted in the recovery of 50.090 kg poppy straw packed in two bags. After completion of the requisite legal formalities, the recovered contraband, along with the Hyundai Grand i10 car and TVS motorcycle, was seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. Two persons were arrested in connection with the case. Further investigation is in progress.

Seizure of 50.090 kg poppy straw along with two vehicles

 

These coordinated enforcement operations reflect the continued vigilance and commitment of the Central Bureau of Narcotics, Madhya Pradesh Unit, to curbing illicit cultivation, production, possession and trafficking of narcotic drugs.

CBN remains steadfast in its efforts to dismantle drug trafficking networks, prevent the illegal movement of narcotic substances, enforce the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and contribute to the national mission of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.
