P. Radhakrishnan, today attended ‘Sardar Katha’, organised at Uprashtrapati Bhavan,…
item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attends ‘Sardar Katha’ at Uprashtrapati Bhavan; pays tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas
Calls upon youth to draw inspiration from Sardar Patel’s ideals of unity, discipline and nation-building; says India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047 must be guided by greater ambition and collective resolve
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended ‘Sardar Katha’, organised at Uprashtrapati Bhavan, marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. The programme featured an inspiring narration by renowned Katha Vachika Dr. Shobhana Radhakrishna, highlighting the life, ideals and extraordinary contributions of Sardar Patel to the nation.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attended ‘Sardar Katha’ at Uprashtrapati Bhavan today, organised on the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. The Katha was presented by Dr. Shobhana Radhakrishna, bringing alive the life, ideals and contributions of the Iron Man of India. Emphasising India's remarkable journey since Independence and its march towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Vice-President called upon the youth to imbibe Sardar Patel’s ideals of unity, courage, discipline and selfless service. The programme was attended by Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, and other distinguished guests.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 31, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President extended his greetings on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and said that Sardar Patel’s story was not merely that of one of India's greatest leaders, but also the story of India's unity, courage and nation-building.

Recalling Sardar Patel’s monumental contribution to the political integration of India, the Vice-President said that at the time of Independence, the country faced enormous challenges, with Partition creating uncertainty and more than 550 princely states needing to be integrated into the Indian Union. Through his determination, persuasion, administrative ability and statesmanship, Sardar Patel accomplished this historic task and gave shape to the vision of a united India. The nation, he said, would always remain grateful for this extraordinary contribution.

The Vice-President said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the spirit of unity championed by Sardar Patel is being channelled into the national mission of Viksit Bharat @2047. He observed that India's journey from 1947 to the present reflected courage, determination and collective resolve, while the journey towards 2047 must be marked by even greater ambition, aspiration and commitment.

Emphasising the continuing relevance of Sardar Patel's ideals, the Vice-President said that truth, simplicity, courage, discipline and service to the last person were values that the nation needed to uphold. He particularly called upon the youth to draw inspiration from Sardar Patel's life and channel their immense energy, talent and potential towards constructive nation-building activities.

Concluding his address, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan expressed his appreciation to Dr. Shobhana Radhakrishna and her team for bringing Sardar Patel's life and legacy closer to the audience through the timeless tradition of Katha. “Sardar Patel gave us a united India. It is our duty to keep it united, strong and just. Bharat is One, and shall always remain One!” he said.

The programme was attended by Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, and other distinguished guests.

Earlier in the day, the Vice-President paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at Sardar Patel Chowk in New Delhi and at Uprashtrapati Bhavan.

Paid homage to the Iron Man of India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, on his birth anniversary, observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas at Sardar Patel Chowk in New Delhi. Sardar Patel’s extraordinary life and legacy stand as an enduring testament to the power of national unity, unwavering determination and selfless service. On this solemn occasion, the nation gratefully remembers his monumental contribution to nation-building and pays heartfelt homage to the great visionary whose legacy continues to guide India’s journey towards unity and progress.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 31, 2026

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his birth anniversary at Uprashtrapati Bhavan today. https://t.co/ed3aoOwhGL

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 31, 2026

The extension would provide eligible students additional time to complete their applications on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP)…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Last date for submission of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme for academic year 2026-27 extended till November 15, 2026
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Education extended the last date for submission of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for the academic year 2026-27 till November 15, 2026. The extension would provide eligible students additional time to complete their applications on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and facilitate timely verification by the concerned authorities.

The revised schedule is as follows:

Process

Last Date

Submission of Application

November 15, 2026

Institute Nodal Officer (L1) Verification

November 30, 2026

District Nodal Officer (L2) Verification

December 15, 2026

 

The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) has been open for student applications since June 1, 2026. Students are required to complete their One-Time Registration (OTR) on the portal before applying for the Scholarship. As on 30.10.2026, 90,483 fresh and 1,99,531 renewal applications had been submitted.

Students who have already submitted their applications should ensure that the applications are verified by the concerned Institute Nodal Officer (L1) by November 30 and District Nodal Officer (L2) by December 15, 2026.

NMMSS is aimed at supporting meritorious students from economically weaker sections and encouraging them to continue their education beyond Class VIII up to Class XII.

The scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year to eligible Class IX students who qualify in the selection examination conducted by the respective State/UT Governments. The scholarship is subsequently continued from Classes X to XII through renewal, subject to the prescribed academic requirements.

Eligible students studying in state government and government-aided schools and also schools managed by local self governments, receive ₹12,000 per annum, which is transferred directly to their bank accounts through DBT.

For appearing in the selection test, students must have secured at least 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in Class VII, with a 5-percentage point relaxation for SC/ST students. The parental income of the applicant should not exceed ₹3.50 lakh per annum.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
15 Day Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Start At Dilli Haat, New Delhi, From Tomorrow
Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment, To Formally Inaugurate The Mela On Monday
‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’ To Celebrate India’s Traditional Crafts, Festive Lighting And Cultural Heritage, Showcasing  Artisan Products, Traditional Craftsmanship and Cultural Programmes through Seven Thematic Zones
More Than 1,000 Artisans Benefit From Shilp Samagam Melas Since 2022
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi

The 15 day Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will be organized at Dilli Haat, INA in the National Capital, from tomorrow until November 15, 2026. The Mela is being organized by the Union Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment.

On 2nd November Monday, the Mela will be formally inaugurated by Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment.

Ms V. Vidyavathi, Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Shri Prabhat Tyagi, Chairman-cum-Managing Director, National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), Shri Ashutosh Jain, Chairman-cum-Managing Director, National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC) besides other senior officers and officials of the Ministry, will be present on the occasion.

Themed ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the event will celebrate India’s traditional crafts, festive lighting and cultural heritage through artisan products, live craft demonstrations and cultural programmes.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela continues the Ministry’s efforts to provide aspirational groups and communities with a platform to showcase their creativity, talent and traditional craftsmanship, while creating opportunities to market their products to a wider audience. He said since 2022, the Shilp Samagam Melas have benefited more than 1,000 artisans.

 

The Official said this year, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan) (DEPwD) will organise Shilp Utsav together for the first time, with approximately 150 stalls under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest. The collaboration will bring together traditional artisans, creative talent and inclusive participation in a shared platform.

The Ministry Official said the Mela will be curated around seven thematic zones showcasing India’s crafts, traditions, food and cultural expressions. कला आँगन will feature live craft demonstrations; प्रकाश चौक will showcase lamps and lights; पूजा पथ will present devotional products; सजावट बाज़ार will focus on home décor; घराना will feature textiles and fashion; स्वाद चौक will offer food; and मंच will host cultural activities and performances.

The Official further said that Bharat TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) is an initiative aimed at marketing products made by aspirational groups to consumers in India and abroad through e-commerce platforms. The programme seeks to support economic empowerment while contributing to the preservation of India’s traditional arts and crafts, he added.

The Ministry Official said the Purple Fest is a multidimensional celebration of disability, creativity, talent and equal participation. It brings together persons with disabilities, organisations, institutions, businesses, artists, professionals and other stakeholders to celebrate achievements, encourage participation and promote greater understanding of inclusion, he further said.

It is pertinent to mention that through Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, the Ministry seeks to provide greater visibility to traditional artisans and their products while celebrating India’s rich cultural heritage and encouraging wider public engagement with craftsmanship, creativity and inclusive participation.

PR-205-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department Participates in ‘Run for Unity’ on Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, participated in the ‘Run for Unity’ organised at Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, New Delhi, on the occasion of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) on 31 October 2026.

 The event was flagged off by the Hon’ble Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, in the presence of dignitaries. The occasion marked the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and reaffirmed the nation’s collective resolve to uphold unity, integrity and solidarity.

 Addressing the gathering, Shri Amit Shah highlighted Sardar Patel’s historic contribution to the political integration of India and described the country’s linguistic, cultural and religious diversity as its strength. He also urged citizens to work collectively towards a drug-free India, describing it as essential for the nation’s youth and future.

Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department, participated in the event along with senior officers and staff of the Department. Their participation reflected the Department’s commitment to the ideals of national unity, integrity and collective responsibility.

 The ‘Run for Unity’ provided officers and staff an opportunity to reaffirm their dedication to the values that strengthen the nation and contribute to the successful conduct of the event.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
EPFO to Celebrate 74th Foundation Day in New Delhi Tomorrow
Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to inaugurate proceedings, launch key EPFO initiatives
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) will celebrate its 74th Foundation Day in New Delhi tomorrow. Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, will inaugurate the event. The celebration will be attended by senior officials of the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Members of the Central Board of Trustees, officers and employees of EPFO, employers, workers and other stakeholders.

On the occasion, Dr. Mandaviya will launch key EPFO initiatives, including the Automatic Settlement of Eligible Inoperative EPF Accounts with balances up to ₹1,000 and EPFO Services through WhatsApp, among others.

The Union Minister will also review exhibition stalls at the venue, and release a series of publications reflecting EPFO's commitment to knowledge creation, institutional learning, legal awareness and compassionate governance.

The proceedings will also see Dr. Mandaviya presenting Bhavishya Nidhi Awards 2026 to recognise outstanding contributions by Regional Offices, Zonal Offices, individual officers and employees.

The 74th Foundation Day celebration seeks to reaffirm that the journey of EPFO is not merely a story of institutional growth; it is a continuing commitment to ensure that the fruits of a worker's years of labour translate into security, dignity and peace of mind for the worker and the family.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses 72nd Annual General Body Meeting of IIPA; Calls for Transformative Reforms in Public Administration to Realise Viksit Bharat @ 2047
Public Administration Must Evolve to Meet the Aspirations of a Rapidly Transforming India: Vice-President
Prepare Civil Services for the India of 2047; Reorient Administrative Systems to Address Emerging Challenges: Vice-President
Economic Growth and Environmental Sustainability Must Go Hand in Hand; Natural Resources Should Be Used Judiciously for People’s Welfare: Vice-President
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India and President of the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 72nd Annual Meeting of the General Body of the Indian Institute of Public Administration in New Delhi. Union Minister and Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, Dr. Jitendra Singh; Director General, IIPA, Dr. Surendra Kumar Bagde; members of the General Body and Executive Council; faculty members; representatives of Regional and Local Branches; and other dignitaries attended the meeting.

Vice-President of India and President of the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 72nd Annual General Body Meeting of IIPA in New Delhi. The Vice-President called for citizen-centric governance, better coordination across all levels of administration, a balanced approach to economic growth and environmental sustainability. He urged IIPA to prepare civil servants for the challenges of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Union Minister and Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Director General, IIPA, Dr. Surendra Kumar Bagde, members of the General Body and Executive Council, faculty members, representatives of Regional and Local Branches, officers and staff of the Institute and other distinguished guests attended the meeting. @DrJitendraSingh

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 31, 2026

Highlighting the significance of the occasion coinciding with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the Vice-President paid tribute to the Iron Man of India, describing him as the architect of India’s political integration, who united hundreds of princely states into one nation.

The Vice-President appreciated the significant institutional reforms undertaken by IIPA during 2026, including the redesigned 52nd Advanced Professional Programme, the structured Internship Programme and the engagement of officers from the Central Civil Services and Central Civil Accounts Service. He observed that these initiatives had strengthened the Institute’s administrative and financial architecture. He also commended Dr. Jitendra Singh for his guidance and support and appreciated the Director General, faculty and staff for their efforts in advancing IIPA as a premier institution for public administration.

Observing that public administration was at a critical juncture, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that governance today was increasingly expected to be faster, citizen-centric, technology-enabled, data-driven and outcome-oriented. The Vice-President emphasised that good governance should not be measured merely by economic growth but also by its impact on people's happiness, living standards and overall well-being.

Highlighting India's progress in poverty reduction, the Vice-President noted that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi over the past 12 years, more than 25 crore people had been brought out of poverty. He described this as a significant achievement reflecting the impact of sustained efforts towards inclusive development and improved living standards. He reiterated that the ultimate objective of governance must be to ensure that economic progress translates into dignity, security and better opportunities for every citizen.

The Vice-President stressed that effective public administration required seamless coordination among the Central Government, State Governments and district-level administration. He said that governance could deliver meaningful results only when different levels of administration worked together with a shared vision and common purpose.

The Vice-President emphasised the need for a balanced and pragmatic approach towards environmental protection and economic development.  He stressed that natural resources must be utilised judiciously for the betterment of people while ensuring environmental sustainability.

The Vice-President urged IIPA to focus its work on the changing role of civil services in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. He observed that India’s administrative structures had largely evolved when the country was predominantly rural and agriculture was the principal source of livelihood. However, with the country undergoing rapid transformation, administrative systems must also be reoriented to address emerging realities. He urged IIPA to take the lead in this important endeavour and prepare the next generation of civil servants.

Concluding his address, the Vice-President observed that IIPA had a significant responsibility in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047. He called upon IIPA and its members to work collectively towards ensuring that India’s governance framework remained responsive, inclusive, ethical and future-ready.

During the occasion, the Vice-President also conferred the Paul H. Appleby Award, the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Award for Academic Excellence, and the Best IIPA Branches Awards at the 72nd Annual General Body Meeting, recognising distinguished contributions to the Indian Institute of Public Administration and the field of public administration.

“Good governance requires teamwork, coordination, and a common purpose.” : Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan at the 72nd Annual Meeting of the General Body of the Indian Institute of Public Administration, New Delhi https://t.co/19h7fqy5qm

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 31, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
MoHUA Conducts Participatory Workshop to Chart a Shared Roadmap for Clean Delhi
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Capital Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) in collaboration with Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban organised a workshop on Planning a Shared Roadmap for Clean Delhi, bringing together sanitation inspectors, supervisors, urban local body officials and key stakeholders to collectively deliberate on practical solutions for making the national capital cleaner, healthier and more liveable. Ms. D. Thara, Secretary, Department of Capital Development, MoHUA, along with senior officials from NDMC, MCD, DDA, and MoHUA, participated in the workshop.

The workshop, “Planning a Shared Roadmap for Clean Delhi,” was envisioned to bring stakeholders together to understand these challenges and co-create practical solutions. For the first time, functionaries from the top to the lowest level, came together on a common platform to deliberate on critical issues and chart a collective path towards a cleaner Delhi.

Sanitation staff, being at the forefront of service delivery, are the ones who are able to share first-hand insights into everyday operational challenges, enabling stakeholders to brainstorm and ideate practical, on-ground solutions alongside policy interventions. An online digital poll was conducted among the participants to identify key challenges affecting cleanliness in Delhi and gather insights from stakeholders working at the grassroots level. The exercise provided valuable feedback on operational gaps, citizen behaviour, service delivery challenges and opportunities for improvement.

As a mark of appreciation for their exemplary contribution towards urban sanitation, the invited Sanitary Inspectors and Supervisors were felicitated for their dedicated efforts in maintaining cleanliness across the city. The workshop commenced with an inspiring motivational address by the distinguished spiritual leader BK Hussain from Brahma Kumaris.

A major highlight of the workshop was an extensive interactive discussion centred around ten critical questions aimed at developing a collective roadmap for a Clean Delhi. The deliberations focused on some of the most pressing urban sanitation challenges, including the reasons Delhi continues to struggle with visible cleanliness despite significant investments and efforts; strategies for transitioning towards a bin-less city through more efficient and frequent door-to-door waste collection; recurring Garbage Vulnerable Points (GVPs) and measures to prevent littering and waste from entering water bodies; and ensuring that public toilets remain clean, safe and functional throughout the day. The discussions also explored ways to improve citizen grievance redressal systems. Best practices were highlighted as success stories while also sharing photographs & incidents requiring focussed efforts and targeted interventions.

The deliberations brought together perspectives from sanitation workers, inspectors, supervisors, urban local body representatives and policymakers, fostering a collaborative dialogue on strengthening urban sanitation systems and enhancing accountability for improving visible cleanliness in Delhi.

Addressing the gathering, Ms. D. Thara, Secretary, DoCD, MoHUA, congratulated the Sanitary Inspectors and Supervisors for their tireless efforts and commitment towards improving cleanliness standards across Delhi. She said, “The most vital part of any Municipality is its sanitation workforce - the Sanitation Inspectors and staff. While a doctor provides medicine after diagnosis, we are the team that works before the doctor. By ensuring cleanliness and sanitation for all, we prevent disease. We are the true givers of health to society, as our Swachhata work reduces illness and enables citizens to lead a healthier, higher quality of life.”

The workshop concluded with a shared commitment from all stakeholders to work collectively towards implementing practical, citizen-centric and results-oriented measures that will contribute to making Delhi cleaner.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INAUGURAL BIMSTEC MARITIME SECURITY EXERCISE
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:38PM by PIB Delhi

Translating Vision to Action

Shared Seas, Shared Security and Shared Prosperity

 

The inaugural BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise, being conducted from 30 Oct to 03 Nov 2026, marks a significant milestone in advancing maritime cooperation among the member states of BIMSTEC. Bringing together Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand, the exercise reinforces the shared commitment of member states towards regional security, stability and prosperity in the Bay of Bengal.

Building upon the outcomes of the 6th BIMSTEC Summit under the theme “BIMSTEC: Prosperous, Resilient and Open”, the exercise provides a practical framework for enhancing maritime cooperation and operational linkages among participating nations. It reflects BIMSTEC’s collective resolve towards “Translating Vision to Action” by advancing cooperation in areas of mutual maritime interest and strengthening regional security mechanisms.

The Bay of Bengal remains a critical maritime space connecting South and South-East Asia and supporting trade, connectivity, energy security and economic growth. The exercise aims to enhance interoperability, strengthen maritime domain awareness, improve coordination mechanisms and promote the exchange of Best Practices among BIMSTEC member states.

The exercise also highlights the strategic importance of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the role of the Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC), India’s first integrated tri-service command. Its location astride critical sea lanes of communication and its capabilities in maritime surveillance, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, search and rescue, and regional engagement make it an important pillar of maritime security in the Bay of Bengal.

As BIMSTEC nations come together for this inaugural exercise, they reaffirm their commitment to a secure, open and inclusive maritime domain. The exercise embodies the spirit of “Shared Seas, Shared Security and Shared Prosperity” and demonstrates regional solidarity in pursuit of peace, stability and sustainable development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
AIR CHIEF MARSHAL AP SINGH SUPERANNUATES AFTER 42 YEARS OF DISTINGUISHED SERVICE TO THE NATION
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi

Air Chief Marshal AP Singh PVSM AVSM, Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), superannuates from the Indian Air Force on 31 October 2026, bringing to a close an illustrious career spanning 42 years of distinguished service to the nation.

An accomplished fighter pilot and an Experimental Test Pilot, he has made significant contributions to the operational capability, combat preparedness and modernisation of the Indian Air Force. His tenure as the Chief of the Air Staff was marked by decisive leadership and an unwavering focus on operational readiness, particularly during Operation SINDOOR, wherein the Indian Air Force demonstrated its combat capability, operational precision and resolve in the service of national objectives. His leadership reinforced the IAF's ability to respond decisively across the full spectrum of operations.

Beyond operational leadership, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh will be remembered for his deep and personal connect with air warriors across the length and breadth of the organisation. His interactions with personnel at the grassroots level reflected his conviction that the strength of the Indian Air Force rests in its people. Whether engaging with the last air warrior in the chain of command or interacting with young officers, airmen and cadets, he consistently emphasised professionalism, accountability, initiative and pride in service. His ability to connect with young minds, and inspire confidence reflected his belief in nurturing the next generation of air warriors and leaders.

Throughout his tenure, he focused on creating a technologically empowered and future-ready Indian Air Force, with emphasis on indigenisation, innovation and the integration of emerging technologies. His vision and guidance have further strengthened the organisation's resolve towards building a capable, credible and combat-ready force.

The Indian Air Force wishes Air Chief Marshal AP Singh and Mrs Sarita Singh, the very best for the years ahead. His legacy of leadership, operational resolve and enduring connect with air warriors will continue to inspire generations.

.***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
AIR CHIEF MARSHAL ASHUTOSH DIXIT PVSM AVSM VM VSM ASSUMES CHARGE AS CHIEF OF THE AIR STAFF OF THE INDIAN AIR FORCE
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit PVSM AVSM VM VSM assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 October 2026. He succeeds Air Chief Marshal    AP Singh, PVSM  AVSM, who superannuated after 42 years of distinguished service to the nation.

An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit was commissioned into the Fighter Stream of the Indian Air Force on 06 December 1986.

Over a career spanning four decades, the Air Chief has rich experience across diverse domains such as Operations, Flight Testing, Capability Development and Joint Staff assignments. An accomplished Fighter Pilot, Qualified Flying Instructor and Experimental Test Pilot, he has over 3,500 hours of flying experience on a wide range of aircraft, including the Mirage-2000, various MiG variants, Jaguar and several transport aircraft.

Widely recognised for his contribution to the modernisation of the Indian Air Force, he was instrumental in finalising the Jaguar and MiG-27 upgrade projects and in the completion of the Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) and Final Operational Clearance (FOC) activities of the LCA MK-I Tejas. His operational command assignments include command of a Mirage-2000 Squadron, a Forward Base Support Unit in the Western Sector and Air Force Station Bidar, a premier fighter training base of the IAF.

The Air Officer has served as Air Defence Commander at Southern Air Command, Senior Air Staff Officer at South Western Air Command and Deputy Chief of the Air Staff, steering key capability development and procurement initiatives. He subsequently commanded Central Air Command as Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief and later served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee during Operation Sindoor. Prior to assuming charge as Chief of the Air Staff, he served as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff.

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is an accomplished graduate of the Defence Services Command and Staff College, Bangladesh, and the National Defence College, New Delhi. He is a recipient of the Vayu Sena Medal, Vishisht Seva Medal, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal and Param Vishisht Seva Medal in recognition of his distinguished service to the nation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Positions IIPA’s Nationwide Outreach for Inclusive Capacity Building in Governance
Union Minister emphasises taking IIPA’s activities beyond the national capital through stronger Regional and Local Branches
Dr. Jitendra Singh addresses IIPA’s 72nd Annual General Body Meeting in the presence of Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan
Digital learning, online courses and private-sector collaboration to widen access to capacity building: Dr. Jitendra Singh
IIPA membership reaches 11,611, with expanded participation of young professionals and recent graduates, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:16PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh has emphasised nationwide outreach by the Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) as a key priority for ensuring inclusive capacity building in governance.

Stressing the need to move beyond the national capital, he said that expanding IIPA’s geographical reach would help make its learning resources, academic activities and professional networks accessible to a wider community.

Addressing IIPA’s 72nd Annual General Body Meeting, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Chairman of the IIPA Executive Council, spoke in the presence of the Vice President of India and President of IIPA, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, along with senior officials, members of the Institute’s governing bodies and representatives of its academic and administrative community.

Referring to IIPA’s efforts to extend its activities beyond the national capital, the Minister said that this experience had proved motivating. He emphasised the importance of building on this momentum and strengthening the Institute’s presence across the country so that capacity-building opportunities in public administration are not confined to Delhi but reach officials and professionals in different regions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed the need to further strengthen IIPA’s Regional and Local Branches and use them as important channels for wider participation, professional engagement and the dissemination of knowledge. A stronger regional presence would help the Institute connect more effectively with public administration professionals and extend its academic and capacity-building activities to a broader geographical base.

The Minister also referred to the broadening of IIPA’s membership framework, including opportunities for younger professionals and recent graduates to become part of the Institute. With its membership reaching 11,611, IIPA has an opportunity to engage a wider and more diverse community, bringing together experienced administrators, young professionals, researchers and others interested in public administration.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the role of digital learning and online courses in widening access to knowledge and training. He also stressed the importance of collaboration with the private sector and exploring different ways of making learning resources available to a larger audience. Such efforts can complement the Institute’s physical presence and help expand participation in capacity-building programmes.

Recalling the legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the role of the civil services in nation-building, the Minister spoke about IIPA’s institutional journey since its establishment in 1954. He emphasised the continuing relevance of strengthening public administration through learning, research and professional development as India advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat.

IIPA’s work during 2025–26 included the completion of 45 research projects, with 13 studies ongoing. The Institute also conducted 130 training programmes and related academic activities, including 35 programmes for State Government officials serving at the state, district and local levels.

As of March 31, 2026, IIPA had 26 Regional Branches and 43 Local Branches across the country. Strengthening this network and expanding nationwide outreach remain important to extending the Institute’s reach and making capacity building more inclusive.

The Annual General Body Meeting reviewed the Institute’s activities and priorities, with discussions centred on strengthening its contribution to public administration, widening participation and enhancing the reach of its academic and capacity-building initiatives in line with the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

The campaign focused on improving workplace cleanliness, strengthening record management, reviewing pending matters and promoting…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Concludes Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Swachhata, Record Management and Digital Governance
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (MoPA) has successfully concluded its participation in Special Campaign 6.0 for institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency, conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign focused on improving workplace cleanliness, strengthening record management, reviewing pending matters and promoting efficient and sustainable administrative practices.

The campaign, steered by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, aims to institutionalise Swachhata in government offices and enhance administrative efficiency through systematic record management, timely disposal of pending matters and improved utilisation of office space.

During the preparatory phase, the Ministry identified targets relating to record management, cleanliness and disposal of obsolete materials. The implementation phase witnessed focused efforts towards achieving the identified targets and improving the overall efficiency of office functioning.

Key Achievements under Special Campaign 6.0

Record Management: The Ministry reviewed all identified physical files and e-files as part of the campaign. A total of 134 physical files were identified for review among which 58 were identified for weeding out and have been weeded out, while 200 e-files were reviewed and 117 e-files were closed. These measures have contributed to systematic record management and streamlined administrative processes.

Cleanliness and Workplace Improvement: The campaign reinforced the importance of maintaining clean, organised and efficient workplaces. Cleanliness and workplace management remained important focus areas, with emphasis on sustaining Swachhata as an integral part of routine office functioning.

Inspections were conducted by senior officers under the leadership of the Secretary and the Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs to assess sanitation and cleanliness standards across Sections/Offices of the Ministry

Digital and Paperless Governance: The Ministry continues to promote digital and paperless functioning through various e-governance platforms, including e-Office, e-HRMS, Consultative Committee Management System, Sub-ordinate Legislation Management System, National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA), OAMS and the National Youth Parliament Portal. These platforms facilitate streamlined administrative processes, reduce dependence on physical records and promote transparency and efficiency.

The National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA), a flagship initiative of the Ministry, continues to support paperless functioning of State Legislatures, contributing to efficient legislative processes and environmentally sustainable governance.

Special Campaign 6.0 has further reinforced the Ministry’s commitment to systematic record management, digital transformation and a clean and organised work environment. The Ministry will continue to sustain these efforts beyond the campaign period and integrate Swachhata, efficiency and sustainable practices into its day-to-day functioning.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Government of India extends Customs Duty Exemption on Cotton imports up to 31st December 2026
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:38PM by PIB Delhi

Keeping in view the raw material requirements of domestic textile industry, Government of India has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports until 31st December 2026.

The extension has been notified by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, vide Notification No. 35/2026-Customs dated 30th October 2026. Through this amendment, the existing exemption, which was available until 31st October 2026, has been extended by two months, up to 31st December 2026.

The Government of India remains conscious of the need to balance the requirements of the textile industry with the interests of domestic cotton farmers, while promoting the sustainable and long-term growth of the entire cotton and textile value chain. The decision aims to augment the availability of cotton for the domestic textile sector, ensure the availability of cotton at competitive prices, support domestic manufacturing, address specialised cotton requirements and support value addition across the textile and apparel value chain.

The measure is expected to provide greater flexibility to textile and apparel manufacturers in meeting their raw material requirements, help ease input cost pressures, support Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and strengthen the competitiveness of Indian textiles in domestic and international markets.

The extension is expected to facilitate uninterrupted availability of raw materials, improve operational flexibility for the textile industry and promote greater value addition across the cotton-based textile and apparel sector.

The Ministry of Textiles welcomes and appreciates the decision of the Ministry of Finance and remains committed to promoting a competitive, resilient and globally integrated textile sector, advancing value addition and employment generation, and fostering the long-term growth of the entire textile value chain.

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of the equity share capital of IntelliSmart Infrastructure (Target) by Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. (Acquirer)
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of equity share capital of IntelliSmart Infrastructure Private Limited (Target) by Adani Energy Solutions Limited (Acquirer).

The Proposed Combination envisages the acquisition of 100% of the equity share capital of the Target by the Acquirer from National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF/Seller 1) and Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL/Seller 2).

The Acquirer is part of the Adani Group and is a public listed company incorporated in India, listed on BSE Limited as well as the National Stock Exchange of India Limited. The Acquirer is primarily involved in the activities of transmission and distribution of electricity and in the business of deployment of advanced metering infrastructure for electricity in India.

The Target is, inter alia, involved in the activity of advanced metering infrastructure for electricity in India. The Target is also involved in the deployment of certain smart gas meters in India.

Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain shareholding in Navi Ltd by MIH Payments Holdings B.V.
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of certain shareholding in Navi Limited by MIH Payments Holdings B.V.

The Proposed Combination involves the acquisition of certain shareholding in Navi Limited (Target) by MIH Payments Holdings B.V. (Acquirer).

The Acquirer is an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Prosus N.V. The Acquirer by itself does not undertake any business activity, other than holding investments in its portfolio companies which have business activities in India.

The Target is the holding company of the Navi Group, which offers financial services accessible through a single consumer-facing mobile app. The Target offers transparent, user-friendly financial products through its subsidiaries, all accessible via mobile devices.

Competition Commission of India
CCI approves merger of Sapphire Foods India with and into Devyani International and related transactions
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the merger of Sapphire Foods India Limited with and into Devyani International Limited and related transactions.

 

The Proposed Combination envisages merger of Sapphire Foods India Limited (Sapphire) with and into Devyani International Limited (Devyani) and certain related transactions.

Devyani, inter alia, operates KFC and Pizza Hut franchise outlets across India. Devyani is also the exclusive franchisee of Costa Coffee, New York Fries, and Sanook Kitchen in India. In addition, Devyani also owns and operates homegrown brands.

Sapphire also operates KFC and Pizza Hut franchise outlets in India.

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of Solenergi Power (Target) by Aditya Birla Renewables Ltd (Acquirer)
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of Solenergi Power Private Limited (Target) by Aditya Birla Renewables Limited (Acquirer).

The proposed combination relates to acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of the Target by the Acquirer from Shell Overseas Investment B.V. (Seller).

The Acquirer (including its subsidiaries) is engaged in the business of power generation through renewable energy resources (solar and wind) as well as captive Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) activities.

The Target is primarily a holding company, registered in Mauritius. It does not have any other businesses except that of a holding company. The Target is present in India through: (i) certain downstream holding entities; and (ii) entities that are engaged in the business of power generation through renewable energy resources (solar and wind).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah Flags off ‘Run for Unity’ in New Delhi on 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas’on the occasion of 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Ever since Shri Narendra Modi became the Prime Minister, we have been observing the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel as 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas'
Sardar Sahab transformed the history and also reshaped the geography of India; by undertaking the arduous task of uniting numerous princely states, Sardar Patel created the map of the unified India we see today
Sardar Sahab not only made successful efforts for the geographical, political, and cultural integration of India, but also unified the nation and bound it into one thread
In just 1,218 days, Sardar Sahab created an undivided India and achieved what many leaders could not accomplish in their entire lifetimes
This year, on 31 March, the country became free from Naxalism and moved forward towards becoming a drug-free nation
We have set a target to make the country completely free from drugs by 31 December 2029, and the first stage of a developed India is a drug-free India
Building a drug-free India will be the greatest achievement for the country’s youth and their future
The linguistic, cultural, and traditional diversity of the country is our greatest strength
Through the reconstruction of Somnath, we experienced civilizational and national renaissance, and the concept of rebuilding this temple was also envisioned by Sardar Sahab
The opposition tried for many years to sideline and forget Sardar Sahab by not giving him due respect for his works, but no one can cover the light of the sun
The ‘Statue of Unity’ that Modi Ji conceptualized and laid the foundation stone for while serving as the Chief Minister of Gujarat has established the towering personality of Sardar Sahab before the entire country
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah also administered the Unity Pledge to the countrymen on the occasion of ‘Rahstriya Ekta Diwas’
Today, Prime Minister Modi Ji will take the salute of the parade of police forces from across the country from the same place and deliver the
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 2:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah flagged off the 'Run for Unity' in New Delhi today, organized on the occasion of 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas'—marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. On this occasion, Union Home Minister also administered the 'Unity Pledge' to the citizens of the country. Several dignitaries were present at the event, including Delhi Lieutenant Governor Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Chief Minister of Delhi Smt. Rekha Gupta, and Union Ministers of State for Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai and Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar.

In his address on this occasion, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that ever since Shri Narendra Modi became the Prime Minister of the country, we have been observing the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel as 'Rashtriya Ekta Diwas'. Today marks the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Sahab. He was a great personality who not only transformed the history of India but also shaped its very geography. By undertaking the arduous task of uniting numerous princely states and royal domains, Sardar Sahab created the map of the unified India we see today. He said that Sardar Sahab not only made successful efforts toward the geographical, political, and cultural integration of India but also brought the nation together, binding it into a single, cohesive entity.

Shri Amit Shah said that when the country attained independence, the world predicted that India would disintegrate. In just 1,218 days following independence, Sardar Patel accomplished what many deemed impossible by forging a united India. Today, the India envisioned by Sardar Patel stands proudly before the world.

Union Home Minister said that on March 31st this year, the country got rid of Naxalism and is now progressing on the path to becoming a drug-free nation. He emphasized that the creation of a drug-free India is the foundational step toward the Prime Minister Modi’s vision of a 'Viksit Bharat'. He said that significant milestones have been achieved during Prime Minister Modi’s tenure—such as the abrogation of Article 370, which permanently integrated Kashmir into India; the eradication of Naxalism; and the implementation of a unified tax system. Shri Shah said that the realization of a drug-free India would be the most significant achievement of all—one that would profoundly benefit the nation's youth and its future.

Shri Amit Shah said that the linguistic, cultural, and traditional diversity of our country is not our weakness, but strength. He said that this was the message of Sardar Patel, and it is the path we must continue to follow. Our linguistic, cultural, and religious diversity is our power. Through dialogue, trust, and an inclusive mindset, we have built a shared national identity over the past 80 years. While our languages, attire, cultural beliefs, and religions may differ, our nation has always remained united.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple served as an experience of civilizational and national resurgence. It was Sardar Patel who envisioned the construction of the Somnath Temple. Today, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the initiatives of 'Make in India' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' are guiding us toward attaining a top position among the world's economies.

Shri Amit Shah said that Sardar Sahab did not get the recognition he deserved for his contributions for many years. The opposition always attempted to erase the memory of Sardar Sahab, but just as the light of the sun cannot be concealed, his legacy could not be suppressed. He said that when Shri Narendra Modi was the Chief Minister of Gujarat, he commissioned the 'Statue of Unity'—a towering monument—thereby presenting the stature of Sardar Sahab’s great personality to the entire nation. Shri Shah said that today, from that very location, Prime Minister Modi will take the salute at a parade of police forces from across the country, conveying a message of national unity.

*******

RK / RR / PR / PS

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS GAYATRI PARIVAR’S CONTRIBUTIONS TO INDIA'S SPIRITUAL RENAISSANCE, SOCIAL TRANSFORMATION AND NATION-BUILDING
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS UPON GAYATRI PARIWAR TO CARRY FORWARD IDEALS OF DEVELOPMENT, RIGHTEOUSNESS AND NATION-BUILDING
MATA BHAGWATI DEVI JI'S LIFE OF PENANCE, COMPASSION AND SERVICE INSPIRED A TRANSFORMATIVE MOVEMENT FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND SOCIAL REFORM: LOK SABHA SPEAKER.
AKHAND JYOTI CONTINUES TO ILLUMINATE LIVES THROUGH SPIRITUAL AWAKENING, VALUE-BASED EDUCATION AND CHARACTER-BUILDING: SHRI OM BIRLA.
LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES CENTENARY CELEBRATION, ORGANISED BY GAYATRI PARIVAR IN NEW DELHI
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 31 October 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today paid rich tributes to the revered spiritual luminaries Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji and Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji at the Shatabdi Samaroh 2026, recalling their invaluable contributions to India's spiritual renaissance, social transformation and nation-building. He observed that the centenary celebration was not merely an occasion to commemorate the past, but a celebration of a creative movement that had transformed countless lives across the country.

Paying homage to Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji during his address at the centenary celebration organised by Gayatri Parivar in New Delhi, Shri Birla said that through Akhand Jyoti, he had spread the light of spirituality across the country and inspired people with the ideals of individual development, family development, social development and nation-building. His inspiring resolve, “We will change, and the era will change”, had become a guiding principle for people in India and across the world. Through the Gayatri Mantra and yajna, Acharya Ji connected people with spiritual consciousness and paved the way for inner purity and spiritual awakening.

Recalling his personal association with the Gayatri Parivar, Shri Birla said that he had witnessed the transformative influence of Acharya Ji's spiritual philosophy even in remote villages and hamlets, where it had helped people overcome difficult circumstances, superstition and harmful social practices. The movement had not only brought about a change in people's social lives but had also contributed to their personal growth, character-building and a deeper sense of responsibility towards society and the nation.

Paying his respectful homage to Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji, the Lok Sabha Speaker highlighted her extraordinary life of maternal affection, compassion, penance, dedication and service. He said that her contribution went far beyond spiritual awakening, as she spearheaded a significant movement for social transformation and women's empowerment at a time when women across the country faced numerous social challenges and restrictive practices. He observed that Mata Ji inspired women to pursue education, develop self-confidence and become self-reliant. Her life and teachings demonstrated that the development of a woman's personality within a household lays the foundation for the progress of the entire family and society. Her maternal affection and compassionate guidance transformed the lives of countless women and gave a new impetus to their social and spiritual empowerment. An environment rooted in spiritual awareness and Indian values, he said, played an important role in nurturing positive attitudes, strengthening families and building a progressive society.

Shri Birla appreciated the Gayatri Parivar's sustained efforts to take India's spiritual heritage, cultural wisdom and value-based philosophy to different parts of the world. He noted that the organisation, through its work in several countries, had been advancing the ideals of individual, family and social development in keeping with contemporary needs. He also appreciated the institution's commitment to education rooted in spirituality, culture and Indian values.

Referring to the university established by Acharya Ji, the Lok Sabha Speaker said that its emphasis on spirituality, cultural values and character-building from the early stages of education was commendable.

He expressed appreciation for the institution's initiatives in value-based education, women's awakening and empowerment, and social reform. He also lauded Dr. Chinmaya Pandya for taking India's spiritual traditions and cultural values to the world while simultaneously familiarising people with developments in science and technology. Emphasising the relevance of spirituality in the contemporary world, Shri Birla said that at a time when people in several countries were experiencing stress and depression, the message of inner peace, spiritual strength and a purposeful life had become increasingly significant. The Gayatri Parivar's spiritual centre, he observed, provided people with peace of mind, self-confidence, determination and a sense of direction in life. Shri Birla called upon the Gayatri Pariwar to continue carrying the light of Akhand Jyoti to every village and every section of society. He emphasised that this mission must continue until the life of the last person in society was touched by positive transformation. The ideals of spirituality, religion, culture, character-building and nation-building, he said, must remain central to this endeavour.

Expressing confidence in the continued contribution of the Gayatri Parivar, Shri Birla said that the spiritual energy and consciousness inspired by Acharya Shri Ram Sharma Ji and Mata Bhagwati Devi Ji would continue to illuminate lives and strengthen the foundations of a harmonious, enlightened and developed society.

परम वंदनीया माता भगवती देवी शर्मा जी के धरती पर अवतरण के 100 वर्ष, अखण्ड दीपक के प्राकट्य के 100 वर्ष तथा परम पूज्य गुरुदेव पण्डित श्रीराम शर्मा आचार्य जी की तप-साधना के 100 वर्ष पूर्ण होने के पावन उपलक्ष्य में नई दिल्ली में आयोजित शताब्दी समारोह में सम्मिलित होकर देश-विदेश से पधारे गायत्री परिवार के परिजनों एवं श्रद्धालुओं को संबोधित किया। इस अवसर पर माताजी को सादर नमन करते हुए उनके सम्मान में जारी स्मारक डाक टिकट का विमोचन किया। अखण्ड दीपक का दिव्य प्रकाश उस महान तप-साधना और युग निर्माण के संकल्प का प्रतीक है, जिसे परम पूज्य गुरुदेव ने अपने साधनामय जीवन से साकार किया। मुझे भी अनेक अवसरों पर पावन अखण्ड दीपक के दर्शन का सौभाग्य प्राप्त हुआ है। माताजी का त्याग, तप, सेवा और लोकमंगल के प्रति समर्पण भारतीय आध्यात्मिक परंपरा की अमूल्य विरासत है। माताजी के जीवन-दर्शन का विशिष्ट पक्ष नारी जागरण और महिला सशक्तीकरण रहा। वर्ष 1975 में उनके नेतृत्व में आरंभ हुआ महिला जागरण अभियान महिलाओं को अपनी सामर्थ्य पहचानने और समाज निर्माण में सक्रिय भूमिका निभाने की प्रेरणा देने वाला दूरदर्शी प्रयास था। उन्होंने साधना, सेवा और संस्कार को जीवन के आचरण, कर्तव्यनिष्ठा, करुणा और परोपकार का आधार बनाया। अखण्ड दीपक से प्रज्वलित आध्यात्मिक चेतना को जन-जन तक पहुँचाने और ज्योति से ज्योति जलाकर राष्ट्र एवं मानवता के नवजागरण का संकल्प आज भी प्रासंगिक है। विकसित भारत की यात्रा में चरित्र निर्माण, मूल्यपरक शिक्षा और सामाजिक समरसता का विशेष महत्त्व है। माताजी की सबसे बड़ी विरासत यही है कि उन्होंने सामान्य जन को भी लोकमंगल के महान उद्देश्य से जोड़ा। इस अवसर पर अखिल विश्व गायत्री परिवार के समर्पित साधकों एवं कार्यकर्ताओं का अभिनंदन करता हूँ। मेरी कामना है कि सेवा, संस्कार और मानव कल्याण का यह यज्ञ निरंतर प्रज्वलित रहे तथा यह आध्यात्मिक आलोक आने वाले समय में राष्ट्र और विश्व के नव निर्माण का पथ प्रशस्त करता रहे। @awgpofficial @dsvvofficial @JM_Scindia

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) October 31, 2026

***

AM

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda administers Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 11:36AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri J.P. Nadda, today administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) pledge to officers and officials of both the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers at a ceremony held at Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi. The observance commemorated the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, whose contributions to the integration and unity of the nation remain an enduring inspiration.

The ceremony was attended by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare; Shri Rajat Kumar Mishra, Secretary, Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers; Shri Tejveer Singh, Secretary, Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers; Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR); Dr. Lovneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (Dte.GHS) and Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, National Health Authority (NHA) along with other senior officers and officials of both the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers.

The pledge-taking ceremony reaffirmed the collective commitment of officers and officials towards upholding the unity, integrity and security of the nation. Rashtriya Ekta Diwas is observed every year on 31st October to honour the legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and reiterate the importance of national unity and solidarity.

The observance served as an occasion to renew the commitment to the ideals of unity, integrity and national cohesion, which continue to guide the country's journey towards a developed and united India.

*****

SR

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Prime Minister visits CCIC Pavilion at Bharat Parv 2026 in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
CCIC Showcases India’s Rich Handloom and Handicraft Heritage, Highlighting Its Efforts to Empower Artisans and Weavers and Promote ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Local to Global’
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 10:48AM by PIB Delhi

Central Cottage Industries Corporation of India Ltd. (CCIC), a Government of India enterprise under the Ministry of Textiles, is participating in the ongoing Bharat Parv 2026 being held at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat. It was a proud and memorable moment for CCIC when the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India visited the CCIC Pavilion on 30 October 2026 at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia. The visit provided an opportunity for CCIC to showcase its rich legacy, its longstanding association with artisans & weavers, and its continued efforts towards promoting India’s traditional handloom and handicraft heritage.

CCIC Pavilion presents the Corporation’s journey of empowering artisans and weavers by providing them with better market access and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through its initiatives, CCIC is actively contributing to the vision of “Vocal for Local” and taking “Local to Global”, by connecting India’s traditional craftsmanship with wider domestic and international markets.

Shri Bimal Gopalachari, Managing Director, CCIC, along with officials of the Corporation, artisans and weavers, were present at the Pavilion. The Pavilion showcases the exceptional skills and craftsmanship of artisans from different parts of the country, including artisans from Gujarat demonstrating traditional artwork using Agate stones and semi-precious stones and intricate Appliqué work.

CCIC is celebrates the rich and diverse heritage of Indian handloom and handicrafts, bringing together exceptional artistry, creativity and craftsmanship from across the country and showcases a wide range of traditional and handcrafted products that reflect India’s vibrant cultural legacy and the timeless beauty of its indigenous art forms.

The exhibition will remain open for visitors up to 15 November 2026 at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, Gujarat

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM congratulates ISRO scientists and engineers on successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi congratulated India's scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03.

The Prime Minister said that the mission marks an important step towards strengthening NavIC, India's indigenous satellite navigation system. Equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further advance India's pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and strengthen navigation services for the benefit of citizens.

Shri Modi lauded the dedication and ingenuity of India's space scientists, stating that their continued achievements make the nation proud.

Shri Modi posted on X:

Congratulations to our scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03.

This mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system. Equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further our pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit our people.

The dedication and ingenuity of our space scientists continue to make our nation proud.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ awarded to 490 personnel of various States/UTs/CAPFs/CPOs for the year 2026
‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ recognizes excellent work, promotes high professional standards and boosts the morale of the concerned officials/officers
Initiated under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ will boost the morale of all police personnel
‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ is announced on 31st of October every year on the occasion of Birth Anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Posted On: 31 OCT 2026 9:55AM by PIB Delhi

The ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ has been awarded to 490 personnel of various States/Union Territories (UTs)/Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)/Central Police Organisations (CPOs) for the year 2026. The medal is given to recognize excellent work, promote high professional standards and boost the morale of the concerned official/officer.

Initiated under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ will boost the morale of all police personnel.

The “Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak” has been instituted vide Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India Notification dated 1st February, 2024. The Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak is conferred on members of the Police Forces, Security Organization, Intelligence Wing/Branch/Special Branch of State/Union Territories/Central Police Organizations(CPOs)/Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)/National Security Guard/Assam Rifles; and Forensic Science (Central/State/Union Territories) throughout the Indian Union in consideration for excellence in Operations, outstanding service in Investigation, exceptional performance, indomitable & daring intelligence service, meritorious work done by Serving Government Scientists in the field of  Forensic Science.

The medal is announced on 31st of October every year, on the occasion of Birth Anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

The list of awardees is available on MHA website - https://www.mha.gov.in
