item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles Highlights Jute Corporation of India’s Extensive Outreach and Cleanliness Activities under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 5:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Textiles appreciates JCI’s dedicated contribution to Special Campaign 6 and its efforts towards achieving the campaign’s objectives of cleanliness, better office management and sustainable governance .The Jute Corporation of India (JCI), under the Ministry of Textiles, has made significant efforts towards the successful implementation of Special Campaign 6, aimed at promoting cleanliness, effective space management, disposal of redundant materials and e-waste, and enhancing overall efficiency in official functioning.

As part of the campaign, JCI undertook various cleanliness and workplace improvement activities, focusing on the systematic management of office spaces, removal of obsolete and unwanted materials, and promotion of a clean, organized and productive working environment. The Corporation also undertook initiatives to strengthen awareness regarding cleanliness, environmental sustainability and responsible waste management.JCI actively contributed to the campaign through various activities and social media outreach, highlighting its commitment to the objectives of Special Campaign 6. These initiatives reflect the Corporation’s continued efforts towards efficient resource utilization, environmental responsibility and the institutionalization of cleanliness practices.

From 2nd to 27 th October 2026 – Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam ,Record Management, Space Management Planning and Scrap Disposal & Cleaning of Record Rooms and Storage Racks

The Jute Corporation of India Limited (JCI) organised the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” plantation drive under the theme of “Swachh Bharat Diwas” and a cleanliness drive was conducted at the office premises


Various activities, including office cleaning, deep cleaning of bathrooms and toilets, beautification of office premises, systematic space management and efficient record management 


Some glimpses of the File Management activities and also Office Desk Cleaning activities:

                                          
JCI undertook extensive cleaning activities included Beautification, Public Area Cleaning& Retting Tank Cleaning at the Office Premises of the Corporation across various locations of the Corporation throughout India. The officials and staff members of JCI actively participated in these activities contributing towards creating cleaner, better organized workplaces.

Some glimpses of the Beautification of Office Premises activities ,Public Area Cleaning activities and also activities conducted at School by Bhadrak are given below:


The activities undertaken, including cleanliness and sanitation drives, plantation programmes, awareness initiatives, beautification of office premises, repair and maintenance works, installation of dustbins, cleaning of public areas and water tanks, systematic record management, digitization of files and disposal of scrap and obsolete materials have contributed towards achieving the objectives of the campaign. The Corporation remains committed to carrying forward these initiatives during the remaining campaign period up to 31st Oct’26 and to sustaining the outcomes achieved through continued efforts towards cleanliness, effective resource management, environmental protection and good governance across all its offices.
The Ministry of Textiles commends the dedicated efforts of the Jute Corporation of India (JCI) and all its officials for their significant contribution to the successful implementation of Special Campaign 6.0, reinforcing the Ministry’s commitment to cleanliness, sustainability, efficient resource management and good governance.

As the Campaign approaches its conclusion on 31 st October, Indian Railways has surpassed several key targets, with significant…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Surpasses Key Targets under Special Campaign 6 Ahead of its Conclusion on 31st October 2026
Rail Jan Samvaad Held at 5,884 Railway Stations for Passenger Feedback on Cleanliness, Passenger Amenities and Service Delivery
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has been actively participating in Special Campaign 6, being implemented from 2nd to 31st October 2026. As the Campaign approaches its conclusion on 31st October, Indian Railways has surpassed several key targets, with significant achievements in cleanliness, scrap disposal, e-waste management, disposal of pending matters and process simplification contributing in a major way in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM-6).

As a major public-centric initiative, Rail Jan Samvaad was organised on 22nd October 2026 at 5,884 railway stations across the country to facilitate direct interaction with passengers and obtain their feedback and suggestions on cleanliness, passenger amenities and service delivery. The Chairman & CEO, Railway Board, Shri Satish Kumar, interacted with stakeholders at New Delhi, while Secretary, DARPG, participated in the programme at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai. The initiative provided an opportunity to identify local issues and take suitable follow-up action for improving passenger services.

With Special Campaign 6 scheduled to conclude on 31st October 2026, Indian Railways continues to focus on consolidating the achievements and sustaining the best practices adopted during the Campaign, with emphasis on cleanliness, efficient management of resources, timely disposal of pending matters and improved passenger services.

***

 Dharmendra Tewari/Dr Nayan Solanki/Vikas Jha

item.description: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Additional Secretary, MoSJE Smt Mona K Khandhar Visits Government Drug Rehabilitation Centre, Raiwala, Uttarakhand Centre Promotes Recovery with Care, Respect and Dignity Promotes A Holistic, Dignity-Centred Approach Combining Medical Care, Counselling, Wellness Activities And Resident Participation Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi The Government Drug Rehabilitation Centre at Raiwala, Uttarakhand, is promoting a holistic, dignity-centred approach to drug rehabilitation by combining medical…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Additional Secretary, MoSJE Smt Mona K Khandhar Visits Government Drug Rehabilitation Centre, Raiwala, Uttarakhand
Centre Promotes Recovery with Care, Respect and Dignity
Promotes A Holistic, Dignity-Centred Approach Combining Medical Care, Counselling, Wellness Activities And Resident Participation
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Government Drug Rehabilitation Centre at Raiwala, Uttarakhand, is promoting a holistic, dignity-centred approach to drug rehabilitation by combining medical care, professional counselling, structured daily routines and wellness activities to support residents on their journey towards recovery.

Additional Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, Smt Mona K Khandhar, visited the Centre, managed by the Society for Promotion of Youth and Masses (SPYM), and interacted with the residents to understand their experiences and learn about the rehabilitation programme being implemented at the facility.

During the visit, Smt Khandhar expressed her intention to engage with the Ministry of AYUSH to explore the integration of appropriate traditional wellness practices, including yoga and naturopathy, into drug rehabilitation programmes.

She said the experience at the Raiwala centre could serve as a starting point for exploring pilot projects in collaboration with the Ministry of AYUSH adding the proposed initiative could examine how yoga, meditation, naturopathy and other suitable wellness practices may complement evidence-based medical treatment and professional counselling under appropriate clinical supervision.

The Additional Secretary said the proposed projects would require structured planning, documentation and evaluation to assess the safety, acceptability and potential benefits of these interventions. Medical professionals, AYUSH practitioners, mental health experts, research institutions and rehabilitation specialists could contribute to developing suitable protocols and quality standards, she added.

Smt Khandhar said subject to the findings of such assessments and the approval of the concerned ministries, successful practices could be considered for adaptation at other government-supported drug rehabilitation Centres across the country.

She said recovery is a gradual process built through small but significant steps, including healthier routines, open communication, restored confidence and preparation for a return to family and community life.

The Addl Secretary said the experience at the Government Drug Rehabilitation Centre, Raiwala, offers an opportunity to examine how professional treatment, psychological support, appropriate wellness activities and compassionate care can work together to support recovery.

With careful documentation, scientific evaluation and institutional collaboration, the initiatives at Raiwala could contribute to wider learning on strengthening drug rehabilitation services across India, she added.

Smt Mona noted that every person deserves care, respect, patience and an opportunity to rebuild their life.

Ms. Mona Kandhar's heard residents' experiences and took note of the initiatives being undertaken at the Raiwala Centre.

Smt Khandhar underlined the importance of transparent institutional practices, qualified professionals, effective grievance-redressal systems and safeguards against abuse. Rehabilitation facilities must provide safe, professional and humane care, ensuring that individuals seeking treatment are protected from violence, intimidation and humiliation, she said.

Smt Khandhar proposed engagement with the Ministry of AYUSH that could open avenues for dialogue on integrating appropriate traditional wellness practices into rehabilitation services. Documenting the programme and evaluating selected interventions through carefully designed pilot projects could help the concerned ministries determine their suitability for wider application, she said.

She said such collaboration could also contribute to common guidelines, staff training, resident participation and quality standards, while ensuring that evidence-based medical care remains central to treatment.

Executive Director of Society for Promotion of Youth and Masses (SPYM) Dr. Rajesh Kumar said the residents shared their experiences of participating in daily activities and explained how structured routines, wellness practices and a supportive environment had become part of their recovery journey. He said the interaction highlighted the importance of addressing not only substance dependence but also the physical, psychological and social challenges associated with recovery.

Dr. Kumar informed that the Centre incorporates wellness activities such as Yoga, Yoga Nidra, Acupressure, Massage, Mud Therapy And Epsom Salt Therapy as part of its broader rehabilitation environment. These activities helped them manage stress, maintain healthier routines and improve their overall sense of well-being, the official said.

The Executive Director said these practices are intended to complement, rather than replace, appropriate medical treatment, professional counselling and clinically supervised withdrawal management adding their safety and effectiveness in supporting recovery would require systematic assessment and evaluation.

He said the approach seeks to address the overall well-being of residents by combining professional support with structured activities that encourage healthy habits, emotional resilience and renewed self-confidence.

Dr Kumar said at the Raiwala Centre, the residents are encouraged to participate in daily routines, share their concerns and contribute to group activities. He added that participation in maintaining their surroundings, supporting fellow residents and undertaking shared responsibilities helps foster a sense of belonging and mutual respect.

Executive Director said the residents are also encouraged to express their preferences regarding daily routines, food, menus and recreational activities. Shared meals and group interactions provide opportunities to build relationships and strengthen community bonds, he added.

The SPYM Official further said the approach recognizes that rehabilitation must be rooted in respect for individual dignity, patience and compassionate care. Giving residents a voice in their rehabilitation helps to create a supportive environment that encourages meaningful participation in the recovery process, he said.

The Raiwala centre's experience presents an opportunity to explore how medical treatment, counselling, wellness activities and resident participation can be brought together within a structured rehabilitation programme.

Further strengthening of such services could include individualized rehabilitation plans, regular resident feedback, confidential grievance-redressal mechanisms, greater family involvement, discharge planning, community reintegration and follow-up support after residents leave the facility. Training for staff in professional, compassionate and safe care would also be important.

Systematic monitoring and independent evaluation could help assess treatment engagement, psychological well-being and longer-term recovery outcomes. Such evidence would be essential before recommending wider adoption of particular wellness interventions or rehabilitation practices.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INS TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT CIVITAVECCHIA, ITALY
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Trishul concluded her port call at Civitavecchia, Italy, on 28 Oct 2026, as part of her ongoing operational deployment in the Mediterranean Sea. The port call provided an opportunity to further strengthen maritime engagement between the Indian Navy and the Italian Navy through professional interactions, cross-deck visits and cultural exchanges.

During her stay, INS Trishul undertook a series of professional and cultural interactions with Italian counterparts. The ship was also opened to visitors, attracting a large number of enthusiastic members of the Indian diaspora and the local populace.

As part of the professional interactions, the Commanding Officer of INS Trishul called on the Fleet Commander of the Italian Navy. The ship’s crew also visited the Italian Navy’s aircraft carrier ITS Cavour at Civitavecchia. These engagements provided opportunities for professional interaction and an exchange of experiences between the two navies.

H.E. Ms Vani Rao, Ambassador of India to Italy, and Vice Admiral Aurelio De Carolis, Fleet Commander and CINCNAV, Italian Navy, visited INS Trishul and interacted with the ship’s crew. They also attended a cultural event hosted onboard, which brought together the Mayor of Civitavecchia, senior officers of the Italian Navy and Coast Guard, Defence Envoys from 13 nations, civil dignitaries and members of the Indian diaspora. The event provided a platform for interaction among naval representatives, diplomatic officials and members of the wider community, further complementing the professional engagements during the port call.

The port call reflected the enduring maritime partnership between India and Italy and the importance of sustained naval engagement in fostering mutual understanding and professional ties. INS Trishul has now proceeded for the next phase of her operational deployment in the Mediterranean Sea.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across Kachchh area including Gandhidham & Bhuj cities and Bhuj to Bachau highway (in Gujarat LSA)during the month of September 2026
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Kachchh area including Gandhidham & Bhuj cities and Bhuj to Bachau highway (in Gujarat LSA), during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Packet loss rate, data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests including City drive – 245.2 KMs,  Hotspot locations – 09 & Bhuj to Bachau highway -75.7 KMs across Kachchh area including Gandhidham & Bhuj cities and Bhuj to Bachau highway during 8th September to 11th September 2026 in Gujarat LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Jaipur. The observations presented in the drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate.

The overall mobile network performance in Kachchh area including Gandhidham & Bhuj cities  and Bhuj to Bachau highway in Gujarat  LSA for the key parameters has been summarised below:

  1. Kachchh area including Gandhidham & Bhuj cities :
  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 242/56687 for Airtel, 575/56051 for BSNL, 290/55391 for RJIL and 245/56876 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/496 for Airtel, 10/496 for BSNL, 3/495 for RJIL and 0/499 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  3. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/460 for Airtel, 6/459 for BSNL, 7/462 for RJIL and 2/476 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  4. Packet Loss rate (Downlink & Uplink): ​​​​​​​

i. Packet Loss rate (Downlink): Downlink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 0.17 %, for BSNL as 1.52%, for RJIL as 0.93%  and  for VIL as 0.42%.

ii. Packet Loss rate (uplink): Uplink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 0.22%, for BSNL as 2.40%, for RJIL as 0.79%  and  for VIL as 0.39 %.

  1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
  1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 177.25 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 10.27 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 231.92 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 31.68 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 34.26 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 7.32 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 29.44 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 16.86 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

 

  1. Bhuj to Bhachau  Highway :

f. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 202/11015 for Airtel, 1718/10423 for BSNL, 187/10902 for RJIL and 164/11198 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

g. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/54 for Airtel, 7/56 for BSNL, 0/54 for RJIL and 1/55 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

h. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/53 for Airtel, 0/61 for BSNL, 1/52 for RJIL and 1/55 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

  1. Packet Loss rate (Downlink & Uplink):

v. Packet Loss rate (Downlink): Downlink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 0.50 %, for BSNL as 3.88%, for RJIL as 0.98%  and  for VIL as 1.11%.

vi. Packet Loss rate (uplink): Uplink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 0.43%, for BSNL as 4.19%, for RJIL as 0.65%  and  for VIL as 1.12%.

 

  1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
  1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 139.15 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 10.66 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 241.22 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 22.97 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 17.68 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 3.80 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 19.41 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 13.80 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as under: -

City: Sukhpar, Uma Nagar, Airport Ring Road, Sanskar Nagar, Din Dayal Nagar, Junavas, Somiya Nagar, Anjar, Jalaram Nagar, Bharat Nagar, Gandhidham, Vinayak Society, Kandla, Mundra etc. in  Kachchh area including Gandhidham & Bhuj.

Highway Route - Bhuj to Bhachau via Danda Bazar, Bhuj-Bhachau Highway, Padhar, Kaniyabe, Budharmora, Amardi, Kumbhardi, Euro Colony, Madina Nagar etc.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end, if required. Detailed report of IDT is made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to Regional office of TRAI at Jaipur on Email id adv.jaipur@trai.gov.in Regional Office of TRAI at Jaipur RO can be contacted on telephone no.  0141-2701919.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
 DRDO Undertakes Special Campaign 6.0 to Expedite Disposal of Pending Matters
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has rolled out Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM 6.0) across its headquarters, laboratories and establishments. Coordinated by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the campaign focuses on reducing pendency, expediting public grievance redressal, digitising records, improving cleanliness and optimising workspace.

DRDO has achieved 100 per cent of its targets for clearing pending public grievances, Parliamentary Assurances and inter-ministerial references. Around 20,000 files earmarked for weeding out are being disposed of as per record retention schedules, with shredded paper sent to the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) for recycling. Approximately 5 lakh historical pages and records have also been digitised to enhance administrative transparency.

Cleanliness and space optimisation drives are underway across DRDO campuses, residential complexes and research testing ranges, with obsolete equipment, redundant furniture and scrap materials being cleared. The eco-friendly disposal of scrap and obsolete hardware has generated ₹35 lakh in revenue.

***

item.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Quality, Scale and Global Market Access to Drive India’s Industrial Transformation
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Quality, Scale and Global Market Access to Drive India’s Industrial Transformation Comprehensive Trade Agreements to Strengthen India’s Global Integration While Safeguarding National Interests: Shri Goyal Global Demand for Indian Talent Growing, Outlines India’s Clean Energy Goals: Shri Goyal Shri Goyal Calls for Industry-Academia Collaboration to Drive Innovation and Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing Startup, Semiconductor and Space Sector to be Growth Drivers of India’s Industrial Transformation: Shri…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Quality, Scale and Global Market Access to Drive India’s Industrial Transformation
Comprehensive Trade Agreements to Strengthen India’s Global Integration While Safeguarding National Interests: Shri Goyal
Global Demand for Indian Talent Growing, Outlines India’s Clean Energy Goals: Shri Goyal
Shri Goyal Calls for Industry-Academia Collaboration to Drive Innovation and Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing
Startup, Semiconductor and Space Sector to be Growth Drivers of India’s Industrial Transformation: Shri Goyal
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal has said that India’s industrial transformation must be driven by quality, economies of scale, global market access and inclusivity, with innovation emerging from collaboration among the government, private sector and academia. Addressing the Fourth National Conference on India’s Industrial Transformation, organised by the ISID and IDRA, Minister said that India must aim to become a globally recognised manufacturing nation.

Shri Goyal identified quality, global market access, economies of scale and inclusivity as four key differentiators that could accelerate the transformation of India’s industrial landscape. He said that quality was the most important priority, reiterating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s emphasis on “Zero Defect, Zero Effect”. With markets opening across the world through free trade agreements, India must compete for market share, expand its global presence and leverage preferential market access. The scale of India’s domestic market of 1.4 billion people, combined with access to international markets, could enable manufacturers to achieve affordability and competitive production costs. He added that sustainable and inclusive growth to ensure wider prosperity for all Indians.

Shri Goyal said that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 was a collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians and called for coordinated efforts across government, industry, academia and research institutions to achieve this objective. He said that the country must draw lessons from its economic history, assess its present position realistically and develop an agenda for the future. Emphasising the importance of intergenerational collaboration, he observed that the experience of senior professionals and the energy of young people must come together to address contemporary challenges, rather than working in silos.

On India’s trade policy, Shri Goyal said that the country’s trade agreements were not limited to reducing tariffs, framing rules of origin or securing market access. They were comprehensive partnerships that considered India’s competitive strengths, identified opportunities for exports, protected sensitive sectors and facilitated access to high-technology products, graphics processing units (GPUs), memory technology, medical technology and other goods required for India’s development.

He said that India’s trade negotiations also encompassed services, investments, education, skill development, technology partnerships and cooperation towards climate goals and countries’ intended nationally determined contributions. These comprehensive agreements were laying the foundation for India’s integration with the global economy while protecting its sensitivities and defensive interests through extensive stakeholder consultations before an agreement was concluded.

Referring to the India-US trade deal negotiations, Shri Goyal expressed confidence that when the details of the deal are released, the people of India will recognise that the sensitive interests of farmers and other stakeholders have not been compromised and that India will be placed at a strong comparative advantage.

Shri Goyal explained that trade was fundamentally about comparative advantage and competitiveness, rather than absolute numbers alone. He observed that many developed countries had structured their tariff schedules to impose high duties on labour-intensive goods, using them as negotiating instruments.

He said that India’s trade agreements covered 38 developed and relatively prosperous countries, creating complementary trade opportunities for both sides, with India exporting products they needed and importing products required for its development. He described these as win-win partnerships and emphasised that effective agreements should be fair, equitable and balanced.

Shri Goyal stated that the nine free trade and bilateral trade agreements concluded by the Government had opened up preferential market opportunities in economies with an aggregate GDP of USD 60 trillion, compared with USD 10 trillion covered by agreements concluded before 2014. He said that the earlier agreements were largely with countries competing with India, whereas the current approach sought to foster complementary economic relationships.

He also highlighted the growing international recognition of Indian talent and skills. Recalling a conversation with the German Foreign Minister regarding the migration agreement between India and Germany and the requirement for 90,000 Indians annually, Shri Goyal said that he was told Germany needed substantially more Indian talent. He cited the presence of Indian professionals in senior positions at Fortune 500 companies and among developers of cutting-edge technologies as evidence of the capabilities of India’s workforce.

The Minister expressed confidence that India would continue to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy for another 20 to 25 years, attributing this prospect to the talent, skills and energy of its people.

Shri Goyal stressed that climate action must be guided by the principles of polluter pays and common but differentiated responsibilities, with adequate financial and technological support for developing countries. He highlighted that 60 per cent of India’s installed electricity capacity came from green and renewable sources, while coal remained essential for energy security and affordable power.

Shri Goyal highlighted that India has moved from being predominantly a buyer of products manufactured elsewhere to becoming a country increasingly recognised for manufacturing. The Minister added that the Make in India initiative and phased manufacturing programmes across different sectors had helped bring factories to India and increase domestic production. He said that India would continue to manufacture a growing share of its requirements domestically.

Shri Goyal emphasised that innovation would be central to industrial transformation. Public institutions, private enterprises and academia would need to work together, with the government acting primarily as a facilitator and catalyst for private-sector-led innovation. He highlighted the scientific knowledge, discoveries and research capabilities available in IITs, engineering colleges and other institutions of higher learning and science.

Citing the Startup Fund of Funds, he said that the first fund had been fully utilised and that the second fund was now in place. He also referred to the Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) in India and said that these initiatives had contributed to the development of India’s startup ecosystem, making it the world’s third-largest.

Shri Goyal also highlighted the opening of the space sector to private participation. He said that India’s space economy, valued at USD 8.4 billion at the time of his address, had the potential to reach USD 44 billion by 2033. He observed that international partners were increasingly interested in collaboration with India in space, artificial intelligence, computing and startups.

Referring to his recent visit to Germany, Shri Goyal said that German research institutions, some employing twelve to thirty thousand people, were working closely with the private sector and have expressed interest in collaborating with India. He attributed this growing interest to the trust in partnership between India and Germany and to the confidence that India offered in terms of talent, skills, fair play and equal opportunity.

The Minister said that the new trade agreements and international relationships being developed under Prime Minister Modi’s leadership were opening opportunities for joint research, technology development and industrial collaboration. He said that these partnerships could help India transform its growth trajectory by combining domestic capabilities with international expertise and investment.

Shri Goyal concluded by commending ISID for organising three days of serious deliberations on India’s industrial future. He reiterated that the country’s industrial transformation would depend on sustained attention to quality, access to global markets, economies of scale and inclusivity, supported by collaboration across manufacturing, innovation and research. He extended his best wishes to the conference and its participants for their contributions towards achieving Viksit Bharat 2047.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported parading of three persons in a semi-nude condition by police in Kolkata, West Bengal
Issues a notice to the Kolkata Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that the police paraded three persons in a semi-nude condition with ropes tied around their waists in Kolkata, West Bengal. A day before the incident, an 18-year-old youth and his 19-year-old friend, who were reportedly seen with a minor girl, were beaten and humiliated by the girl’s family members at her house. The youth’s father, whom the girl’s family summoned, was also assaulted. Subsequently, all three were stripped and forced to walk naked on the road at gunpoint.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Kolkata Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 28th October 2026, the police brought three arrested persons, including the girl’s father, her maternal uncle and his friend, to the same locality and made them walk shirtless and barefoot for over 100 metres purportedly for reconstruction of the crime scene.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
NICSI Undertakes Cleanliness and Pendency Reduction Activities Under Special Campaign 6.0
Campaign Improves Workplace Cleanliness and Hygiene, Frees Space Occupied by Obsolete and Unused Material
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi

National Informatics Centre Services Incorporated (NICSI), a Government of India Enterprise under the National Informatics Centre (NIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), conducted Special Campaign 6.0 for Swachhata and pendency reduction across its establishments in Delhi-NCR.

The campaign focused on promoting workplace cleanliness, removal of obsolete material, optimisation of office space and improvement in record management. It began with a cleanliness pledge by NICSI officers and staff, followed by cleanliness and related activities across its locations.

As part of the campaign, general office cleaning was undertaken at NICSI Headquarters at Bhikaji Cama Place, Delhi. At NICSI Headquarters at WTC, unwanted material was removed and the external area was cleaned.

Indoor and outdoor cleaning, including corridors, common areas and washrooms, was undertaken at NICSI, New Delhi and SPDC, Noida. Office and common areas were cleaned at LNDC, while unwanted items were removed and corridors and washrooms were cleaned at SPDC. Old and unused items were also removed across all locations.

The campaign improved workplace cleanliness and hygiene and freed space occupied by obsolete and unused material.

NICSI will sustain the outcomes of the campaign through regular housekeeping, periodic record review and weeding, and timely disposal of unserviceable assets in accordance with applicable rules.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
ESIC Extends the New Amnesty Scheme 2025 till 31 December 2026: More Time for Employers and Insured Persons to Resolve Pending Cases
Three-Month Extension Reinforces ESIC’s Commitment to Reducing Litigation and Promoting Voluntary Compliance
Posted On: 29 OCT 2026 9:21AM by PIB Delhi

Post review of representations from various stakeholders, the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has extended the ‘New Amnesty Scheme, 2025’ which ran from 01.10.2025 to 30.09.2026, for a further period of three months i.e from 01.10.2026 to 31.12.2026, on existing terms and conditions.

The ‘New Amnesty Scheme 2025’ is a one-time dispute resolution initiative aimed at reducing the backlog of court cases and promoting compliance under the erstwhile ESI Act. The scheme provides a structured mechanism for employers to resolve legal disputes with ESIC for an out-of-court settlement. The scheme allows:

  • Settlement of ad-hoc assessments by paying actual contributions and interest—no damages will be levied.
  • Withdrawal of cases where employers have already paid dues, subject to payment of 10% of disputed damages.
  • Cases filed by ESIC for non-submission of records or delayed payments, which were later complied with, will also be withdrawn with court permission.
  • Court cases filed up to 31.03.2025 are eligible under this scheme.

With the extension of this Scheme, eligible employers and Insured Persons will have additional time to avail themselves of the benefits of the Scheme. All concerned stakeholders are encouraged to make use of the extended window before it closes on 31.12.2026. The details of the scheme can be accessed at [https://esic.gov.in/attachments/publicationfile/Amnesty_Flyer_2025_1762755260.pdf]

The ‘New Amnesty Scheme, 2025’ is a practical and employer-friendly route to dispute resolution and supports the government’s broader goal of enhancing ease of doing business while upholding the rights of citizens served by ESIC.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat Organises ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad: Know Your Vote’ Across 14 States/UTs to Promote Electoral Awareness
Youth Take Loktantrik Pledge to Uphold Democratic Values and Strengthen Civic Participation
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 10:20PM by PIB Delhi

Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, organised editions of Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad: Know Your Vote across educational institutions in 10 States and 4 Union Territories today as part of its nationwide campaign to promote electoral awareness and encourage informed and responsible participation of young people in democracy. The events brought together students, public representatives, Youth Icons, accomplished sportspersons and institutional leaders for discussions on voting rights, civic responsibilities and democratic values.


The nationwide campaign, being conducted across 500 universities, colleges and institutions from 26.10.2026 to 05.11.2026, aims to provide young people, including first-time voters, a platform to interact directly with elected representatives and exchange ideas on democratic participation in the journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047. As of 28 October  a total of 27 Yuva Samvaads have been conducted across the country, with 5,856 young people participating in the programmes.

In the Northern Region, programmes were today held at institutions in Delhi, Gurugram, Panchkula, Rajouri and Jhajjar. At Shri Ram College of Commerce, the event was attended by Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, along with sportspersons Shri Arjun Singh Nagra and Shri Ajeet Yadav. The programme in Panchkula and the event in Sunderbani also saw participation by students and young citizens in large numbers.


In the Central Region, programmes in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh focused on electoral awareness, youth leadership and responsible citizenship. In Sheopur, Member of Parliament Shri Shivmangal Singh Tomar interacted with students on voting rights and the electoral process. In Raigarh, the dialogue was held alongside the Neighbourhood Youth Parliament in the presence of Lok Sabha MP Shri Radheyshyam Rathia and MY Bharat Joint Director Shri Raman Patel.

In the Eastern Region, MY Bharat Darjeeling organised a Youth Samvaad in Phansidewa. The programme featured a presentation on the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD), interactive discussions on ‘Know Your Vote’, a voter-awareness pledge and a Signature Wall reaffirming participants’ commitment to democratic values. Other programmes were held in Bihar and West Bengal.


In the North-Eastern Region, the programme at Rajiv Gandhi University in Arunachal Pradesh featured Youth Icon Porbindar Kaur and Commonwealth and South Asian karate gold medallist Johny Mangkhiya.

In the Southern and Western Regions, programmes brought together students, Youth Icons, sportspersons and invited dignitaries for discussions on electoral processes, civic responsibilities and democratic participation.

The programmes concluded with the administration of the Loktantrik Pledge, through which participants resolved to uphold democratic values and participate actively in the democratic life of the nation. The Know Your Vote online quiz competition, organised by MY Bharat in collaboration with MyGov, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, was also promoted to raise awareness about the electoral process. MY Bharat registrations were facilitated at the venues, and suggestions from participants were collected through QR-based suggestion boxes.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Interacts with Export Promotion Councils, Calls for Greater Export Competitiveness and Market Diversification
Shri Piyush Goyal Reviews Export Scenario with Export Promotion Councils, Emphasises Market Access and Global Competitiveness
Shri Goyal Highlights Government Measures to Facilitate Exports and Address Challenges Faced by Exporters
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 10:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, interacted with representatives of Export Promotion Councils (EPCs) in New Delhi today to review the prevailing export scenario, discuss emerging opportunities and challenges in international trade, and deliberate on measures to further strengthen India’s export competitiveness.

During the interaction, Shri Goyal highlighted the evolving global trade environment, characterised by geopolitical uncertainties, changes in tariff structures, supply chain realignments and emerging regulatory requirements in major international markets. He noted that while these developments pose challenges for exporters, they also present opportunities for India to strengthen its position as a reliable and competitive global trading partner.

Shri Goyal emphasised the need for Indian industry to remain agile and responsive to the changing international business environment. He encouraged exporters to focus on improving product quality, innovation, cost competitiveness, reliability of supply and compliance with international standards to enhance India’s participation in global value chains.

Referring to his recent international engagements, including his visits to Germany and the Netherlands, Shri Goyal highlighted the growing interest in India as a manufacturing, sourcing and investment destination. He stressed the importance of translating these engagements into tangible business outcomes through sustained interaction between Indian industry and overseas businesses. He encouraged EPCs to engage proactively with their international counterparts, identify potential buyers and facilitate business partnerships in established and emerging markets.

The Minister also highlighted the importance of effectively leveraging the opportunities arising from India's expanding network of Free trade agreements and economic partnerships. He emphasised that preferential market access under Free Trade Agreements must translate into increased exports, greater market penetration and wider participation of Indian enterprises in international trade. EPCs were encouraged to undertake sector-specific assessments of export opportunities in partner countries and strengthen awareness among exporters regarding applicable trade preferences, standards and market requirements.

Shri Goyal also emphasised the need for a focused approach towards product and market diversification in response to changing global demand and emerging supply chain opportunities. He encouraged EPCs to identify products with untapped export potential, explore new destinations and develop market-specific strategies. He highlighted the importance of consolidating India’s competitive advantages in established sectors while building capabilities in emerging areas.

Reiterating the Government’s commitment to facilitating exports, the Minister highlighted ongoing efforts to improve ease of doing business, strengthen trade infrastructure and address challenges faced by exporting enterprises. He referred to the Export Promotion Mission as an important initiative for addressing constraints related to export finance, market access and international competitiveness, particularly for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

Highlighting the contribution of MSMEs to India’s export ecosystem, Shri Goyal called upon EPCs to expand their outreach to smaller enterprises, startups, new exporters and businesses in emerging export clusters and districts. He stressed the need for practical handholding support, improved access to market intelligence and greater integration of these enterprises into global markets.

The Minister further encouraged EPCs to adopt a more data-driven and outcome-oriented approach to export promotion. He emphasised the value of timely market intelligence, identification of sector-specific opportunities, monitoring of international trade trends and resolution of operational bottlenecks. He highlighted the need for greater collaboration among EPCs, industry associations, State Governments and field formations of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).

During the interaction, representatives of the Export Promotion Councils also shared their perspectives on the international trading environment and sector-specific issues concerning export competitiveness, market access, logistics, regulatory requirements and trade facilitation. The discussions provided an opportunity to exchange views on addressing exporters’ concerns and strengthening coordination between the Government and industry.

Reaffirming the Government's commitment to maintaining regular engagement with industry stakeholders, the Minister underscored the importance of collective efforts to make Indian products and services globally competitive and strengthen India's reputation as a trusted trading partner.

The interaction reflected the shared commitment of the Government and Export Promotion Councils to work collaboratively towards expanding India's export footprint, harnessing emerging global opportunities and supporting sustainable, broad-based export growth.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ C N Abhijith Narayanan/ Abhimanyu Panwar

item.title: Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi releases ₹1,000 Crore Margin Money Subsidy under PMEGP to support 11,333 new Micro Enterprises across India
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
item.description: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi releases ₹1,000 Crore Margin Money Subsidy under PMEGP to support 11,333 new Micro Enterprises across India Landmark PMEGP support facilitates Bank Credit of ₹3,260 Crore, generates over 1.02 lakh sustainable employment opportunities and promotes Inclusive Entrepreneurship in rural India Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, achieved another significant milestone in promoting…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi releases ₹1,000 Crore Margin Money Subsidy under PMEGP to support 11,333 new Micro Enterprises across India
Landmark PMEGP support facilitates Bank Credit of ₹3,260 Crore, generates over 1.02 lakh sustainable employment opportunities and promotes Inclusive Entrepreneurship in rural India
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, achieved another significant milestone in promoting self-employment and grassroots entrepreneurship with the release of ₹1,000 crore in Margin Money (MM) subsidy under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP).

The subsidy was released by Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME, during a special function organised by the Ministry at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. The event was graced by Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State for MSME; Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME; other senior officials from the Ministry, CEO,Khadi and Village Industries Commission, CMD National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), and the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME).

PMEGP is one of the flagship credit-linked subsidy programmes of the Government of India aimed at creating sustainable self-employment opportunities through establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. The scheme administered by the Ministry of MSME is implemented nationally by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), with support from other designated implementing agencies such as KVIBs, District Industries Centres and Coir Board. Under the scheme, aspiring entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance in the form of MM subsidy on bank-sanctioned project loans for setting up new micro-enterprises. Awareness generation, handholding, capacity building, market linkages, monitoring and post-establishment support is also provided by KVIC field offices and Implementing Agencies at the grassroot level to promote long-term enterprise sustainability and growth. The programme plays a vital role in promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening local economies, and generating sustainable employment opportunities, particularly in rural and underserved regions of the country.

PMEGP's Transformational Impact since 2014-15

PMEGP has emerged as one of the country's most successful employment generation programmes. Since FY 2014-15, PMEGP has facilitated the establishment of more than 8.38 lakh micro enterprises through bank-sanctioned loans exceeding ₹ 70,000 crore and MM subsidy of over ₹ 25,193 crore, resulting in the generation of approximately 75 lakh sustainable employment opportunities across the country.

The achievements of PMEGP also reflect its strong commitment to inclusive and equitable development. Nearly 80% of the assisted units have been established in rural areas. Further, nearly 50% of the beneficiaries belong to SC, ST and OBC categories, while around 40% of the enterprises are owned by women entrepreneurs, demonstrating the scheme's pivotal role in fostering social inclusion, women-led development, and empowerment of disadvantaged sections of society.

₹1,000 Crore Subsidy to Benefit 11,333 Entrepreneurs to Date

The release of ₹ 1,000 crore MM subsidy will facilitate support to 11,333 beneficiaries under PMEGP. These beneficiaries have received bank-sanctioned project loans amounting to approximately ₹ 3,260 crore for setting up new micro-enterprises across various sectors.

The enterprises being established under this tranche are expected to generate more than 1.02 lakh sustainable employment opportunities, primarily in rural areas across the country. The assistance is strategically targeted to advance Women-led entrepreneurship and gender-inclusive growth; socially inclusive development, particularly among SC and ST communities; and balanced regional development, with a special focus on the North Eastern Region (NER) and Aspirational Districts.

Strong Performance During FY 2026-27

Prior to this release, during FY 2026-27, PMEGP had already supported 25,895 micro enterprises with MM subsidy amounting to ₹ 794.52 crore to October 2026. With the release of the present ₹ 1,000 crore subsidy tranche, the scheme is expected to further accelerate entrepreneurship development and employment generation across the country, strengthening the Government's vision of building a self-reliant, inclusive, and employment-oriented economy.

Speaking on the occasion, the Union Minister emphasized the critical role of micro enterprises in driving economic growth, fostering innovation, and generating livelihoods at the grassroots level. He reiterated the Government's commitment to ensuring that aspiring entrepreneurs, particularly those from rural areas, women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and economically weaker sections, receive adequate institutional support to transform their entrepreneurial aspirations into successful enterprises.

The Ministry of MSME remains committed to expanding the reach of PMEGP and strengthening the entrepreneurship ecosystem to create sustainable livelihoods, promote local manufacturing and services, and contribute significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat through inclusive and broad-based economic development.

***

Sunil Kumar Tiwari

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs 54th PRAGATI Meeting
PM reviews infrastructure projects worth over ₹16,000 crore across 31 States and UTs
PM calls for faster redevelopment of major railway stations as multimodal transport hubs
PM emphasizes the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs
PM asks Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to improve welfare delivery
PM says focus should be on outcomes rather than on outlays to improve citizens’ lives
PM calls for linking Ekta malls with tourism and local businesses
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes.

During the meeting, Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks covering 31 States/ UTs and costing more than 16 thousand crores. These projects, pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, were reviewed with a focus on timelines, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution.

Prime Minister underlined that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen the livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises. He called for linking the malls with tourism and local businesses, noting that increased demand could create employment in rural production, packaging, storage and transportation. He stressed on review of progress regularly by Chief Secretaries and to ensure timely completion of the malls.

Reviewing Bulk Drug Parks in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, Prime Minister stressed the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs to strengthen self-reliance.

Prime Minister asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to address implementation gaps and ensure that benefits reach eligible beneficiaries on time. He emphasised that governance must focus on outcomes over outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Referring to the Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks Programmes, he highlighted the role of convergence, regular monitoring and local accountability in accelerating development in underserved areas. He noted that sustained efforts to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of welfare schemes had helped nearly 25 crore people move out of multidimensional poverty.

During the review of the redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station, PM called for expediting the redevelopment of major railway stations across the country to improve passenger convenience and ease of travel. He emphasised that redeveloped stations should serve as multimodal transport hubs, with seamless connectivity to metro and other transport networks.

Prime Minister asked  the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule.

item.title: India’s Cultural Consciousness and Knowledge Traditions Form the Foundation of Its Civilisational Continuity: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Culture
item.description: Ministry of Culture India’s Cultural Consciousness and Knowledge Traditions Form the Foundation of Its Civilisational Continuity: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Book ‘Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’ launched in collaboration with IGNCA and ASI Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi Highlighting the preservation of India’s cultural identity, the revival of monuments and the discourse on the nation’s historical memory, the book Timeless India: Protection & Revival…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
India’s Cultural Consciousness and Knowledge Traditions Form the Foundation of Its Civilisational Continuity: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
Book ‘Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’ launched in collaboration with IGNCA and ASI
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

Highlighting the preservation of India’s cultural identity, the revival of monuments and the discourse on the nation’s historical memory, the book Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi was launched on today through a collaboration between the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA). The book has been published by IGNCA and Subhi Publications and edited by Tarun Vijay. The event was held at Dharohar Bhawan, ASI, Mandi House, New Delhi, with Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat as the Chief Guest. Dr. Jitendra Singh, Minister of State for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, attended as the Guest of Honour. Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, former Rajya Sabha Member and former President of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), delivered the keynote address. The session was chaired by cultural thinker Dr. Anil Goyal.

The welcome address was delivered by Shri Y. S. Rawat, Director General, Archaeological Survey of India. The inaugural address was delivered by Prof. (Dr.) Ramesh C. Gaur, Dean, School of Arts, Media and Design, South Asian University. Shri Tarun Vijay, author and editor of the book, noted journalist and former Rajya Sabha Member, spoke about the book’s content and objectives. The vote of thanks was delivered by Prof. K. Anil Kumar, Head of the Kala Nidhi Division, IGNCA.

Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries, but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, spiritual practice, struggle and experience. India’s civilisation and cultural consciousness have flowed uninterrupted through the centuries. India has established connections with civilisations across the world through dialogue and cultural exchange. Its knowledge traditions, architectural heritage and cultural legacy have attracted countries across the world.

He said that during colonial rule, efforts were made to weaken Indians’ sense of pride in their civilisation, culture and traditions. This also influenced the way Indians viewed their own knowledge traditions and cultural ideals. The distinctive feature of Indian civilisation is its ability to draw inspiration from the past while moving towards the future. Ideals represented by Lord Rama and Lord Krishna, along with the traditions of sages, thinkers and seekers of knowledge, remain important foundations of India’s cultural consciousness.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the book and commended its editor, cultural thinker, author and senior journalist Shri Tarun Vijay, for bringing out a significant publication that highlights the importance of preserving and revitalising India’s cultural identity.

Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe said that understanding India’s ancient culture and its timeless journey requires an awareness of, and pride in, its cultural heritage. He observed that, for a long time after Independence, there had been an unnecessary hesitation in speaking openly about Indian culture, making it difficult to break completely free from the colonial mindset. Books such as Timeless India provide an opportunity to understand India’s cultural continuity and the essence of Indianness.

Referring to Mark Tully’s book No Full Stops in India, he drew attention to a distinctive characteristic of the Indian mind. He said that the Indian mind does not seek to undermine the faith of ordinary people, but rather to understand their beliefs and lived experiences. The journey of Indian civilisation has been one of continuity, dialogue and change, and cannot be confined to a single conclusion or a limited perspective.

He emphasised that alongside publishing and preserving books, it is equally important to encourage the habit of reading. Indian culture should not remain confined to books but should become part of education and everyday life. He stressed the need to promote education in the mother tongue and to bring content related to Indian life and culture to students. He added that understanding India’s timeless cultural journey from an appropriate perspective and freeing the education system from colonial influences are important needs of the present time.

Dr. Anil Goyal while delivering his chair remarks  said that India is an ancient civilisation and a cultural consciousness shaped by a living tradition that has flowed for thousands of years. Despite numerous invasions and changes, India’s cultural spirit remains alive. Its temples, stupas, forts, sculptures and inscriptions are not merely historical monuments, but testimonies to the knowledge, art, science, faith and philosophy of its ancestors. He said that preserving heritage is a responsibility towards national identity, cultural continuity and future generations.

He emphasised the need to understand Indian history through facts and evidence and to bring forgotten achievements to light. Stressing the importance of understanding cultural heritage free from colonial influences, he said that a country should be assessed through parameters that reflect its social and cultural realities. Development and heritage, modernity and tradition, and science and culture are not contradictory but complementary. Books such as Timeless India play an important role in broadening understanding of India’s civilisational continuity and cultural heritage.

On the occasion, scholars, historians and intellectuals highlighted the importance of India’s civilisational continuity, cultural heritage and the preservation of its historical legacy through Timeless India.

A Book Focused on Monument Preservation and Cultural Memory

Timeless India explores the role of monuments in preserving and revitalising India’s cultural identity, alongside the discourse surrounding the nation’s historical memory. The title points to India’s cultural continuity, which remains evident through different historical periods, architectural traditions and forms of cultural heritage.

The book gives particular importance to monument preservation and the idea of “decolonising the nation’s memory”. This perspective highlights the need to understand India’s cultural heritage through its own historical experiences, traditions and cultural outlook.

The launch presented the publication as an important initiative towards preserving Indian cultural heritage and broadening the discourse around it. The event also provided an opportunity to advance dialogue on culture, history, archaeology and cultural studies.

***

M Annadurai

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Three-Day Workshop on Telugu Ayurvedic Manuscripts Transcription and Editing Concludes at CCRAS-NIIMH, Hyderabad
2,040 folios across 30 Telugu Ayurveda manuscripts transcribed, proofread and edited during the workshop
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 8:51PM by PIB Delhi

A three-day workshop on ‘Telugu Ayurvedic Manuscripts Transcription and Editing’ concluded today at the auditorium of the National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), Hyderabad. Organised from October 26 to 28, 2026, the workshop focused on developing specialised skills for deciphering, transcribing, analysing and critically editing ancient medical knowledge preserved in historical Telugu palm-leaf and paper manuscripts.

The workshop was organised under the guidance of Padmashree Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr Koustubha Upadhaya, Advisor (Ayu), Ministry of Ayush. It was conducted under the aegis of the Centre of Excellence in Medico-Historical Studies and Indian Medical Heritage, functioning under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)–National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), Hyderabad, Ministry of Ayush.

Designed as an initiative for capacity building and human resource development, the workshop aimed to equip researchers and scholars with specialised skills required for the systematic study and preservation of India's medical heritage.

During the inaugural session, Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS, underscored the importance of such workshops and outlined the Council's ongoing research initiatives and projects dedicated to preserving Indian medical heritage. Dr N. Srikanth, Deputy Director General, CCRAS, emphasised the need to uncover and bring to light the immense therapeutic wisdom preserved in ancient medical palm-leaf texts.

Dr G.P. Prasad, Assistant Director In-charge, CCRAS-NIIMH, outlined the core objectives of the workshop and presented the strategic roadmap for manuscript transcription. The inaugural function was attended by distinguished scholars, including Dr B. Ramarao, Former Director, National Ayurveda Research Institute for Panchakarma (NARIP), and Uttama Vaidya Pammi Satyanarayana Sastry, who participated as Guests of Honour.

The three-day programme featured intensive hands-on practical training and expert technical sessions conducted by distinguished scholars, including Shri Narasimha, Conservator, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) Library, Tirupati; Shri P.V.S. Kumar, Indic Manuscriptology Expert; and Uttama Vaidya Pammi Satyanarayana Sastry, Manuscriptology and Literary Expert.

Over 37 delegates, faculty members and postgraduate scholars participated in the practical sessions. The participants represented premier institutions, including S.V. Ayurvedic College, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh; Rajarajeshwari Ayurveda Medical College, Humnabad, Bidar, Karnataka; and Basavaraj Patil Ayurveda College, Bidar, alongside research scholars and officers from CCRAS.

The workshop concluded with a valedictory session on the afternoon of October 28, 2026. Over the three days, participants gained extensive knowledge of palaeography, including manuscript deciphering, transliteration, editing, proofreading, text-critical analysis and script variants.

Under the expert guidance of renowned scholars, the workshop achieved a significant milestone with the completion of transcription, primary proofreading and editing of 2,040 folios across 30 Telugu Ayurveda manuscripts, contributing to efforts to preserve and systematically document India's traditional medical knowledge.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
GeM Samvad 2026 Highlights Reforms to Improve Public Procurement Access and Affordability for MSEs
GeM–LUB Partnership Facilitates 108 Virtual Conferences to Expand MSME Access to Government Procurement Opportunities
GeM Reduces Transaction Charges to 0.30%, Raises Exemption Threshold to ₹10 Lakh and Cuts OEM Assessment Fees by Up to 92%
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 8:50PM by PIB Delhi

Government e Marketplace (GeM), in collaboration with Laghu Udyog Bharati (LUB), organised an event as part of GeM Samvad 2026 , highlighting key reforms aimed at making public procurement more accessible and affordable for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs).

Formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in 2024, the GeM–LUB partnership has facilitated 108 virtual conferences, apart from numerous physical events across India, to build awareness, support digital onboarding and help MSMEs navigate the platform and access government procurement opportunities.

In his address, CEO, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar, stated that reforms undertaken by GeM have helped MSMEs by reducing participation costs, simplifying processes and improving access to finance, enabling them to participate more confidently in government procurement and contribute to the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047. He further stated that GeM endeavours to build a Trusted Seller ecosystem where business opportunities are completely democratised in digital format.

GeM has reduced transaction charges from 0.50% to 0.30% of the order value. Orders up to ₹10 lakh are exempt from transaction charges, compared with the earlier threshold of ₹5 lakh. For orders above ₹10 crore, charges are capped at ₹3 lakh, compared with the earlier maximum of ₹72.50 lakh. Nearly 97% of orders placed on GeM attract no transaction charges. The requirement for a Caution Money deposit as part of the onboarding process was also dispensed with in July 2025. Moreover, vendor assessment charges applicable to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) have been reduced by 66% to 92% since January 2024.

As part of the event, President, LUB, Shri Madhusudan Dadu; National General Secretary, LUB, Shri Om Prakash Gupta; National Treasurer, LUB and GeM Nodal, Shri Janak Bhatia; and Additional CEO, GeM, Shri Ajit B. Chavan, participated in the deliberations and interacted with the MSMEs attending the event.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ajit B. Chavan highlighted that, in line with the Union Budget 2026–27 announcement, GeM has integrated with all five Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) exchanges. He stated that this enablement, coupled with GeM SAHAY’s collateral-free lending against purchase orders on GeM, would go a long way in addressing the working capital and timely payment challenges faced by MSMEs.

President, LUB, Shri Madhusudan Dadu and National General Secretary, LUB, Shri Om Prakash Gupta outlined LUB’s plans to further deepen collaborative efforts with GeM and enhance outreach to MSMEs through LUB’s pan-India network of offices, regular weekly GeM–LUB virtual conferences and the setting up of dedicated facilitation counters at various offices, staffed by trained volunteers.

 

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Shabbir Azad / Ishita Biswas

item.description: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals Special Campaign 6.0: Department of Pharmaceuticals Focuses on E-Waste Management, Cleanliness, and Efficient Space Utilization; 14,700 cleanliness drives conducted, 2,200 sq. ft. of office space freed up, ₹2.30 lakh earned from office scrap disposal Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 8:47PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, is actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6.0 , along with its…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Special Campaign 6.0: Department of Pharmaceuticals Focuses on E-Waste Management, Cleanliness, and Efficient Space Utilization; 14,700 cleanliness drives conducted, 2,200 sq. ft. of office space freed up, ₹2.30 lakh earned from office scrap disposal
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 8:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, is actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6.0, along with its attached office, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), and its organisations, including the seven National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPERs), the Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), and three Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), namely Bengal Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals Limited (BCPL), Hindustan Antibiotics Limited (HAL), and Karnataka Antibiotics & Pharmaceuticals Limited (KAPL).

Being conducted from October 2 to October 31, 2026, the campaign focuses on promoting cleanliness, scientific management and disposal of e-waste, systematic record management, effective grievance redressal, and optimum utilisation of office space, with the objective of enhancing administrative efficiency and promoting a clean, organised, and productive work environment.

Field Office Outreach and Sustainable Workplace Practices: Promoting Swachhata and environmental awareness forms a core pillar of the campaign. Across field and outstation offices, 14,700 cleanliness drives have been conducted so far against a baseline target of 12,208, reflecting the Department’s continued efforts to improve workplace hygiene and sanitation, strengthen environmental awareness, and foster sustainable workplace practices.

Record Management and Optimum Utilisation of Office Space 

The campaign has strengthened systematic record management and promoted the efficient utilisation of office space. Against a baseline target of 2,716 physical files and 20 e-files, the Department has reviewed 4,283 physical files and 20 e-files, while 489 files have been weeded out and closed. Additionally, 2,200 square feet of office space has been freed up through these efforts, contributing to better space management and the creation of more organised, efficient, and clutter-free workplaces.

Grievance Redressal and Liquidation of Pendency

Administrative efficiency and responsive governance are being strengthened through the timely resolution of pending matters, including MP references (3 against target of 4), parliamentary assurances(1 out of 2), a Cabinet proposal (02 proposals), State reference (57 against 58) and PMO references (02 cases).

Against the target of 72 public grievances and 28 appeals, registered on the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), 132 public grievance cases and 39 appeals have been settled. Against target of 20 items identified for easing of rules/processes, this has been completed for 17 items. These efforts aim to expedite the resolution of pending matters, improve service delivery, and promote greater accountability and efficiency in public administration.

Scientific E-Waste Management and Responsible Disposal

Scientific e-waste management is one of the key focus areas of SCDPM 6. The Department has targeted 1,011 obsolete electronic and electrical items - comprising IT equipment, consumer electronics, appliances, and laboratory tools - for safe disposal through empanelled recyclers under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. The process for disposing of these items is currently underway.

Further, the Department has earned a revenue of ₹2,30,187/- from the disposal of office scrap. Department of Pharmaceuticals remains committed to the objectives of SCDPM 6 and is monitoring targets closely and documenting achievements via the National Special Campaign Portal.
